# Fizlet API v0.27.0

> Fizlet™ (fzlt™) is the bricks for DOM animation and games, by Chris Cooley: a game or an animation boils down to logic and style, from a prompt. Every brick has a gzip budget in CI, there are no runtime dependencies, and the page always comes back.

Every public export of every brick, generated from the published type declarations (dist/*.d.ts) of v0.27.0 by the TypeScript compiler at site build time. Each brick's page on https://fizlet.com/bricks/ shows the same, with live demos.

Fizlet 0.x is a public beta: every brick carries a status flag, and a 0.x minor release may change a BETA brick's API (the CHANGELOG says how). COMPLETE bricks keep theirs.

Status flags:
- COMPLETE: Done, and always getting smaller and faster.
- BETA: Tested and budgeted; not yet carried by a shipped game, or its API is still moving.
- ALPHA: In the package to try; no promise yet.
- ROADMAP: Planned, not shipped: a name, a purpose, a size target.
- DEPRECATED: Still in the package, replaced by something named.

## @fzlt/core

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 3372 B gzip (budget 4096 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/kernel.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core"`

The kernel: one loop, bounded work, and the page always comes back. It is the whole default export: one shared requestAnimationFrame for every engine on the page, a fixed 60 Hz step with a catch-up cap, auto-pause, bounded pools, the event ring, seeded random, settle and an fps cap for page interactions, and the ledger that gives the page back on destroy(). Every brick is its own subpath.

### createEngine (function, COMPLETE)

Make an engine: a fixed-step loop on the page's shared clock, with its own pools, event ring, seeded random and ledger. Add systems with `add()`, then `start()`; `destroy()` (or aborting `o.signal`) stops it and gives the page back.

Signature: `createEngine(o?: EngineOptions): Engine`
- o (optional): `EngineOptions`
- returns: `Engine`

```ts
export declare function createEngine(o?: EngineOptions): {
    signal: AbortSignal;
    events: EventRing;
    ledger: Ledger;
    random: Random;
    root: Element | null;
    /**
     * The current (or last) frame, as a typed-array view (reading a slot never boxes a number):
     * `[0]` seconds this frame advances on the shared clock (0 after a pause or a settle), `[1]` ms
     * the last finished frame's hooks took (read, steps, render). Read-only by convention.
     */
    timing: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Fixed step length in seconds. */
    dt: number;
    readonly time: number;
    /** Fixed steps run so far: an integer, so reading it in a hot path never boxes a number. */
    readonly steps: number;
    readonly phase: number;
    /** Pooled things in use right now, summed over every `engine.pool` (no allocation). */
    readonly live: number;
    readonly running: boolean;
    /** Why it's paused right now (empty when running). */
    readonly paused: string[];
    add<S extends System>(s: S): S;
    /** Safe from inside a hook: the rest of the frame still runs every other system. */
    remove(s: System): void;
    /** A named, bounded pool, listed in stats(). */
    pool<T>(name: string, cap: number, create: () => T): Pool<T>;
    /** Run (again). On a settled engine this is wake() too: the quiet time starts over, so it runs a
     *  full settle window instead of going back to sleep on its first frame. Inert once destroyed. */
    start(): void;
    /**
     * Something moved this frame: keeps a settling engine awake (no-op without `settle`). With
     * `sec`, something is scheduled that far ahead (an intro delay, a pause between beats): the
     * engine stays awake for `sec` of its own time (steps, so a slow frame can't outrun it), and
     * settle counts from then. A later, shorter hold never cuts a longer one; 0 or NaN is busy().
     */
    busy(sec?: number): void;
    /** Wake a settled engine (input does this for you); the quiet time starts again. */
    wake(): void;
    stop(): void;
    /** Called by the scheduler with the rAF timestamp. */
    frame(now: number): void;
    /** Run one frame's worth of time by hand (tests, headless, a server). A hook's error throws here.
     *  `sec` must be a finite number (0 or less runs a frame with no steps); anything else throws a
     *  RangeError before the frame starts, instead of stalling the clock for good (S6 P2-04). */
    advance(sec: number): void;
    stats(): EngineStats;
    /** Stop for good: every listener and observer goes (one signal), the page is restored.
     *  Idempotent; afterwards the engine is inert (start, add and advance do nothing). */
    destroy(): void;
};
```

### scheduler (const, COMPLETE)

Scheduler facts for tests and the debug HUD.

Type: `{ readonly engines: number; readonly requests: number; }`

```ts
export declare const scheduler: {
    readonly engines: number;
    readonly requests: number;
};
```

### IDLE, READ, STEP, RENDER (const, COMPLETE)

Frame phases. Read geometry only in READ, never in STEP; write the DOM only in RENDER.

```ts
export declare const IDLE = 0, READ = 1, STEP = 2, RENDER = 3;
```

### Engine (type, COMPLETE)

The engine `createEngine()` returns: what every system and brick takes.

```ts
export type Engine = ReturnType<typeof createEngine>;
```

### EngineOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `createEngine()`. Every field is optional.

```ts
export interface EngineOptions {
    /** The element the engine lives in; it pauses while this is off screen. */
    root?: Element | null;
    /** Fixed step in seconds (default 1/60). */
    step?: number;
    /** Most steps per frame before dropping time instead of spiralling (default 4). */
    maxSteps?: number;
    /** Seed for `engine.random` (default 1). */
    seed?: number;
    /** Event ring capacity per frame (default 64). */
    events?: number;
    /** Aborting this destroys the engine (Recall included). */
    signal?: AbortSignal;
    /** A hook threw during a scheduled frame. The engine is already stopped (`start()` resumes it);
     *  other engines and the shared clock keep running. Default: `console.error(error)`. */
    onError?: (error: unknown, engine: Engine) => void;
    /** Settle (page interactions): after this many seconds in which no system called `busy()`, the
     *  engine sleeps (paused: "settled", no frames at all) until `wake()`, input or `start()`. Off by default.
     *  Counted in engine time (steps). Something scheduled for later (an intro delay, a beat, an
     *  autoplay timer) holds it awake with `busy(sec)`. */
    settle?: number;
    /** Frame-rate cap (e.g. 30 for an ambient hero): between frames the engine is off the shared clock
     *  and a timer brings it back, so it asks for ~fps requestAnimationFrame calls a second. */
    fps?: number;
    /** Auto-pause rules (all on by default; reducedMotion is opt-in: most games calm their effects). */
    pause?: {
        hidden?: boolean;
        offscreen?: boolean;
        editable?: boolean;
        reducedMotion?: boolean;
    };
}
```

### EngineStats (interface, COMPLETE)

What `engine.stats()` reports: frame and step counts, frame time, the event ring and pool fill, the ledger's size and the auto-pause rules holding the engine right now.

```ts
export interface EngineStats {
    frames: number;
    steps: number;
    dropped: number;
    time: number;
    frameMs: {
        avg: number;
        max: number;
    };
    events: {
        size: number;
        cap: number;
        dropped: number;
    };
    pools: Record<string, {
        used: number;
        cap: number;
    }>;
    ledger: number;
    paused: string[];
}
```

### System (interface, COMPLETE)

A system: game logic or a harness. Every hook is optional; systems run in the order added.

```ts
export interface System {
    /** Once per frame, before the steps: read cached geometry, sample input. */
    read?(e: Engine): void;
    /** Fixed step (dt = engine.dt): the simulation. No DOM reads or writes, no allocation. */
    step?(e: Engine, dt: number): void;
    /** Once per frame, after the steps: write the DOM (change-only), play sounds from the ring. */
    render?(e: Engine, alpha: number): void;
    /** When a running engine pauses (stop() or an auto-pause rule): drop held input, stop sounds. */
    pause?(e: Engine): void;
}
```

### Ledger (class, COMPLETE)

Records every change the engine makes to the page (styles, attributes, classes, text, added nodes) so `restore()` puts it back exactly. Writes that change nothing touch nothing, and an edit the host page made after ours always wins. Each engine has one: `engine.ledger`.

Signature: `new Ledger(): Ledger`
- returns: `Ledger`

```ts
export declare class Ledger {
    /** Replace a text node's value. False if the host changed it since our last write. */
    text(node: CharacterData, value: string): boolean;
    /** Set one inline style property (e.g. "transform", "--hp"). */
    style(el: El, prop: string, value: string, priority?: string): boolean;
    /** Put one style property back now (as Recall would) and forget it: a later `style` records the
     *  value then in place as the new original. Hands off if the host changed it since our last write. */
    unstyle(el: El, prop: string): boolean;
    /** Set (string) or remove (null) an attribute. */
    attr(el: El, name: string, value: string | null): boolean;
    /** Add or remove one class. */
    cls(el: El, name: string, on: boolean): boolean;
    /** A node the engine put on the page (canvas, overlay, debris): removed on restore. Once closed
     *  (after engine.destroy()) it is removed as soon as the caller's task ends: the caller inserts it
     *  after this returns, so it can't be refused here. */
    add<N extends Node>(node: N): N;
    /** Recall: put back everything we still own, newest first. Host edits win. With `close` (what
     *  `engine.destroy()` passes) every later text, style, attr or cls write is refused (returns false,
     *  touches nothing), so nothing written after Recall outlives it; without it the ledger is reused. */
    restore(close?: boolean): void;
    /** How many things the ledger holds (for stats). */
    get size(): number;
}
```

### Pool (class, COMPLETE)

A bounded pool. Every item is made up front, so acquiring and releasing never allocates and the pool never grows: when it's full, `acquire()` returns undefined (refuse new work).

Signature: `new Pool<T>(cap: number, create: () => T): Pool<T>`
- cap: `number`
- create: `() => T`
- returns: `Pool<T>`

```ts
export declare class Pool<T> {
    readonly cap: number;
    readonly items: T[];
    constructor(cap: number, create: () => T);
    get size(): number;
    acquire(): T | undefined;
    /** Swap-remove by index (order is not kept). Iterate backwards when releasing in a loop. */
    releaseAt(i: number): boolean;
    release(item: T): boolean;
    clear(): void;
}
```

### EventRing (class, COMPLETE)

Fixed-capacity event ring, filled during a frame's steps and read in render (sound adapter, effects, HUD). Harnesses talk through it instead of callbacks. Full = the event is dropped.

Signature: `new EventRing(cap?: number): EventRing`
- cap (optional): `number`
- returns: `EventRing`

```ts
export declare class EventRing {
    readonly cap: number;
    size: number;
    dropped: number;
    constructor(cap?: number);
    emit(type: string, a?: number, b?: number, x?: number, y?: number, v?: number): boolean;
    at(i: number): FizEvent | undefined;
    clear(): void;
}
```

### FizEvent (interface, COMPLETE)

One event in the ring. Slots are reused; copy what you need before the next frame.

```ts
export interface FizEvent {
    type: string;
    a: number;
    b: number;
    x: number;
    y: number;
    v: number;
}
```

### seeded (function, COMPLETE)

A seeded random number generator: `r()` returns [0, 1). The same seed gives the same sequence; read or set `r.state` to snapshot and restore it.

Signature: `seeded(seed?: number): Random`
- seed (optional): `number`
- returns: `Random`

```ts
export declare function seeded(seed?: number): Random;
```

### Random (interface, COMPLETE)

Seeded random (the DOM VIRUS core LCG, same sequence). Use it for anything that changes the simulation, so a run can be replayed or synced; `state` reads and restores it for snapshots. The state lives in a Uint32Array so drawing a number never allocates.

```ts
export interface Random {
    (): number;
    state: number;
}
```

## @fzlt/core/input

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1909 B gzip (budget 1920 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/input.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/input"`

One controller for keys, pointer and a touch stick, mapped to named intents. Listeners only record; the engine's read phase latches edges and measures the target, so a step sees a stable snapshot. Keys typed into the host page's fields (or inside [data-fizlet-ignore]) never count. Keys, the pointer, `press()` and `steer()` wake a settled engine. Held state is dropped on window blur, when the engine pauses, on dispose() and on destroy: nothing stays stuck. `hit` (an intent or the pointer): a press is seen by exactly one fixed step, the first step after it, even when that comes frames later (0-step frames while catching up) and never again in the same frame's later steps. Outside a step (read, render), `hit` is true for the one frame whose read latched it. Presses between two steps count once.

### ControlsOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `controls()`: the intents and their keys, the pointer target and the touch stick.

```ts
export interface ControlsOptions {
    /** intent → key codes, e.g. { fire: ["Space"], up: ["KeyW", "ArrowUp"] } (KeyboardEvent.code). */
    keys?: Record<string, string[]>;
    /** Where the pointer is measured and the stick lives (default: the engine root, else window). */
    target?: HTMLElement;
    /** Touch: a drag that starts on the left half (or anywhere: "any") drives a virtual stick. */
    stick?: "left" | "any" | false;
    /** Stick radius in CSS px (default 60). */
    radius?: number;
}
```

### Intent (type, COMPLETE)

An intent by name, or by the number `id(name)` gave.

```ts
export type Intent = string | number;
```

### controls (function, COMPLETE)

One controller for keys, pointer and a touch stick on engine `e`, mapped to named intents: `down(intent)`, `hit(intent)` (one step per press), `pointer` and `stick`. It registers its own read-phase system; `dispose()` removes it.

Signature: `controls(e: Engine, o?: ControlsOptions): Controls`
- e: `Engine`
- o (optional): `ControlsOptions`
- returns: `Controls`

```ts
export declare function controls(e: Engine, o?: ControlsOptions): {
    /** An intent's number, for a hot path: `const FIRE = c.id("fire")`, then `c.hit(FIRE)` in a step.
     *  A name that is not an intent throws here, at setup (a typo is never a silent `false`). */
    id(intent: string): number;
    /** Held right now (any of its keys, or press()). */
    down: (intent: Intent) => boolean;
    /** Pressed: true in the first step after the press; outside steps, for the frame it latched. */
    hit: (intent: Intent) => boolean;
    /** -1..1 from two intents (keys), plus the stick when it's active. */
    axis(neg: Intent, pos: Intent, stickAxis?: 0 | 1): number;
    pointer: {
        readonly x: number;
        readonly y: number;
        readonly down: boolean;
        readonly hit: boolean;
    };
    stick: {
        readonly x: number;
        readonly y: number;
        readonly active: boolean;
    };
    /** Press an intent from code (on-screen keys): `press("strike")`. */
    press(intent: string, down?: boolean): void;
    /** Drive the stick from code (an on-screen stick, @fzlt/core/pad): x, y in -1..1; `on = false` lets go. */
    steer(x: number, y: number, on?: boolean): void;
    dispose: () => void;
    system: System;
};
```

### Controls (type, COMPLETE)

The controller `controls()` returns.

```ts
export type Controls = ReturnType<typeof controls>;
```

### GamepadOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `gamepad()`: which buttons press which intents, the dead zone, which pad.

```ts
export interface GamepadOptions {
    /** intent → standard-layout button indices, e.g. { fire: [0], jump: [1, 7] } (0 is A / cross). */
    map?: Record<string, number[]>;
    /** Dead zone, 0..1, for the left stick and analog buttons (default 0.15). */
    dead?: number;
    /** Read only the pad at this `navigator.getGamepads()` index (local multiplayer: a controller per
     *  seat); default: every pad, merged. */
    index?: number;
}
```

### gamepad (function, COMPLETE)

Gamepads into a `controls()` controller: mapped buttons `press` their intents (down from half a pull), the left stick `steer`s the controller's stick, both past the dead zone. It polls in the controller's read phase, before the edges latch, and only while a pad is connected: a page without one never calls `getGamepads()` per frame. Pads have no events for buttons, so a settled engine is not polled: a pad connecting wakes it, and a game that settles between rounds wakes it from its own start key. Zero allocation per read. `stop()` removes it (listeners, polling, held intents and the stick).

Signature: `gamepad(c: Controls, o?: GamepadOptions): { … }`
- c: `Controls`
- o (optional): `GamepadOptions`
- returns: `{ … }`

```ts
export declare function gamepad(c: Controls, o?: GamepadOptions): {
    /** A pad is connected (the one at `index`, when given). */
    readonly connected: boolean;
    /** Pads connected (the one at `index` counts as at most 1). */
    readonly count: number;
    /** An intent's analog value, 0..1 past the dead zone (a trigger's pull), as of the last read. */
    value: (intent: string) => number;
    /** Stop reading pads: listeners off, polling off, its held intents and the stick let go. */
    stop(): void;
};
```

## @fzlt/core/pad

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 2068 B gzip (budget 2120 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/pad.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/pad"`

Swappable on-screen controls for touch (and mouse). One move control (an analog stick, a d-pad or move keys) under one thumb and round arcade action keys under the other, all driving `controls` intents through `press()` / `steer()`: game code reads `down`, `hit` and `axis` and never knows which scheme is on screen. Swap with `setScheme()` at any time. Visuals are the Board UI kit's (`.bui-pad`, `.bui-stick`, `.bui-dpad`, `.bui-arcade` + roles): mount the pad inside a `.bui` root. Listeners are delegated on the pad's one element (bound to the engine's signal), so a scheme swap adds none; the element goes through the ledger.

### Scheme (type, COMPLETE)

The move control on screen: an analog stick, a one-finger d-pad, or a key per move intent.

```ts
export type Scheme = "stick" | "dpad" | "buttons";
```

### PadRole (type, COMPLETE)

A Board UI kit key role: it sets an action key's colour.

```ts
export type PadRole = "fire" | "aim" | "attack" | "advance" | "fallin" | "sys" | "cmd" | "go" | "flag";
```

### PadAction (interface, COMPLETE)

One round action key: the intent it drives, its caption and accessible name, its role colour.

```ts
export interface PadAction {
    /** The `controls` intent this key drives. */
    intent: string;
    /** Short caption on the key (e.g. "FIRE"); empty for icon-only. */
    label: string;
    /** Accessible name (default: label), e.g. "Hold to fire the cannon (Space)". */
    name?: string;
    /** Inline SVG markup (trusted game code). */
    icon?: string;
    /** Shortcut chip for fine pointers, e.g. "SPACE". */
    key?: string;
    /** Kit role colour (default: "fire" for the first action, "sys" for the rest). */
    role?: PadRole;
    /** Held while the finger is down (default: a tap = one press, one `hit`). */
    hold?: boolean;
    /** Each tap flips the intent: `down(intent)` is the switch; `press(intent, on)` from code flips the key too. */
    toggle?: boolean;
}
```

### PadOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `pad()`: the move scheme, the action keys, which thumb gets them and where the pad goes.

```ts
export interface PadOptions {
    /** "stick" (analog, drives the stick axes), "dpad" (one finger, 8-way) or "buttons" (a key per move intent). */
    scheme?: Scheme;
    /** Action keys; the first is the big primary key. */
    actions?: PadAction[];
    /** Which thumb gets the action keys (default "right"); the move control takes the other. */
    side?: "left" | "right";
    /** Where the pad goes (default: the engine root). Must be inside a `.bui` root for the kit look. */
    host?: HTMLElement;
    /** Move intents [up, down, left, right] for the d-pad and move keys; "" leaves one out. */
    move?: string[];
}
```

### stickAt (function, COMPLETE)

Stick vector from a drag offset in radii: clamped to the unit circle, dead zone rescaled so a light push still creeps (Battlefield's feel). Writes out[0], out[1]; never allocates (the exact `hypot` from

@fzlt /core/steer: `Math.hypot` boxes its arguments, K5).

Signature: `stickAt(dx: number, dy: number, out: Float64Array): void`
- dx: `number`
- dy: `number`
- out: `Float64Array`
- returns: `void`

```ts
export declare function stickAt(dx: number, dy: number, out: Float64Array): void;
```

### dpadAt (function, COMPLETE)

D-pad direction mask (up 1, down 2, left 4, right 8; diagonals combine) from a drag offset in radii.

Signature: `dpadAt(dx: number, dy: number): number`
- dx: `number`
- dy: `number`
- returns: `number`

```ts
export declare function dpadAt(dx: number, dy: number): number;
```

### pad (function, COMPLETE)

On-screen controls for touch (and mouse) that drive the intents of `c` (a `controls()` controller): a move control and action keys, in the Board UI kit's look. Swap the move control with `setScheme()`; `destroy()` (or the engine's) removes the pad.

Signature: `pad(e: Engine, c: Controls, o?: PadOptions): Pad`
- e: `Engine`
- c: `Controls`
- o (optional): `PadOptions`
- returns: `Pad`

```ts
export declare function pad(e: Engine, c: Controls, o?: PadOptions): {
    /** The pad's root element (`.bui-pad`). */
    el: HTMLDivElement;
    readonly scheme: Scheme;
    setScheme: (s: Scheme) => void;
    /** Let go of every finger, remove the listeners and the pad (engine.destroy() does this too). */
    destroy(): void;
};
```

### Pad (type, COMPLETE)

The pad `pad()` returns.

```ts
export type Pad = ReturnType<typeof pad>;
```

## @fzlt/core/collide

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1265 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/collide.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/collide"`

A fixed-capacity spatial hash (no allocation per insert or query) and the shape tests games need: circle–circle, circle–rect, swept segment–circle.

### Grid (class, COMPLETE)

Spatial hash over a w×h world. Insert ids each step (after clear), then query a circle. Three separate capacities, each saturating visibly (counters, never silent): - entities `cap`: ids 0..cap-1; any other id (or a non-finite x, y, r) is refused, `rejected`; - index `nodes` (default cap × 4): one node per cell a body covers; past it, `dropped`; - query results: the caller's `out` buffer; ids that don't fit set `missed` (this query) and count in `truncated` (queries cut short). Size `out` so `missed` stays 0: collision results must not drop, so a game should treat any of these counters rising as a bug.

Signature: `new Grid(cell: number, cap: number, w: number, h: number, nodes?: number): Grid`
- cell: `number`
- cap: `number`
- w: `number`
- h: `number`
- nodes (optional): `number`
- returns: `Grid`

```ts
export declare class Grid {
    cell: number;
    cols: number;
    rows: number;
    /** Entity capacity: valid ids are 0..cap-1. */
    readonly cap: number;
    /** Index capacity: cell entries per step (a body covering 4 cells takes 4). */
    readonly nodes: number;
    /** Index entries refused because the node store was full (raise `nodes`). Cumulative. */
    dropped: number;
    /** Inserts and queries refused: id outside 0..cap-1, or a non-finite (or negative r) circle. Cumulative. */
    rejected: number;
    /** Queries whose result did not fit in `out`. Cumulative. */
    truncated: number;
    /** Ids the last query found but could not write to `out` (0 = complete). */
    missed: number;
    constructor(cell: number, cap: number, w: number, h: number, nodes?: number);
    /** World size changed (resize is not a hot path). */
    resize(w: number, h: number): void;
    clear(): void;
    /** The circle being inserted or queried. The work below takes only integers, so a call that
     *  V8 doesn't inline never boxes a number (numbers stay in this typed array). */
    /** Add id (0..cap-1) covering the circle (x, y, r). */
    insert(id: number, x: number, y: number, r: number): void;
    /**
     * Hot-path forms: read body i's x, y, r from typed arrays (arrays and integers never box, even
     * when a big step function stops V8 inlining these calls). `pad` widens the search radius.
     */
    add(x: Nums, y: Nums, r: Nums, i: number): void;
    near(x: Nums, y: Nums, r: Nums, i: number, out: Int32Array, pad?: number): number;
    /**
     * Ids whose cells touch the circle, each once, into `out`. Returns the count written. If more
     * were found than `out` holds, `missed` says how many (and `truncated` counts the query).
     */
    query(x: number, y: number, r: number, out: Int32Array): number;
}
```

### circles (const, COMPLETE)

```ts
export declare const circles: (ax: number, ay: number, ar: number, bx: number, by: number, br: number) => boolean;
```

### overlap (function, COMPLETE)

Bodies i and j overlap, reading x, y, r from typed arrays. Prefer this in big step functions: it passes arrays and integers, so V8 never boxes numbers even when the call isn't inlined (number arguments to a non-inlined function allocate).

Signature: `overlap(x: Nums, y: Nums, r: Nums, i: number, j: number): boolean`
- x: `Nums`
- y: `Nums`

## @fzlt/core/grid

Status: BETA. Size: 1652 B gzip (budget 1664 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/grid.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/grid"`

The game board. A cols × rows tile grid in typed arrays (terrain id, move cost, flags), A* paths, line of sight, movement range and seeded terrain. Every search reuses buffers made once by `board()`, so no call allocates. Cell ids are `row * cols + col`. Not collision: @fzlt/core/collide's `Grid` re-buckets moving bodies every step; a `Board` holds the ground they move over. Use the same cell size for both and a body's collide bucket is its cell. The size is checked at setup: `cols` and `rows` are positive integers, `cell` a finite number > 0 (a RangeError names all three). A search (`path`, `flood`, `los`, `hit`) checks its cell ids: an id that is not an integer on the board throws `fizlet/grid: cell … is not on the board`.

### BLOCKED, COVER, OCCUPIED (const, BETA)

Flags: BLOCKED stops movement and sight, COVER stops sight (pass it in a mask), OCCUPIED marks a unit standing there (paths avoid it unless it is the goal). Bits 8–128 are yours.

```ts
export declare const BLOCKED = 1, COVER = 2, OCCUPIED = 4;
```

### BoardOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `board()`: the cell size in world units and whether moves go 8-way.

```ts
export interface BoardOptions {
    /** World units per cell (default 1: world = grid units). */
    cell?: number;
    /** 8-way moves (never cutting a blocked corner). Default false: 4-way. */
    diagonal?: boolean;
}
```

### Board (class, BETA)

The board `board()` makes: typed-array terrain, cost and flags per cell, plus the searches (A* paths, line of sight, movement range) on buffers made once. Make one with `board()`.

Signature: `new Board(cols: number, rows: number, opts?: BoardOptions): Board`
- cols: `number`
- rows: `number`
- opts (optional): `BoardOptions`
- returns: `Board`

```ts
export declare class Board {
    readonly cols: number;
    readonly rows: number;
    readonly cell: number;
    diagonal: boolean;
    /** Per cell: your terrain id (0 = open ground), move cost to enter (1–255, default 1), flags.
     *  Plain typed arrays: write them directly (`flags[i] |= OCCUPIED`, `flags.fill(0)` to reset). */
    readonly terrain: Uint8Array;
    readonly cost: Uint8Array;
    readonly flags: Uint8Array;
    /** Cells the last search expanded; `partial` is true when the last path ran out of budget. */
    expanded: number;
    partial: boolean;
    constructor(cols: number, rows: number, opts?: BoardOptions);
    /** The cell under a world point, clamped to the board (so always a valid id). */
    at(x: number, y: number): number;
    /** Hot-path form: the cell under body i, reading typed arrays (nothing boxes). */
    cellOf(x: Float64Array | Float32Array, y: Float64Array | Float32Array, i: number): number;
    /** World centre of cell i into out[k], out[k + 1]. */
    center(i: number, out: Float64Array | Float32Array, k?: number): void;
    set(i: number, terrain: number, cost?: number, flags?: number): void;
    /**
     * Seeded terrain: inside the rect (c0, r0)–(c1, r1) (default the whole board), each open cell
     * (terrain 0, no flags) becomes `terrain` with chance `density`. One draw per cell in the rect,
     * whatever is there, so the same seed always lays the same board. Returns cells placed.
     */
    scatter(rand: () => number, density: number, terrain: number, cost?: number, flags?: number, c0?: number, r0?: number, c1?: number, r1?: number): number;
    /** A random cell with none of `mask`, or -1 after `tries` misses (spawns, pickups, crates). */
    pick(rand: () => number, mask?: number, tries?: number): number;
    /**
     * A* from `from` to `to` into `out`: the cells to step through, start excluded, goal last.
     * Returns the step count (0 when from === to, -1 for no path); if it is over out.length only the
     * first out.length steps are written. `budget` caps the cells expanded (0 = no cap) so a frame
     * never stalls: on a cap it writes the path to the closest cell found and sets `partial`.
     * Cells with any `avoid` flag are walls, except that the goal may be OCCUPIED.
     */
    path(from: number, to: number, out: Int32Array, budget?: number, avoid?: number): number;
    /**
     * Movement range: every cell reachable from `from` for at most `max` cost (an orthogonal step
     * into a cost-1 cell costs 1, a diagonal 1.4), nearest first, start included. Returns the count
     * (capped at out.length). `dist(i)` then reads each cell's cost.
     */
    flood(from: number, max: number, out: Int32Array, avoid?: number): number;
    /** Cost from the last search's start to cell i (exact after flood), or -1 if it was not reached. */
    dist(i: number): number;
    /** Line of sight between two cells: no cell strictly between them has a `mask` flag.
     *  Symmetric (a sees b exactly when b sees a). Pass BLOCKED | COVER to let cover block it. */
    los(a: number, b: number, mask?: number): boolean;
    /** The first cell strictly between a and b (walking from a) with a `mask` flag, or -1 if clear.
     *  Bresenham over cells: what a shot hits on its way. */
    hit(a: number, b: number, mask?: number): number;
}
```

### board (const, BETA)

A cols × rows board; every buffer a search needs is made here, once.

Signature: `board(cols: number, rows: number, opts?: BoardOptions): Board`
- cols: `number`
- rows: `number`
- opts (optional): `BoardOptions`
- returns: `Board`

```ts
export declare const board: (cols: number, rows: number, opts?: BoardOptions) => Board;
```

## @fzlt/core/fx

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 2792 B gzip (budget 3072 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/fx.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/fx"`

Explosions that land. One fixed pool of particles (struct-of-arrays, no allocation), drawn on a canvas: square debris, flashes, shock rings, spinning square rings, smoke, scorch marks and pop words, plus screen shake. `blast()` is the DOM VIRUS / Battlefield hero recipe. Gravity (`gravity`, px/s²) pulls each kind by its own share. Particle kinds are data (shape, drag, gravity, how they leave an emitter): `emitter(fx, KINDS)` registers the built-in bubble, spark, drip and debris (or your own) and sprays them; a page that never calls it never ships it. Visual only: its own random (seeded from Math.random), never the simulation's seeded random.

### SHAPES (const, COMPLETE)

Shapes a kind can draw as (a streak trails its velocity: sparks, drips).

Type: `readonly ["square", "disc", "ring", "frame", "word", "smoke", "streak"]`

```ts
export declare const SHAPES: readonly ["square", "disc", "ring", "frame", "word", "smoke", "streak"];
```

### Kind (interface, COMPLETE)

A particle kind, as data. Ranges are [min, max]; speed and size scale with emit's `scale`.

```ts
export interface Kind {
    shape: (typeof SHAPES)[number];
    /** Velocity lost per second, as a fraction (1.4 is the blast's smoke and flashes). */
    drag: number;
    /** Share of the pool's gravity (0: none; negative floats up, like a bubble). */
    gravity: number;
    /** Emit direction in radians (-π/2 is up) and the spread around it (2π: all round). */
    angle: number;
    spread: number;
    speed: readonly [number, number];
    size: readonly [number, number];
    life: readonly [number, number];
}
```

### BUBBLE (const, COMPLETE)

Built-in particle kind: small squares that drift up and fade.

Type: `Kind`

```ts
export declare const BUBBLE: Kind;
```

### SPARK (const, COMPLETE)

Built-in particle kind: fast streaks thrown in every direction, falling a little.

Type: `Kind`

```ts
export declare const SPARK: Kind;
```

### DRIP (const, COMPLETE)

Built-in particle kind: streaks that fall straight down.

Type: `Kind`

```ts
export declare const DRIP: Kind;
```

### DEBRIS_KIND (const, COMPLETE)

Built-in particle kind: square debris thrown in every direction, falling under full gravity.

Type: `Kind`

```ts
export declare const DEBRIS_KIND: Kind;
```

### KINDS (const, COMPLETE)

All four by name: `emitter(fx, KINDS)`, or pick some (`emitter(fx, { bubble: BUBBLE })`).

Type: `{ bubble: Kind; spark: Kind; drip: Kind; debris: Kind; }`

```ts
export declare const KINDS: {
    bubble: Kind;
    spark: Kind;
    drip: Kind;
    debris: Kind;
};
```

### FxOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `effects()`: the particle cap, the colour and word tables, scorch marks and gravity.

```ts
export interface FxOptions {
    /** Max live particles (default 420). New ones are refused (and counted in `dropped`) when full. */
    cap?: number;
    /** Colour table, at most 256; particles store an index (default: the Battlefield blast palette). */
    colors?: string[];
    /** Word table for pop words (index into it), at most 256. */
    words?: string[];
    /** Max scorch marks kept on the ground (default 36; 0 turns them off). */
    scorch?: number;
    /** Gravity in px/s² down (default 0); each kind takes its own share of it. */
    gravity?: number;
}
```

### effects (function, COMPLETE)

Overload policy: particles are decorative, so a full pool refuses new ones and counts them in `dropped`; a blast stops its per-particle work as soon as the pool is full. Invalid input (non-finite numbers, a life that would never end) is refused and counted the same way.

Signature: `effects(o?: FxOptions): Effects`
- o (optional): `FxOptions`
- returns: `Effects`

```ts
export declare function effects(o?: FxOptions): {
    colors: string[];
    words: string[];
    spawn: (k: number, x: number, y: number, vx: number, vy: number, size: number, life: number, c: number, rot?: number, spin?: number, w?: number) => boolean;
    readonly live: number;
    readonly shake: number;
    /** Particles refused so far: pool full, or invalid input. Decorative, so they may drop; counted. */
    readonly dropped: number;
    /** Set gravity in px/s² down (each kind takes its own share; read it back from your own state). */
    gravity: number;
    /** The pool itself, for emitter() and other helpers in this file. Not public API. */
    raw: {
        f: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>[];
        kind: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        col: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        word: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        st: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        K: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        cap: number;
        rnd: (a: number, b: number) => number;
    };
    /** Add screen shake (decays on its own; read `shake` when drawing). */
    kick(amount: number): void;
    /** Pop word (index into `words`), drifting up. */
    word(x: number, y: number, w: number, c: number, size?: number): void;
    /** The hero explosion: flash, fireball, shock ring, spinning square ring, debris, smoke, scorch. */
    blast(x: number, y: number, power?: number, tint?: number): undefined;
    /** Advance every particle (call once per frame or per step). */
    step(dt: number): void;
    /** Scorch marks under everything; call before drawing the actors. */
    drawGround(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, light?: boolean): void;
    /** Every live particle, on top of the actors. */
    draw(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, light?: boolean): void;
    clear(): void;
};
```

### Effects (type, COMPLETE)

The particle pool `effects()` returns.

```ts
export type Effects = ReturnType<typeof effects>;
```

### emitter (function, COMPLETE)

Named particle kinds on a pool: `const { ids, emit } = emitter(fx, KINDS)`, then `emit(ids.bubble, x, y, 12)`. Its own export, so a page that never sprays kinds never ships it. At most 26 kinds per pool (ids 6-31); a second emitter on the same pool adds after the first.

Signature: `emitter<N extends string>(fx: Effects, kinds: Record<N, Kind>): { … }`
- fx: `Effects`
- kinds: `Record<N, Kind>`
- returns: `{ … }`

```ts
export declare function emitter<N extends string>(fx: Effects, kinds: Record<N, Kind>): {
    ids: Record<N, number>;
    /**
     * `n` particles of kind `k` from (x, y), as that kind's data says: direction, spread, speed, size
     * and life (speed and size times `scale`). Colours are picked from `c`...`c + cn - 1`, and a word
     * kind's words from `w`...`w + wn - 1` (indexes into the pool's `words`). Bounded: it stops at
     * capacity and counts the rest in `dropped`. Writes the arrays directly: nothing boxes.
     */
    emit(k: number, x: number, y: number, n: number, c?: number, cn?: number, scale?: number, w?: number, wn?: number): undefined;
};
```

## @fzlt/core/camera

Status: BETA. Size: 1400 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/camera.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/camera"`

The page is the camera. Pan and zoom a DOM stage (any element) with one `transform` written through the engine's ledger, so Recall gives it back exactly. Moves ease and settle (the engine sleeps when they end); with reduced motion they jump. `contain` (default on) keeps the stage covering its own box, so no edge shows and the page never scrolls sideways. Coordinates: world = the stage's own untransformed CSS px (0,0 is its top-left corner); screen = the same box after the camera (what the visitor sees, in the stage's untransformed layout box).

### CameraOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `camera()`: easing rate, zoom limits, containment and reduced-motion handling.

```ts
export interface CameraOptions {
    /** Easing rate per second (default 7; higher is snappier). A move settles in about 6 / ease s. */
    ease?: number;
    /** Zoom limits (default 1 and 4). */
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
    /** Keep the stage covering its own box and clip its parent (default true). */
    contain?: boolean;
    /** Ease moves (default: yes, unless the visitor prefers reduced motion; then every move jumps). */
    motion?: boolean;
}
```

### camera (function, BETA)

A camera on stage `el`: pan and zoom it with one `transform` written through the engine's ledger (so Recall gives it back). Moves ease and settle; `to()`, `pan()` and `home()` drive it.

Signature: `camera(engine: Engine, el: HTMLElement | SVGElement, o?: CameraOptions): Camera`
- engine: `Engine`
- el: `HTMLElement | SVGElement`
- o (optional): `CameraOptions`
- returns: `Camera`

```ts
export declare function camera(engine: Engine, el: HTMLElement | SVGElement, o?: CameraOptions): {
    /** Show world point (x, y) at screen point (px, py) (default: the same point, a zoom about it). */
    to(x: number, y: number, zoom?: number, px?: number, py?: number): void;
    /** Stage size in px (untransformed), as last measured. */
    readonly width: number;
    readonly height: number;
    /** Drag by a screen delta (px): follows at once, no easing. */
    pan(dx: number, dy: number): void;
    /** Back to the page as it is (zoom 1, no offset), eased. */
    home(): void;
    /** Screen (stage box px) to world, into `out` (no allocation). */
    toWorld<T extends {
        [i: number]: number;
    }>(x: number, y: number, out: T): T;
    readonly zoom: number;
    /** Still easing toward the target. */
    readonly moving: boolean;
    read(): void;
    step(e: Engine, dt: number): void;
    render(): void;
};
```

## @fzlt/core/sprite

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1437 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/sprite.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/sprite"`

The character layer's drawing primitive. Pixel-art sprites written as data (rows of characters + a colour map whose values can be palette roles), baked once per (sprite, frame, scale, palette) into a bounded cache, then blitted with one drawImage. `spriteSVG()` / `spriteURL()` give the same pixels as an SVG for characters that live in the page instead of on a canvas; they stand alone, so a page that only places SVG characters never ships the canvas half.

### Paint (type, COMPLETE)

A colour for a character: a hex, or a role name (`team`, `enemy`, `hazard`…) a palette fills.

```ts
export type Paint = string;
```

### SpriteDef (interface, COMPLETE)

One sprite as data: its frames as rows of characters, the colour or role of each character, its pivot and an optional outline.

```ts
export interface SpriteDef {
    /** Rows of characters, one per pixel (one frame), or a list of those (an animation). */
    frames?: string[] | string[][];
    /** Character → colour or role. Any character not listed is empty (use `.` by convention). */
    colors?: Record<string, Paint>;
    /** Pivot in sprite pixels (default: the centre). Draw places it at (x, y) and rotates about it. */
    ax?: number;
    ay?: number;
    /** A 1px rim around the silhouette (colour or role): readable on light and dark pages. */
    outline?: Paint;
    /** Vector sprite instead of pixels: its size, frame count and a painter, baked like the rest. */
    w?: number;
    h?: number;
    n?: number;
    paint?: (c: CanvasRenderingContext2D, frame: number, color: (p: Paint) => string) => void;
}
```

### SpriteOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `sprites()`: the palettes and the size of the baked-tile cache.

```ts
export interface SpriteOptions {
    /**
     * Palettes: role → hex. Index 0 is the default and fills roles the others leave out. The key `*`
     * paints every pixel one colour (a hit flash). Push more at runtime (max 32); `clear()` after
     * changing one in place.
     */
    palettes?: Record<string, string>[];
    /** Max baked tiles kept (default 256). The oldest is dropped when a new one is baked. */
    cap?: number;
    /** Tile factory (default: OffscreenCanvas, else a detached canvas). */
    canvas?: (w: number, h: number) => OffscreenCanvas | HTMLCanvasElement;
}
```

### spriteSVG (function, COMPLETE)

One sprite as an SVG string (crisp at any size), for characters placed in the page. Frames wrap.

Signature: `spriteSVG(d: SpriteDef, frame?: number, palettes?: Palettes, palette?: number): string`
- d: `SpriteDef`
- frame (optional): `number`
- palettes (optional): `Palettes`
- palette (optional): `number`
- returns: `string`

```ts
export declare function spriteSVG(d: SpriteDef, frame?: number, palettes?: Palettes, palette?: number): string;
```

### spriteURL (const, COMPLETE)

`spriteSVG()` as a data URL, for an `<img src>` or a CSS background.

Signature: `spriteURL(d: SpriteDef, frame?: number, palettes?: Palettes, palette?: number): string`
- d: `SpriteDef`
- frame (optional): `number`
- palettes (optional): `Palettes`
- palette (optional): `number`
- returns: `string`

```ts
export declare const spriteURL: (d: SpriteDef, frame?: number, palettes?: Palettes, palette?: number) => string;
```

### sprites (function, COMPLETE)

Frames ≤ 64, palettes ≤ 32 and baked scales 1–8 per sprite: the cache key is one small integer.

Signature: `sprites<K extends string>(defs: Record<K, SpriteDef>, o?: SpriteOptions): Sprites`
- defs: `Record<K, SpriteDef>`
- o (optional): `SpriteOptions`
- returns: `Sprites`

```ts
export declare function sprites<K extends string>(defs: Record<K, SpriteDef>, o?: SpriteOptions): {
    ids: Record<K, number>;
    /** Width and height of each sprite in sprite pixels (outline not included), by id. */
    w: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    h: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    palettes: Record<string, string>[];
    tile: (id: number | K, frame?: number, scale?: number, palette?: number) => Tile;
    /**
     * Draw sprite `id` (number from `ids`, or its name) with its pivot at (x, y), turned by `angle`
     * radians, `scale` pixels per sprite pixel. Bakes on the first call; after that, no allocation.
     * An id that names no sprite throws a RangeError (as `tile` does).
     */
    draw(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, id: number | K, frame: number, x: number, y: number, angle?: number, scale?: number, palette?: number): void;
    /** Baked tiles kept now. */
    readonly size: number;
    /** Tiles baked so far (cache misses). Flat in a steady scene. */
    readonly baked: number;
    /** Drop every baked tile (after changing a palette in place). */
    clear(): void;
};
```

### Sprites (type, COMPLETE)

The sprite set `sprites()` returns: `draw()` blits a baked frame.

```ts
export type Sprites = ReturnType<typeof sprites>;
```

## @fzlt/core/sound

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1062 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/sound.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/sound"`

The sound adapter. After each frame it reads the engine's event ring and plays the mapped cues, so collisions and game events make sound without knowing about audio. The default voice is a tiny synth (oscillators, no assets); pass `play` to use your own sounds. Silent until the first trusted gesture, while paused, and when switched off.

### Cue (type, COMPLETE)

A built-in sound cue the synth can play.

```ts
export type Cue = "fire" | "hit" | "boom" | "hurt" | "power" | "ready" | "win" | "end" | "click";
```

### CueName (type, COMPLETE)

A cue name: a built-in Cue, or one of your own `notes`.

```ts
export type CueName = Cue | (string & {});
```

### Note (type, COMPLETE)

One synth voice: pitch from → to (Hz) over `sec`, after `delay`, its wave and volume.

```ts
export type Note = [from: number, to: number, sec: number, delay: number, wave: OscillatorType, vol: number];
```

### SoundOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `sound()`: which event types play which cue, on or off, volume, or your own player.

```ts
export interface SoundOptions {
    /** event type → cue, e.g. { shot: "fire", wreck: "boom" }. */
    cues: Record<string, CueName>;
    /** Your own cues for the built-in synth: name → voices (a name here wins over a built-in). */
    notes?: Record<string, Note[]>;
    /** Start switched on (default true). */
    on?: boolean;
    /** Master volume 0..1 (default 0.12). */
    volume?: number;
    /** Your own player instead of the synth. */
    play?: (cue: CueName, intensity: number) => void;
}
```

### sound (function, COMPLETE)

The sound adapter for engine `e`: after each frame it plays the cue mapped to each event in the ring. Silent until the first trusted gesture and while paused; set `on` to mute, `dispose()` to remove it.

## @fzlt/core/embed

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 2040 B gzip (budget 2560 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/embed.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/embed"`

Drop a game onto any page with one small config. palette - hex colours for the Board UI roles (anything else is ignored: no CSS injection) easterEgg - false: open now. true / {...}: stay dormant (tiny listeners only) until a trigger (key sequence, gesture on a selector, click on a selector), then lazy-load the game. toggle - a floating key to reopen / close once unlocked. Escape closes and restores the page. Lifted from Swarm Protocol's loader: keys typed in fields never count, only a position and a timestamp are kept for the sequence (never the typed text), and destroy() removes everything.

### EasterEgg (interface, COMPLETE)

```ts
    sequence?: "konami" | string[] | false;

        on: string;
        type: "hold-tap" | "double-tap" | "long-press";

    click?: string | false;
    scope?: {
        sequence?: Scope;
        gesture?: Scope;
        click?: Scope;
    };
    toggle?: boolean;
```

```ts
    /** With no easter egg: open right away (default) or wait closed behind the toggle key. */
```

### embed (function, COMPLETE)

Drop a game onto the page: `load` is called (and awaited) only when the game opens, at once or when the easter egg fires. Returns the controls: `open()`, `close()`, `unlock()`, `opened`, `unlocked` and `destroy()`.

## @fzlt/core/slot

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1849 B gzip (budget 2048 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/slot.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/slot"`

Mount a Fizlet scene into an Astro page engine slot: the element carrying class="ae-slot" data-slot-target="<page>#<slot>" role="img" aria-label="…". Both shapes the engine has rendered are found: the figure itself (`<figure class="ae-slot">`), or a box inside one (`<figure class="ae-slot-figure"><div class="ae-slot">…</div><figcaption class="ae-slot__fallback">`, where the caption sits outside the role="img" box and stays: it is not over the scene). - Lazy: nothing loads or runs until the slot comes near the viewport, and then only once the main thread is idle (or `idle` ms have passed), so the page's own work goes first. - Safe first tap: a tap on the slot before the scene is up loads it at once and is handed to the scene as plain numbers (`first`), never as a stale PointerEvent whose pointer is gone. - Reduced motion: the slot keeps its placeholder and fallback; the scene never loads. If the setting turns on while a scene runs, the scene goes and the fallback comes back. - Accessible: role="img" + aria-label stay unless the scene says it renders real accessible content (`accessible: true`): then role="img" becomes role="figure" (a <figure>'s own role, so the label stays on a role that takes one) in place, and Recall puts "img" back in the same spot, byte for byte. Until then the stage is aria-hidden. - Contained: the scene gets its own stage inside the slot (contain: strict). Every change the slot makes goes through a Ledger, so destroy() gives the page back exactly. - Off screen, off the page's frame: the stage is content-visibility: auto, so a scene scrolled away is skipped for style, layout, paint and layers. Without it a 3D scene's composited layers stayed in every repaint elsewhere on the page (Chromium layerizes the whole document).

### SlotScene (interface, COMPLETE)

What a slot's mount function returns: the scene, with `destroy()` to remove it.

```ts
export interface SlotScene {
    /** Remove the scene (its engine's destroy() restores what it changed). */
    destroy(): void;
    /** True when the scene renders real accessible content: the slot's role="img" becomes "figure". */
    accessible?: boolean;
}
```

### SlotTap (interface, COMPLETE)

A tap on the slot before the scene was up: where (px from the slot's top left) and when.

```ts
export interface SlotTap {
    x: number;
    y: number;
    /** `performance.now()` when the finger went down. */
    at: number;
}
```

### SlotMount (type, COMPLETE)

Build the scene inside `stage` (sized to the slot). `slot` is the figure, read-only. `first` is the tap that started the load, if one did: act on it as an intent (aim, fire), not as an event.

```ts
export type SlotMount = (stage: HTMLElement, slot: HTMLElement, first: SlotTap | null) => SlotScene;
```

### SlotOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `slot()`: how near the viewport the slot must come before loading, and the idle wait.

```ts
export interface SlotOptions {
    /** How close to the viewport the slot must come before the scene loads (default "200px"). */
    margin?: string;
    /** Longest wait (ms) for an idle main thread once the slot is near (default 1000; 0: no wait). */
    idle?: number;
}
```

### findSlot (const, COMPLETE)

The slot for "<page>#<slot>" (or null): any `.ae-slot` carrying the target, figure or box.

Signature: `findSlot(target: string, doc?: Document): HTMLElement | null`
- target: `string`

- returns: `HTMLElement | null`


### slot (function, COMPLETE)

Mount a scene into an Astro page engine slot (`target`: its `data-slot-target` or the element). `load` runs once the slot nears the viewport and the main thread is idle (or on the first tap); with reduced motion it never loads. Returns `el`, `mounted` and `destroy()`.

Signature: `slot(target: string | HTMLElement, load: () => Promise<SlotMount> | SlotMount, opts?: SlotOptions): { … }`

## @fzlt/core/hud

Status: BETA. Size: 1306 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/hud.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/hud"`

Change-only HUD bindings that never allocate in the steady state. A binding reads a number (or a flag) every render, compares it as a number after rounding to what the readout shows, and formats and writes only when that changed. Feeds and banners react to the event ring (`engine.events`), never to polling. Every write goes through `engine.ledger`, so `destroy()` gives the page back. Render phase only: no layout reads, nothing in the step. No visuals of its own: it binds to the game's markup (Board UI or anything else).

### Fmt (type, BETA)

How a number shows: `int` 12 · `clock` 3:05 (seconds) · `rank` #2 · `pct` 75% (0..1 in), or your own.

```ts
export type Fmt = "int" | "clock" | "rank" | "pct" | ((v: number) => string);
```

### Src (type, BETA)

Where a number comes from: a getter, or a slot in a typed array (`[state, 3]`). A getter V8 doesn't inline boxes a fractional double on every call (16 bytes); a slot never does, so it is the safe choice for running fractions (clock, hp, heat). Whole numbers and booleans never box.

```ts
export type Src = (() => number) | readonly [ArrayLike<number>, number];
```

### hud (function, BETA)

Change-only HUD bindings on `engine`, finding readouts in `root` (default `document`): `num`, `meter`, `flag`, `feed` and `banner`. Values are read every render and written only when what shows changes; every write goes through the ledger.

Signature: `hud(engine: Engine, root?: ParentNode): Hud`
- engine: `Engine`
- root (optional): `ParentNode`
- returns: `Hud`

```ts
export declare function hud(engine: Engine, root?: ParentNode): {
    /** A number readout: written only when its shown value changes. */
    num: (t: Target, get: Src, fmt?: Fmt) => /*elided*/ any;
    /** A bar: `width` in whole percent (0..1 in), `aria-valuenow` on a progressbar, class `low` at or under `low`. */
    meter: (t: Target, get: Src, low?: number) => /*elided*/ any;
    /** A class that follows a condition. */
    flag: (t: Target, cls: string, get: () => boolean) => /*elided*/ any;
    /** A list of the last `rows` events of a type, newest first (`play` runs on the newest row). */
    feed: (list: Target, rows: number, on: string, line: (a: number, b: number) => string, play?: (row: HTMLElement) => void) => /*elided*/ any;
    /** Title and sub from an event; `play` (re)starts the game's own animation. */
    banner: (t: Target, on: string, text: (a: number, b: number) => readonly [string, string?], play?: (el: HTMLElement) => void) => /*elided*/ any;
    /** The render system (already added to the engine; `engine.remove(system)` unbinds everything). */
    system: System;
};
```

### Hud (type, BETA)

The HUD `hud()` returns.

```ts
export type Hud = ReturnType<typeof hud>;
```

## @fzlt/core/match

Status: BETA. Size: 2617 B gzip (budget 2816 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/match.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/match"`

The match flow every game shares, intro → count → play → paused → end, on the Board UI kit's overlay (grey dim, a sticker that slams, at most two sticker keys). One overlay is built once; each phase only flips attributes, styles and text through the ledger, so destroy() gives the page back exactly. Every transition is an event on the ring (`match:play`, …), so the HUD, sound and coach layers react without knowing about this one. Pass `null` as the root to run the phase machine headless (tests, a server).

### Phase (type, BETA)

Where a match is: the intro, the countdown, play, paused or the end.

```ts
export type Sticker = [kicker: string, word: string];
```

```ts
export interface MatchLabels extends Record<MatchKey, string> {
```

### MatchOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `match()`: the countdown, the match length, labels and key icons, the pause keys.

```ts
export interface MatchOptions {
    /** Countdown beats of one second before play (default 3; 0 skips it). */
    count?: number;
    /** Match length in seconds; 0 or left out = no time limit (the clock counts up). */
    seconds?: number;
    labels?: Partial<MatchLabels>;
    /** SVG markup per key (64 × 64), e.g. the game's skull on KEEP FIGHTING. */
    icons?: Partial<Record<MatchKey, string>>;
    /** Pause / resume keys (KeyboardEvent.code; default Escape and P). [] turns them off. */
    keys?: string[];
    /** A new round starts (start, rematch): reset the game. Runs in the click (user activation). */
    begin?(): void;
    /** The match ended. Return a sticker to replace the default words (e.g. ["INSERT COIN", "RED WINS"]). */
    end?(r: MatchResult): Sticker | void;
    /** The clock ran out: did the player win? (default: no) */

        reduced?: boolean;

     *  a step made it in): a host that owns more than the overlay (@fzlt/core/arcade's skirmish preset)
     *  follows the phase here. Not called for the first intro. */
    on?(phase: Phase): void;
    /** Phases that show no overlay (the phase machine and its events still run), e.g. ["paused"]. */
    hide?: Phase[];
}
```

### match (function, BETA)

The shared match flow on engine `e`, intro → count → play → paused → end, on the Board UI overlay in `root`. Every transition is an event on the ring (`match:play`, …). Drive it with `start()`, `pause()`, `finish()`, `restart()`; read `phase` and `clock`.

Signature: `match(e: Engine, root: HTMLElement | null, o?: MatchOptions): Match`

- returns: `Match`

```ts
export declare function match(e: Engine, root: HTMLElement | null, o?: MatchOptions): {
    readonly phase: Phase;
    /** Seconds left (timed match) or played so far (no limit). Counts only in play. */
    readonly clock: number;
    /** The overlay element (null headless): add your own content, style it by `[data-phase]`. */
    el: HTMLElement | null;
    /** PRESS START: from the intro (or the result), begin a round. */
    start(): void;
    /** Pause (true), resume (false) or toggle (no argument). Only during play. */
    pause(on?: boolean): void;
    /** End the match now (a win, a loss, "flag" for surrender). */
```

## @fzlt/core/board-page

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 4104 B gzip (budget 4160 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/board-page.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/board-page"`

The host page as the board. Its text glyphs become terrain and food, its buttons become targets. Geometry is measured only in the read phase, on a budget (Range reads capped per refresh; 12.5 Hz while the page moves, 2 Hz once it is still), kept in typed arrays and indexed with a collide Grid, so `near` / `hit` in a step never read layout or allocate. `consume` writes a literal 0/1 into the page's own Text node through the ledger (no wrappers, no clones); from a step it is queued and written in render. Recall gives every glyph back, and a newer edit by the host page wins. Coordinates are viewport CSS px (getBoundingClientRect). Glyph indices hold for a frame: a rescan (read phase, after the page changed) renumbers them. Targets only (`text: false`) with `still: Infinity`: a scene that reads page elements (headings, buttons) re-measures only when the page moves or changes, so its still frames read nothing.

### BoardPageOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `boardPage()`: which part of the page is the board, which elements are text and targets, and the measuring budget.

```ts
export interface BoardPageOptions {
    /** The part of the page that is the board (default document.body). The board lives in its document
     *  and window (an iframe's page works too). */
    root?: Element;
    /** Text containers (default headings, p, li, blockquote, [data-fizlet-text]); 160 at most. false: no glyphs, targets only. */
    text?: string | false;
    /** Targets (default button, [role=button], a.button, a.btn, [data-fizlet-target]). */
    targets?: string;
    /** More to leave alone, on top of fields, editable, code, live regions, dialogs, [data-fizlet-ignore]. */
    exclude?: string;
    /** Glyphs indexed at most (default 8000). */
    maxGlyphs?: number;
    /** Targets at most (default 32). */
    maxTargets?: number;
    /** Letters only (default false: letters and digits are glyphs). */
    letters?: boolean;
    /** Range reads per refresh at most (default 900); the rest are measured on the next refresh. */
    reads?: number;
    /** Seconds between re-measures while the page is still (default 0.5; Infinity: only after a scroll, resize or change). */
    still?: number;
    /** Hex colour for consumed glyphs (a CSS Custom Highlight, where supported). Off by default. */
    color?: string;
}
```

### BoardTarget (interface, COMPLETE)

One target on the board (a button or link): its element and its viewport rect, measured in read.

```ts
export interface BoardTarget {
    readonly el: Element;
    /** Viewport rect, measured in read; w = h = 0 while hidden or off screen. */
    x: number;
    y: number;
    w: number;
    h: number;
    /** The game's to use: starts at 100 and survives a rescan. */
    hp: number;
}
```

### boardPage (function, COMPLETE)

The host page as the board for engine `e`: its glyphs become terrain and food, its buttons targets. Measured only in the read phase, on a budget; `near()` and `hit()` in a step never read layout or allocate. `consume()` changes a glyph through the ledger.

Signature: `boardPage(e: Engine, o?: BoardPageOptions): BoardPage`
- e: `Engine`
- o (optional): `BoardPageOptions`
- returns: `BoardPage`

```ts
export declare function boardPage(e: Engine, o?: BoardPageOptions): {
    glyphs: {
        /** Glyphs indexed, spent ones included (w = 0 while not on screen). */
        readonly count: number;
        x: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        y: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        w: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        h: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        /** 1 once consumed. */
        spent: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    };
    /** Page targets (rects measured in read). */
    targets: readonly BoardTarget[];
    /** Unspent on-screen glyphs touching the circle, into `out`. Returns how many. */
    near(px: number, py: number, pr: number, out: Int32Array): number;
    /** `near` for hot paths: the circle is p[i], p[i + 1] (centre) and p[i + 2] (radius), so no
     *  number is passed (a number passed to a call V8 doesn't inline boxes: one allocation). */
    nearAt: (p: Float64Array, i: number, out: Int32Array) => number;
    /** First unspent glyph the segment touches (2 px pad), or -1; how far along it (0..1) is `t`. */
    hit(x0: number, y0: number, x1: number, y1: number): number;
    /** `hit` for hot paths: the segment is p[i .. i + 3] (x0, y0, x1, y1); how far along it the
     *  glyph is goes in p[i + 4] (and `t`). No number is passed, so nothing boxes. */
    hitAt(p: Float64Array, i: number): number;
    readonly t: number;
    /** Rescans so far: glyph indices from before a rescan mean nothing after it. */
    readonly scans: number;
    /** Range reads made by the last refresh (never more than `reads`). */
    readonly reads: number;
    /**
     * Consume glyph i: a 0/1 ("binary": the board's random draw; "0" / "1": the game's) or a no-break
     * space ("erase") in the page's own text, through the ledger; from a step it is written in
     * render. False if spent or not ours anymore.
     */
    consume(i: number, as?: "binary" | "erase" | "0" | "1"): boolean;
    /** Glyph i as it was before the game changed it (the letter a bite ate). Not for a step: a string. */
    char: (i: number) => string;
    /** The element that holds glyph i's text (for a game's own read-phase checks, e.g. what covers it). */
    parent: (i: number) => HTMLElement | null;
    /** Rescan and re-measure now; from a step, at the next read. */
    refresh(): void;
    system: System;
};
```

### BoardPage (type, COMPLETE)

The board `boardPage()` returns.

```ts
export type BoardPage = ReturnType<typeof boardPage>;
```

## @fzlt/core/presence

Status: BETA. Size: 2197 B gzip (budget 2240 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/presence.html

In-house / experimental: Used in our games. Not a supported multiplayer service. Build your own room server: https://fizlet.com/guides/build-your-own-room-server/

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/presence"`

Lockstep input exchange for multiplayer, behind a tiny transport adapter. Every peer runs the same fixed-step simulation from the same seed. Each sim frame needs every player's input for that frame; your own input is sent `delay` frames ahead, so on a good link the game never waits. A missing input stalls the sim (never guesses), so peers can't drift apart. Inputs live in fixed rings of typed arrays: a confirmed per-frame input log a rollback layer can replay. State hashes are exchanged every `hashEvery` frames to catch a desync early.

### INPUT, HASH, WELCOME, LEAVE, RESUME, AWAY, START, LOBBY (const, BETA)

Wire kinds. Every message is 12 bytes: kind, slot, players, mode, u32 frame (or seed), u32 value (or token). From the room: WELCOME, LEAVE, RESUME (a seat is back: resend), AWAY (a seat dropped and may come back), LOBBY (before the start: your seat, room size, seated); START goes to the room from the host (the protocol: /guides/build-your-own-room-server/).

```ts
export declare const INPUT = 1, HASH = 2, WELCOME = 3, LEAVE = 4, RESUME = 5, AWAY = 6, START = 7, LOBBY = 8;
```

### Transport (interface, BETA)

Moves 12-byte messages to the room (or the other peers) and back.

```ts
export interface Transport {
    /** Send one message. The buffer is reused: copy it before returning. */
    send(data: Uint8Array): void;
    /** Deliver every incoming message to `fn` (messages that arrived earlier are flushed to it). */
    listen(fn: ((data: Uint8Array) => void) | null): void;
    close(): void;
}
```

### PresenceOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `presence()`: the transport, this peer's seat, the number of players, the input delay and the ring sizes.

```ts
export interface PresenceOptions {
    transport: Transport;
    /** This peer's seat, 0..players-1 (the room says which). */
    slot: number;
    players: number;
    /** Frames of input delay (default 2: 33 ms at 60 Hz). */
    delay?: number;
    /** Input frames kept per player (default 64; at least 2 × delay + 2). */
    cap?: number;
    /** This player's input for the frame being scheduled, as bits (read latched intents here). */
    input(): number;
    /** The simulation for one frame: same inputs + same seed → same state on every peer. */
    step(e: Engine, inputs: Uint32Array, frame: number): void;
    /** A hash of the sim state (see `hash32`); compared across peers to catch a desync. */
    hash?(): number;
    /** Frames between hash checks (default 30). */
    hashEvery?: number;
}
```

### presence (function, BETA)

Lockstep multiplayer on engine `e`: each sim frame waits for every player's input (sent `delay` frames ahead), so peers never drift; state hashes are compared to catch a desync. Read `frame`, `stalls`, `desync` and `lost`; `destroy()` stops it.

Signature: `presence(e: Engine, o: PresenceOptions): Presence`
- e: `Engine`
- o: `PresenceOptions`
- returns: `Presence`

```ts
export declare function presence(e: Engine, o: PresenceOptions): {
    system: System;
    /** Sim frames run so far (every peer passes the same frames, maybe at different times). */
    readonly frame: number;
    /** Engine steps spent waiting for someone's input. */
    readonly stalls: number;
    /** Messages refused (out of the window, bad seat, a second input or hash for one frame). */
    readonly dropped: number;
    /** First frame whose state hash differed from a peer's, or -1. */
    readonly desync: number;
    /** Bitmask of seats the room said left (their frames never arrive: the sim waits). */
    readonly lost: number;
    /** Bitmask of seats reconnecting (dropped, may come back; this one too, while `join`'s link retries). */
    readonly away: number;
    /** The confirmed input of `slot` for `frame`, or -1 if it isn't known (yet, or any more). */
    confirmed(slot: number, frame: number): number;
    destroy: () => void;
};
```

### Presence (type, BETA)

The lockstep session `presence()` returns.

```ts
export type Presence = ReturnType<typeof presence>;
```

### memory (function, BETA)

In-memory hub: `peers` transports that broadcast to each other (like the room relay) after `latency` ± `jitter` ticks. Call `tick()` once per frame. Bounded: `cap` messages in flight.

```ts
export declare function memory(o: {

    jitter?: number;
    seed?: number;
    cap?: number;

    ends: Transport[];

    readonly dropped: number;
```

### websocket (function, BETA)

Wrap an open-or-opening WebSocket as a transport. Messages before `listen` are kept (≤ 256). `send` takes presence's 12-byte messages (the room refuses any other size). `eat` (join's) sees each message first and keeps it from the listener when it returns true.

### JoinOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `join()`.

```ts
export interface JoinOptions {
    /** Reconnect tries after a drop, 250 ms apart and doubling (default 6: about 16 s; 0: off). Meanwhile
     *  `away` has this seat's bit (the others see AWAY); when they run out, `lost` (LEAVE). */
    retry?: number;
    /** Called on each LOBBY from the room before the start (on every join and leave): this player's
     *  `seat`, how many are `seated`, the room `size`. Seat 0 is the host: its `start(seats, mode)` asks
     *  the room to begin once `seats` are taken (0: now) with the seats it has; `mode` (0..255) reaches
     *  every peer. Other seats' starts are ignored by the room. */
    lobby?(start: (seats?: number, mode?: number) => void, seat: number, seated: number, size: number): void;
}
```

### join (function, BETA)

Join a room (a server speaking the `fizlet-rooms` subprotocol): resolves when the room starts with your seat, the player count, the shared seed and the host's `mode`. `protocols` go to the WebSocket handshake: the room reads its access token there (`["fizlet-rooms", "invite." + code]`), so the code stays out of the URL and the logs. A dropped link (1006, or a server restart: 1011, 1012, 1014) reconnects on its own (`o.retry`) with the seat's resume token, kept in memory only (never in a URL); the room's own closes (idle, full, seat gone, the caps) end it.

Signature: `join(url: string, signal?: AbortSignal, protocols?: string | string[], o?: JoinOptions): Promise<{ transport: Transport; slot: number; players: number; seed: number; mode: number; }>`
- url: `string`
- signal (optional): `AbortSignal`
- protocols (optional): `string | string[]`
- o (optional): `JoinOptions`
- returns: `Promise<{ transport: Transport; slot: number; players: number; seed: number; mode: number; }>`

```ts
export declare function join(url: string, signal?: AbortSignal, protocols?: string | string[], o?: JoinOptions): Promise<{
    transport: Transport;
    slot: number;
    players: number;
    seed: number;
    mode: number;
}>;
```

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/presence/check"`

The determinism check as one function any game can call from a test. It runs `players` copies of your sim as lockstep clients over the in-memory link (each with only its own input), hashes the state after every frame, and reports the first frame that differs.

### SyncGame (interface, BETA)

Your sim as `syncCheck()` runs it: its input for the next frame, one step from every player's inputs, and a byte view of its whole state.

```ts
export interface SyncGame {
    /** This player's input bits for the next scheduled frame (only this client knows them). */
    input(): number;
    /** One sim frame from every player's inputs. Use `e.random`, never Math.random or the clock. */
    step(e: Engine, inputs: Uint32Array, frame: number): void;
    /** A byte view of the whole sim state (typed arrays; make the view once). */

}
```

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/presence/rollback"`

Rollback netcode for a deterministic sim, on presence's 12-byte wire and room (nothing in the room server changes). Presence's lockstep waits for every input, so on a phone's network the sim runs only as fast as the slowest round trip; this runs every frame at once instead. Each frame runs with this screen's own input (a small delay, 1 to 3 frames, picked from the measured latency) and a guess for everyone else's (the last input heard from them). When a real input arrives that differs from the guess, the state goes back to that frame (a ring of snapshots of the sim's byte views, made once) and the frames since run again: the sim is deterministic, so every screen ends on the same state. A frame whose inputs are all real is final: `confirm` hears each one, in order, once; state hashes are compared on final frames only (a desync shows; it never drifts). A screen that runs ahead of the others (by the trip each side measures, carried in the INPUT message's spare byte) waits a frame now and then until they meet. At most `window` frames run past the last final one: past it the sim waits (a link that went quiet). A seat the room says left plays `gone` from the frame after its last input, on every screen. No allocation per frame. Wire: INPUT [1, seat, delay, lead × 2 (int8), frame u32, bits u32], HASH [2, seat, 0, 0, frame, hash]. One INPUT per frame, frames rising (the room relays each once; over TCP nothing is lost or reordered, and a resend only follows a RESUME).

### RollbackOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `rollback()`: the link, the seat, the sim (its input, step and bytes) and the window.

```ts
export interface RollbackOptions {
    transport: Transport;
    /** This screen's seat, 0..players-1 (the room says which). */
    slot: number;
    /** Seats in the room, at most 8. */
    players: number;
    /** This screen's input bits for `frame` (called once per frame, in order, `delay` frames ahead). */
    input(frame: number): number;
    /** Run one frame from `inputs[0..players-1]`. `live`: the first time this frame runs (false: again,
     *  after a correction); `sure`: every input is real and every frame before it final (it never runs
     *  again). Return false to wait instead (nothing changed). Only the state in `bytes` may change. */
    step(inputs: Uint32Array, frame: number, live: boolean, sure: boolean): boolean | void;
    /** The sim's whole state (typed-array byte views, the seeded random's state too): saved and restored
     *  byte for byte, and hashed on final frames. */
    bytes: Uint8Array[];
    /** A final frame, in order, once, with its real inputs (a replay log, scores, sounds that must not repeat). */
    confirm?(inputs: Uint32Array, frame: number): void;
    /** Around a correction: before the state goes back (true) and after the frames ran again (false). */
    rewind?(before: boolean): void;
    /** The input bits a seat that left plays from the frame after its last one (default 0). */
    gone?: number;
    /** Frames run past the last final frame, at most, 2..100 (default 64: 1.07 s at 60 Hz). */
    window?: number;
    /** Frames between hash checks (default 30). */
    hashEvery?: number;
    /** A fixed input delay, 1..3 frames; omitted, it adapts 1..3 to the measured latency. */
    delay?: number;
}
```

### rollback (function, BETA)

Rollback multiplayer on engine `e`: runs every frame at once on guessed remote inputs and runs frames again when a real input differs; final frames are hashed and compared. Read `frame`, `final`, `desync`, `delay`; `destroy()` stops it.

Signature: `rollback(e: Engine, o: RollbackOptions): Rollback`
- e: `Engine`
- o: `RollbackOptions`
- returns: `Rollback`

```ts
export declare function rollback(e: Engine, o: RollbackOptions): {
    /** Frames run so far on this screen (some on guesses). */
    readonly frame: number;
    /** Frames final so far (every input real): the same frames on every screen, maybe at different times. */
    readonly final: number;
    /** Engine steps the sim waited: the window was full (someone went quiet) or a step asked to. */
    readonly stalls: number;
    /** Engine steps this screen waited a frame for the others to catch up (time sync). */
    readonly waits: number;
    /** Frames run again after corrections, in all. */
    readonly resims: number;
    /** The deepest correction (frames run again at once). */
    readonly deepest: number;
    /** Corrections so far. */
    readonly corrections: number;
    /** The slowest correction so far (ms, the frames run again). */
    readonly resimMs: number;
    /** All the time spent running frames again (ms). */
    readonly resimTotal: number;
    /** Engine steps so far. */
    readonly steps: number;
    /** The input delay now (frames, 1..3). */
    readonly delay: number;
    /** How far this screen runs ahead of the others (frames, the mean over the seats still playing). */
    readonly lead: number;
    /** The first frame whose state hash differed from a seat's, or −1. */
    readonly desync: number;
    /** Seats the room said left, as bits (this one too when its own link is gone for good). */
    readonly lost: number;
    /** Seats reconnecting, as bits. */
    readonly away: number;
    /** Other seats that left (they play `gone`), as bits. */
    readonly left: number;
    /** The frame seat s's `gone` starts, or −1 (it has not left). */
    leftAt: (s: number) => number;
    /** Messages ignored: late, repeated, out of the ring or of an unknown kind. */
    readonly dropped: number;
    /** Stop running new frames at `frame` (−1: run on); inputs and corrections still land (tests, a
     *  match's end). */
    hold: number;
    /** Stop: the system leaves the engine, the link closes. */
    destroy: () => void;
};
```

### Rollback (type, BETA)

What `rollback()` returns.

```ts
export type Rollback = ReturnType<typeof rollback>;
```
