### mount (function, COMPLETE)

Mount a board inside a shadow root on `host`, isolated both ways: the kit can't touch the page and the page's CSS (a global `button {}` rule, a reset) can't touch the board. Pass the kit CSS text (e.g. `import css from "board-ui/board-ui.css?raw"`). Returns the `.bui` root to build in. Stylesheet ownership: the kit owns one constructed sheet per CSS text (keyed by the text), so games composed independently with different CSS each get their own, and boards with the same text share one. Treat it as read-only; it is appended to the shadow root's adoptedStyleSheets, never replacing sheets you adopted there yourself.

Signature: `mount(host: HTMLElement, css: string, opts?: { theme?: "dark" | "light"; side?: 0 | 1; palette?: Palette; }): HTMLDivElement`

### setting (function, COMPLETE)

A Settings switch: a key that is `aria-pressed` (the kit's locked state) while on, remembered in localStorage under `key` as "1" / "0". Storage that throws (private mode, blocked cookies, a sandboxed frame) is ignored: the switch still works, it just forgets. `change` runs once with the stored value and on every flip; `set(on)` flips it from code (a keyboard shortcut). ## @fzlt/core/perf

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 2019 B gzip (budget 2022 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/perf.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/perf"`

A live performance overlay for players, off until they switch it on. Frames per second, a rolling frame-time bar chart (one bar per frame, coloured against the budget), dropped frames, the engine's work per frame (read, steps, render), live pooled entities and, where the browser exposes it, the JS heap. It reads the engine's own frames on the shared clock (`engine.timing`, `engine.live`): no clock or requestAnimationFrame of its own, and it never calls `engine.busy()`, so a settling engine still settles and the chart rests with it. Its own cost stays out of what it measures: frame times go into a typed-array ring (nothing is allocated per frame), the numbers are written twice a second through the ledger (change-only, strings cached), the chart is one canvas, and the root is `contain: layout paint style` and `pointer-events: none`. Hidden, it only records (a few typed-array writes a frame). Not the dev-only `@fzlt/core/debug`, which patches Element prototypes: this one ships to players.

### Corner (type, COMPLETE)

A corner of the host: top left, top right, bottom left or bottom right.

```ts
export type Corner = "tl" | "tr" | "bl" | "br";
```

### PerfOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `perf()`: where the overlay goes, the toggle key and the frame budget.

```ts
export interface PerfOptions {
    /** Where the overlay goes (default the engine root, else `document.body`, where it is fixed). */
    host?: HTMLElement | null;
    /** Corner of the host (default "tr"). */
    corner?: Corner;
    /** `KeyboardEvent.code` that toggles it (default "F9"); null for none. */
    key?: string | null;
    /** Shown from the start (default false: players switch it on in Settings). */
    on?: boolean;
    /** The frame budget in ms (default 1000 / 60): a frame over 1.5 budgets counts as dropped. */
    budget?: number;
    /** Called when it is shown or hidden (the key or `show()`): keep a Settings switch in step. */
    change?: (on: boolean) => void;
}
```

### perf (function, COMPLETE)

## @fzlt/core/rules

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1318 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/rules.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/rules"`

The rules every arcade game repeats, as three small systems on the kernel: - `waves`: a wave clock, prepare → assault → rebuild, with a spawn budget per wave; - `drops`: pickups that fall, wait to be collected and expire; - `score`: points, a combo that decays, and levels from XP thresholds. Each is DOM-free, steps without allocating (state lives in typed arrays) and says what happened on the event ring (`wave:start`, `wave:clear`, `drop:spawn`, `drop:land`, `drop:collect`, `drop:expire`, `score`, `combo:end`, `level`), so the HUD, sound, fx and coach layers react without reaching into the game. Defaults are the DOM VIRUS core's (WaveDirector, SupplyDrops) and Null Invaders' numbers, so a port keeps its feel. The game still decides where and what to spawn. Call `collect`, `add` and `miss` from a step, like the rest of the game: their events go on that frame's ring.

### WavePhase (type, COMPLETE)

Where the wave clock is: prepare (before a wave), assault (spawning) or rebuild (between waves).

```ts
export type WavePhase = "prepare" | "assault" | "rebuild";
```

### WaveOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `waves()`: how many are alive now, the cap, the phase lengths and each wave's size, limit and spawn gap.

```ts
export interface WaveOptions {
    /** Alive now. A wave clears when it has spawned everything and this reaches 0. */
    alive(): number;
    /** Most alive at once, whatever the wave (default 32). */
    cap?: number;
    /** Seconds before wave 1 (default 4) and between waves (default 8). */
    prepare?: number;
    rebuild?: number;
    /** Enemies in wave n (default min(40, 5 + 5n)). */
    size?(wave: number): number;
    /** Most alive at once in wave n, before `cap` (default 8 + 4n). */
    limit?(wave: number): number;
    /** Seconds between two spawns in wave n (default max(0.7, 2.1 − 0.12n)). */
    gap?(wave: number): number;
}
```

## @fzlt/core/steer

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 2759 B gzip (budget 2816 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/steer.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/steer"`

How things move toward, away from and around a point, as DOM-free steering on typed arrays. Every mover has a position (`x`, `y`), a heading (`a`, radians) that turns at most `turn` rad/s, and moves `speed × scale` px/s along it. Behaviours: - `seek`: drive at a point, stop inside `stop`; - `flee`: drive straight away from a point until `far`; - `arrive`: seek with an arrival band: full pace far off, slower inside `slow`, stop inside `near`; `arriveGoal` is the same toward the goal the game wrote in `gx[i]`, `gy[i]` (a target that moves every frame: no double crosses a call, so nothing is boxed); - `wander`: pick a random goal in `area` every `every + random × jitter` s and seek it; - `patrol`: seek waypoints in turn, looping. Each writes the distance moved this call to `moved[i]` (0 when standing). The heading turn and the per-axis wall check (`blocked`, so a mover slides along walls) are DOM Battlefield Blitz's `drive`, and the defaults are its tank numbers, so a port keeps its feel. Nothing allocates: call them from a step, one mover at a time. Pass `engine.random` as `random` so seeded runs replay: the heading's trig is `@fzlt/core/math`'s, so a replay gives the same bits in every browser (in Node, the builtins' bits: the moves are Blitz's to the bit). Options are checked at setup: a bad number throws a RangeError with its name instead of turning into NaN mid-game.

### SteerOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `steer()`: how many movers, their pace, turn rate and arrival bands, the wander area and timing, the wall check and the random source.

```ts
export interface SteerOptions {
    /** Movers, a positive integer (fixed: the arrays never grow). */
    cap: number;
    /** Pixels per second at full pace (default 150) and a multiplier for the board's scale (default 1). */
    speed?: number;
    scale?: number;
    /** Most the heading turns, radians per second (default 7). */
    turn?: number;
    /** Seek, wander and patrol stop inside this many pixels of the goal (default 16). */
    stop?: number;
    /** Arrive: stop inside `near` (14), slow down inside `slow` (140): pace `fast` (1.05) then `calm` (0.8). */
    near?: number;
    slow?: number;
    fast?: number;
    calm?: number;
    /** Flee stops once this far away (default 240). */
    far?: number;
    /** Wander: a new goal every `every` (2) + random × `jitter` (2) seconds, inside `area` [left, top, width, height]. */
    every?: number;
    jitter?: number;
    area?: readonly [number, number, number, number];
    /** Is (at[0], at[1]) a wall for mover i? Checked per axis, so movers slide along walls. The spot
     *  comes in a typed array, not as two numbers: doubles passed to a callback are boxed. */
    blocked?(i: number, at: Float64Array): boolean;
    /** 0..1 (default Math.random; pass engine.random to replay). */
    random?(): number;
}
```

### turn (const, COMPLETE)

Turn `from` toward `to` by at most `max` radians, the short way round.

Signature: `turn(from: number, to: number, max: number): number`
- from: `number`
- to: `number`
- max: `number`
- returns: `number`

```ts
export declare const turn: (from: number, to: number, max: number) => number;
```

### hypot (const, COMPLETE)

Math.hypot of two numbers, without the builtin call: V8 boxes Math.hypot's arguments, a heap number per call in a hot loop. Same steps as V8's own (Infinity wins over NaN, scale by the larger, sum, sqrt), so it returns the same bits (tested against Math.hypot).

Signature: `hypot(dx: number, dy: number): number`
- dx: `number`
- dy: `number`
- returns: `number`

```ts
export declare const hypot: (dx: number, dy: number) => number;
```

### steer (function, COMPLETE)

Steering for `o.cap` movers on typed arrays: `seek`, `flee`, `arrive`, `wander` and `patrol`, each with a turn-limited heading and a per-axis wall check. DOM-free and allocation-free: call them from a step, one mover at a time.

Signature: `steer(o: SteerOptions): Steer`
- o: `SteerOptions`
- returns: `Steer`

```ts
export declare function steer(o: SteerOptions): {
    x: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    y: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    a: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** The goal: wander's current one (and seconds until it picks the next), or one the game writes for `arriveGoal`. */
    gx: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    gy: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    think: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Patrol: the waypoint each mover is heading for. */
    leg: Uint32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    cap: number;
    /** Put mover i at (px, py) facing `heading`; wander picks a goal at once, patrol starts at 0. */
    place(i: number, px: number, py: number, heading?: number): void;
    /** Pixels each mover went on its last call (0 when it stood). */
    moved: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Drive mover i along (ax, ay) (a stick, length ≤ 1) for dt seconds. */
    drive(i: number, ax: number, ay: number, dt: number): void;
    /** Toward (tx, ty) at `pace` (dt is scaled by it, so the turn slows too), until inside `stop`. */
    seek(i: number, tx: number, ty: number, dt: number, pace?: number): void;
    flee(i: number, fx: number, fy: number, dt: number, pace?: number): undefined;
    arrive(i: number, tx: number, ty: number, dt: number): void;
    /**
     * `arrive` toward (gx[i], gy[i]): write the goal there, then call it. For a goal computed every
     * frame (a slot behind a leader): passed as two numbers, V8 boxes each one whenever it doesn't
     * inline the call (3 young GCs per 20k steps in Blitz's platoons); a typed array never boxes.
     */
    arriveGoal(i: number, dt: number): void;
    wander(i: number, dt: number, pace?: number): void;
    /** Waypoints as [x0, y0, x1, y1, …] (a typed array is best); the next one once inside `stop`.
     *  No waypoint (fewer than two numbers): it stands still. */
    patrol(i: number, points: ArrayLike<number>, dt: number, pace?: number): undefined;
};
```

### Steer (type, COMPLETE)

The movers `steer()` returns.

```ts
export type Steer = ReturnType<typeof steer>;
```

## @fzlt/core/coach

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1220 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/coach.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/coach"`

The hints and tutorial layer the board games share, in three small parts: - `flag`: a once-only switch kept in localStorage ("tips off", "seen the tour"). Every read and write is wrapped in try/catch, so a page with storage blocked (private mode, sandboxed iframe, quota) just reads "not set" and plays on; - `tour`: DOM-free tutorial steps. It counts time on the current step, moves on when the game says the step is done (`coach:step` on the event ring), then cycles tips every `every` seconds. `show()` says which card to draw only when it changed, so the DOM is written once per card; - `card`: the Board UI kit card that shows it (count, title, text, an End button) and rings the control it is about. Its look is DOM Battlefield's coach card, inline on the kit tokens. Defaults are DOM Battlefield Blitz's practice coach (10 steps, then a tip every 6 s), so a port keeps its pace. `tour` steps without allocating; call it from a step like the rest of the game.

## @fzlt/core/timeline

Status: BETA. Size: 2137 B gzip (budget 2304 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/timeline.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/timeline"`

Scripted DOM choreography on the kernel clock. Keyframe tracks animate CSS properties (transform, translate, scale, rotate, opacity, clip-path, filter, custom properties: any value whose numbers change and whose words stay) or plain numbers, with easings, delays, staggers, sequencing and overlap, labels, repeats and yoyo. Time moves in the fixed step (no allocation, no DOM); writes happen in render through the ledger, change-only, so Recall restores every property touched. Done or paused, it asks for no frames: the engine settles. With reduced motion, play() lands on the end state in one step (or build a gentler variant on `tl.reduced`).

### Ease (type, BETA)

An easing: progress 0..1 in, eased progress out (it may overshoot).

```ts
export type Ease = (p: number) => number;
```

### EASES (const, BETA)

The named easings: cubic in, out and in-out; back overshoots a little and settles. Also by name: "steps(n)" (n equal jumps: a ticking counter, a typed-out line).

Type: `Record<string, Ease>`

```ts
export declare const EASES: Record<string, Ease>;
```

### Value (type, BETA)

A number, a CSS value ("translate(0px,8px)", "inset(0 50% 0 0)") or keyframes, evenly spaced. Keyframes share one shape: the same words, only the numbers change. A single value starts where the property's last track ended (or is set at once if it has none).

```ts
export type Value = number | string | readonly (number | string)[];
```

### TrackOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for one track: where it starts (`at`), its duration, delay, easing and stagger.

```ts
export interface TrackOptions {
    /** Seconds (default 0.4). */
    dur?: number;
    /** Seconds after `at`; negative overlaps the track before (default 0). */
    delay?: number;
    /** A name in EASES, "steps(n)" or a function (default "out"). */
    ease?: string | Ease;
    /** Seconds between one target's start and the next. */
    stagger?: number;
    /** Where it starts: seconds, "<" (with the track before) or a label (default: the end so far). */
    at?: number | string;
}
```

### TimelineOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `timeline()`: repeats, yoyo, speed and reduced-motion handling.

```ts
export interface TimelineOptions {
    /** Extra plays after the first (default 0; Infinity loops). */
    repeat?: number;
    /** Every other play runs backwards. */
    yoyo?: boolean;
    /** Speed (default 1). */
    rate?: number;
    /** Animate (default: yes, unless the visitor prefers reduced motion; then play() jumps). */
    motion?: boolean;
    /** `a` on this timeline's events (default 0). */
    id?: number;
}
```

### timeline (function, BETA)

A timeline on `engine` (paused until `play()`). Events on the ring, `a` = id: "timeline:start", "timeline:end", and each label's own name (b = its index) as the playhead passes it.

Signature: `timeline(engine: Engine, o?: TimelineOptions): Timeline`
- engine: `Engine`
- o (optional): `TimelineOptions`
- returns: `Timeline`

```ts
export declare function timeline(engine: Engine, o?: TimelineOptions): {
    /** Add tracks: each property of `values` on each target (an element, a list of them, or any
     *  object or typed array for plain numbers: `tl.to(arr, { 0: [0, 1] })`). Chainable. */
    to(targets: object | ArrayLike<object>, values: Record<string, Value>, t?: TrackOptions): /*elided*/ any;
    /** Name a moment (default: the end so far) for `at`; its name goes on the ring as it passes. */
    label(name: string, t?: number | string): /*elided*/ any;
    /** Play forward (from the start if it is at the end). */
    play: () => /*elided*/ any;
    /** Play backward (from the end if it is at the start). */
    reverse: () => /*elided*/ any;
    /** Stop where it is. The engine calls this as its System pause hook (off screen, hidden tab,
     *  stop()): then it only suspends, and plays on when the engine resumes unless you paused it. */
    pause(by?: unknown): /*elided*/ any;
    /** Move the playhead to `t` seconds; it keeps playing or stays paused. */
    seek(t: number): /*elided*/ any;
    /** Land on the end in the next step ("timeline:end" fires). */
    finish: () => /*elided*/ any;
    /** Pause and give every property back as it was before the timeline wrote it: styles through
     *  the ledger (a newer host edit wins), plain numbers to their value when the track was added. */
    revert(): /*elided*/ any;
    /** Resolves the next time the timeline ends, or when its engine is destroyed (at once if it was). */
    done: () => Promise<void>;
    /** The playhead in seconds (over every play). */
    readonly time: number;
    /** Every play together, in seconds (Infinity when it loops forever). */
    readonly duration: number;
    readonly playing: boolean;
    /** The visitor prefers reduced motion (or `motion: false`): build the gentler variant on it. */
    readonly reduced: boolean;
    step(e: Engine, dt: number): void;
    render(): void;
};
```

### Timeline (type, BETA)

The timeline `timeline()` returns: add tracks with `to()`, then play it.

```ts
export type Timeline = ReturnType<typeof timeline>;
```

## @fzlt/core/touch

Status: BETA. Size: 310 B gzip (budget 512 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/touch.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/touch"`

Taps and swipes on an animation or a game never zoom or pan the page. One delegated listener set on the document (capture, not passive) cancels, on the surfaces that match `sel`, what CSS `touch-action` can't: iOS Safari's `gesturestart` / `gesturechange` (its pinch, which ignores `user-scalable=no`) and any multi-touch `touchstart` / `touchmove` (a pinch anywhere else). One finger is never touched, so taps, drags and the page's own scroll stay. The CSS half lives in the Board UI kit (board-ui.css): `touch-action: manipulation` on the page (no double-tap zoom) and `touch-action: none` / `pan-y` plus `overscroll-behavior: none` on the same surfaces. Pass `null` to lock the whole page (a full-screen board; content pages keep pinch-zoom for WCAG 1.4.4). Returns `release()`: the page gets its gestures back.

### SURFACES (const, BETA)

The surfaces Fizlet draws on: slot stages, game hosts, the touch pad, draggable panels, and anything marked `data-touch-lock`.

Type: `"[data-fizlet-slot],[data-fizlet-host],[data-touch-lock],.bui-pad,.bui-grip"`

```ts
export declare const SURFACES = "[data-fizlet-slot],[data-fizlet-host],[data-touch-lock],.bui-pad,.bui-grip";
```

### lockTouch (function, BETA)

Lock pinch on the surfaces matching `sel` (`null`: the whole page). Returns `release()`.

Signature: `lockTouch(doc?: Document, sel?: string | null): () => void`
- doc (optional): `Document`
- sel (optional): `string | null`
- returns: `() => void`

```ts
export declare function lockTouch(doc?: Document, sel?: string | null): () => void;
```

## @fzlt/core/css-clock

Status: BETA. Size: 5368 B gzip (budget 5566 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/css-clock.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/css-clock"`

A page's own CSS @keyframes, on the kernel clock. The look stays in the stylesheet; Fizlet owns the time. Each animation under `root` is paused and reads its time from one custom property that a timeline moves through the ledger: .led { animation: blink 1s steps(2) infinite paused; animation-delay: var(--fz-t, 0s); } .bug { animation: walk 6s linear infinite paused; animation-delay: calc(var(--fz-t, 0s) - 3s); } - One shared requestAnimationFrame with every other engine on the page; off screen or in a hidden tab it asks for no frames at all. - Settles: after `loops` plays of `span` seconds it rests where it started (every animation whose duration divides `span` is back on its first frame) and the engine sleeps. A pointer over the root, focus inside it or coming back into view plays it again. - Reduced motion: play() lands on the rest frame at once (the still poster). - Recall: destroy() (or aborting `signal`) gives the root's style back as it was.

### CssClockOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `cssClock()`: the loop length, how many plays before it rests, the custom property, the frame cap, reduced motion and an abort signal.

```ts
export interface CssClockOptions {
    /** Seconds in one play: the loop length (the longest animation, or a common multiple). Default 6. */
    span?: number;
    /** Plays before it rests and the engine settles (default 3). */
    loops?: number;
    /** The custom property the animations read (default "--fz-t"). */
    prop?: string;
    /** Frame-rate cap, e.g. 30 for steps() blinks (default: none, 60 Hz). */
    fps?: number;
    /** Animate (default: yes, unless the visitor prefers reduced motion). */
    motion?: boolean;
    /** Aborting it destroys the clock (Recall included). */
    signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

### cssClock (function, BETA)

Run the CSS

@keyframes under `root` on the kernel clock: each paused animation reads its time from one custom property a timeline moves. It settles after `loops` plays and wakes on pointer, focus or coming back into view; `destroy()` gives the root's style back.

Signature: `cssClock(root: HTMLElement, o?: CssClockOptions): CssClock`
- root: `HTMLElement`
- o (optional): `CssClockOptions`
- returns: `CssClock`

```ts
export declare function cssClock(root: HTMLElement, o?: CssClockOptions): {
    engine: {
        signal: AbortSignal;
        events: import("./kernel/index.js").EventRing;
        ledger: import("./kernel/index.js").Ledger;
        random: import("./kernel/index.js").Random;
        root: Element | null;
        timing: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        dt: number;
        readonly time: number;
        readonly steps: number;
        readonly phase: number;
        readonly live: number;
        readonly running: boolean;
        readonly paused: string[];
        add<S extends import("./kernel/index.js").System>(s: S): S;
        remove(s: import("./kernel/index.js").System): void;
        pool<T>(name: string, cap: number, create: () => T): import("./kernel/index.js").Pool<T>;
        start(): void;
        busy(sec?: number): void;
        wake(): void;
        stop(): void;
        frame(now: number): void;
        advance(sec: number): void;
        stats(): import("./kernel/index.js").EngineStats;
        destroy(): void;
    };
    tl: {
        to(targets: object | ArrayLike<object>, values: Record<string, import("./timeline.js").Value>, t?: import("./timeline.js").TrackOptions): /*elided*/ any;
        label(name: string, t?: number | string): /*elided*/ any;
        play: () => /*elided*/ any;
        reverse: () => /*elided*/ any;
        pause(by?: unknown): /*elided*/ any;
        seek(t: number): /*elided*/ any;
        finish: () => /*elided*/ any;
        revert(): /*elided*/ any;
        done: () => Promise<void>;
        readonly time: number;
        readonly duration: number;
        readonly playing: boolean;
        readonly reduced: boolean;
        step(e: import("./kernel/index.js").Engine, dt: number): void;
        render(): void;
    };
    /** Play from the start (unless held). */
    play: () => void;
    /** Hold or release (a pause button): held, it keeps its frame and asks for nothing. */
    hold(on: boolean): void;
    /** Stop for good and give the page back (Recall). */
    destroy: () => void;
};
```

### CssClock (type, BETA)

The clock `cssClock()` returns.

```ts
export type CssClock = ReturnType<typeof cssClock>;
```

## @fzlt/core/layout

Status: ALPHA. Size: 1745 B gzip (budget 2048 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/layout.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/layout"`

Force-directed layout on typed arrays, with a Barnes-Hut pass, for diagrams and graphs that settle. Nodes repel (a quadtree, rebuilt each step, sums far groups as one mass: O(n log n)), links pull like springs toward their length, and a weak pull holds the graph around (`cx`, `cy`). One tick per fixed step, so a run replays exactly. - Settle: `alpha` cools from 1 toward 0 over `ticks` steps; when it is spent, or nothing moved more than `still` px in a step, the layout rests and stops calling `busy()`: the engine sleeps. `heat()`, `pin()` and `link()` warm it up and wake the engine. - Reduced motion: the whole run happens in one step, so the graph lands where it settles. - Zero allocation per step; fixed capacity (`cap` nodes, `links` links: add and link return -1 when full). - DOM-free: draw it anywhere (@fzlt/core/view-canvas), frame it with @fzlt/core/camera (`bounds`). Distances use steer's exact `hypot` (Math.hypot boxes its arguments).

### LayoutOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `layout`: capacity, forces, cooling and motion.

```ts
export interface LayoutOptions {
    /** Nodes (fixed: the arrays never grow). */
    cap: number;
    /** Links (default 2 × cap). */
    links?: number;
    /** Repulsion between nodes, px² per tick (default 30). */
    charge?: number;
    /** A link's rest length in px (default 40; `link` takes its own). */
    distance?: number;
    /** Pull toward the centre, per tick (default 0.04). */
    gravity?: number;
    /** The centre gravity pulls toward, x (default 0). */
    cx?: number;
    /** The centre gravity pulls toward, y (default 0). */
    cy?: number;
    /** Barnes-Hut accuracy: a cell of size s at distance d counts as one mass when s / d < theta (default 0.9). */
    theta?: number;
    /** Velocity kept per tick (default 0.6). */
    keep?: number;
    /** Steps a full run cools over (default 300: five seconds at 60 Hz). */
    ticks?: number;
    /** At rest once no node moves more than this many px in a step (default 0.02). */
    still?: number;
    /** Animate (default: yes, unless the visitor prefers reduced motion; then each run lands at once). */
    motion?: boolean;
}
```

### layout (function, ALPHA)

A force-directed layout on typed arrays (`x`, `y`): Barnes-Hut repulsion, links, centre gravity. It cools over `ticks` steps, then rests and stops calling `busy()` so the engine settles. DOM-free.

Signature: `layout(engine: Engine, o: LayoutOptions): Layout`
- engine: `Engine`
- o: `LayoutOptions`
- returns: `Layout`

```ts
export declare function layout(engine: Engine, o: LayoutOptions): {
    x: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    y: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    vx: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    vy: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Nodes and links added so far. */
    readonly size: number;
    readonly links: number;
    /** How warm the run is: 1 just heated, 0 at rest. */
    readonly alpha: number;
    /** At rest: no ticks, no busy(); the engine can settle. */
    readonly resting: boolean;
    /** Add a node at (x, y) (default: a sunflower spiral round the centre); its index, or -1 when full. */
    add(ax?: number, ay?: number): number;
    /** Link nodes a and b at rest length `len` (default `distance`); its index, or -1 when full. */
    link(a: number, b: number, len?: number): number;
    /** Hold node i at (x, y) (a drag): the rest flows round it. */
    pin(i: number, ax: number, ay: number): void;
    /** Let node i go. */
    free(i: number): void;
    /** Warm the run up to at least `alpha` (default 1) and wake the engine. */
    heat(alpha?: number): void;
    /** The node nearest (ax, ay) within `r` px, or -1. */
    nearest(ax: number, ay: number, r?: number): number;
    /** The box round every node, [left, top, right, bottom], into `out` (no allocation). */
    bounds<T extends {
        [i: number]: number;
    }>(out: T): T;
    step(e: Engine): void;
};
```

### Layout (type, ALPHA)

What `layout` returns: `x`, `y`, `add`, `link`, `pin`, `free`, `heat`, `nearest`, `bounds`.

```ts
export type Layout = ReturnType<typeof layout>;
```

## @fzlt/core/view-canvas

Status: ALPHA. Size: 936 B gzip (budget 1229 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/view-canvas.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/view-canvas"`

One overlay canvas per root, sized for the screen's pixel density and redrawn only where something changed. The canvas covers the root's padding box (`pointer-events: none`, so the root keeps its input), its backing store is the CSS size × devicePixelRatio (capped by `maxDpr`), and drawing is in CSS px. - Dirty redraw: `dirty([x, y, w, h])` grows one box (no arguments: the whole canvas); in the render phase that box, snapped out to whole device pixels, is cleared, clipped and handed to `draw`. Nothing dirty, nothing drawn: a still view costs no canvas work at all. - Settle: it never keeps the engine awake; `dirty()` wakes a settled engine for one redraw. - Layout reads only in the read phase, and only after a resize or a zoom (a ResizeObserver). - Recall: the canvas goes and the root's style comes back exactly (the engine's ledger). It has no motion of its own: reduced motion belongs to whatever moves the drawing.

### ViewCanvasOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `viewCanvas`: the `draw` callback, the density cap and an accessible name.

```ts
export interface ViewCanvasOptions {
    /** Paint. The canvas is already cleared and clipped to `box` ([x, y, w, h], CSS px): draw the
     *  scene (anything outside the box is clipped away, so drawing it all is fine). */
    draw(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, box: Float64Array): void;
    /** The most pixel density drawn (default 2: sharp on a phone, a quarter of the pixels at 4×). */
    maxDpr?: number;
    /** An accessible name: the canvas becomes role="img" (default: aria-hidden, decoration). */
    label?: string;
}
```

### viewCanvas (function, ALPHA)

One overlay canvas on `root`, sized for the pixel density (capped by `maxDpr`) and redrawn only inside the dirty box: `dirty([x, y, w, h])` (CSS px), or `dirty()` for all of it. Never keeps the engine awake; Recall removes the canvas and gives the root's style back.

Signature: `viewCanvas(engine: Engine, root: HTMLElement, o: ViewCanvasOptions): ViewCanvas`
- engine: `Engine`
- root: `HTMLElement`
- o: `ViewCanvasOptions`
- returns: `ViewCanvas`

```ts
export declare function viewCanvas(engine: Engine, root: HTMLElement, o: ViewCanvasOptions): {
    canvas: HTMLCanvasElement;
    ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D;
    /** The canvas size in CSS px, as last measured. */
    readonly width: number;
    readonly height: number;
    /** The device pixels per CSS px it draws at. */
    readonly dpr: number;
    /** Redraw box [x, y, w, h] (CSS px) on the next render; no box, the whole canvas. The box comes
     *  in an array, not as four numbers: doubles passed to a call are boxed. Wakes a settled engine. */
    dirty(b?: {
        readonly [i: number]: number;
    }): void;
    read(): void;
    render(): void;
};
```

### ViewCanvas (type, ALPHA)

What `viewCanvas` returns: `canvas`, `ctx`, `width`, `height`, `dpr` and `dirty(box?)`.

```ts
export type ViewCanvas = ReturnType<typeof viewCanvas>;
```

## @fzlt/core/diorama

Status: ALPHA. Size: 7258 B gzip (budget 7296 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/diorama.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/diorama"`

Software 3D for cutaway tabletop scenes, drawn on a 2D canvas you own. A scene is data: objects `{ id, shape, size, pos, rot, color, on }` where `on` names the object it rests on (its `pos` is then from the parent's top centre, and it moves, tilts and sinks with it, its alpha and tint inherited). Flat-shaded convex shapes (box with a face mask, wedge, cylinder or cone, prism from an outline, group), one directional light, edge lines, blob shadows, picking. - Painter's sort by cluster → layer → depth: a cluster is a group drawn together (fixed ranks first, then far to near by its anchor), a layer orders parts inside it, and depth orders the rest. `below` puts the faces under a cut plane on their own layer (hulls under water). - Points (sparks, shells, smoke) and decals go into the same sort, so effects sit between faces; a pool with `rank: "depth"` sorts each point among the clusters by its own depth. - Limits: faces are never split, so two faces that cross each other, or a big face beside a small one at the wrong depth, can draw in the wrong order: split them into parts, or order them with clusters and layers. A face with a vertex behind the camera is dropped, not clipped. - Pools: there is no `remove`; add a fixed pool up front and let go of an object (a composite with its parts) with `ob.off = true`: its whole subtree stops drawing, shadowing, picking and costing matrix work. `hidden` hides the object alone (an invisible parent whose parts still show). - No allocation per `draw()` in the steady state (typed arrays, a merge sort into fixed buffers, shades cached as strings). No DOM of its own and no clock: call `draw()` from the engine's render phase (`engine.add({ render: () => d.draw() })`) or on your own, and `resize()` after a resize. Colours are `#rrggbb`. 2D lengths use steer's exact `hypot` (the builtin boxes its arguments).

### DioramaShape (type, ALPHA)

The shapes: `box` (`mask` drops faces), `wedge` (a ramp, tall at −x), `cyl` (`sides`, `top` scale: 0 is a cone), `prism` (an `outline` of [x, z] points, `taper` scales its bottom) and `group` (no faces: a parent to move, tilt and tag a set of parts).

```ts
export type DioramaShape = "box" | "wedge" | "cyl" | "prism" | "group";
```

### DioramaObjectDef (interface, ALPHA)

One object to `add`. Sizes and positions are world units; y is up; the origin is the bottom centre.

```ts
export interface DioramaObjectDef {
    /** A name for `get`, `on` and an `on` parent. */
    id?: string;
    /** The shape (default `box`). */
    shape?: DioramaShape;
    /** [width (x), height (y), depth (z)] (default [1, 1, 1]). */
    size?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Position: world, or from the parent's top centre when `on` is set. */
    pos?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Rotation in radians, [x, y, z], applied y, then x, then z. */
    rot?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** `#rrggbb` (default `#cccccc`). */
    color?: string;
    /** 0..1, multiplied down through the children (default 1). */
    alpha?: number;
    /** A colour that replaces this object's and its children's (a hit flash, a selection). */
    tint?: string | null;
    /** Not drawn (its children still are: an invisible parent). */
    hidden?: boolean;
    /** Off with its whole subtree: none of them draw, cast a shadow or pick, and their matrices are not
     *  computed (`M` keeps its last value until it is on again). Let go of a pooled composite with it. */
    off?: boolean;
    /** The id of the object it rests on. */
    on?: string | null;
    /** Blob shadow strength on the parent's top, 0..1 (0: none); drawn on the parent's layer + 0.5. */
    shadow?: number;
    /** Order inside its cluster, 0..655 in steps of 0.01 (default: its parent's + 1, so what rests on
     *  something draws after it and its shadow, which sits at the parent's + 0.5; at the root, 4). */
    layer?: number;
    /** Faces whose centre is under the plane y draw on `layer` (a hull under the water line). */
    below?: {
        y: number;
        layer: number;
    } | null;
    /** Layers it and its children drop by while it is on the far side of its parent: its place across
     *  the parent (`pos` x, z, turned with the parent) points away from the eye, along the ray from the
     *  eye to the parent (right anywhere on screen, not only in the middle). A wheel set above
     *  the body with `behind` past it draws over the body on the near side and under it on the far
     *  side, at any heading and view (default 0: off). */
    behind?: number;
    /** Its cluster's name; default: its parent's, or its own (anchored on itself) at the root. */
    cluster?: string;
    /** Full brightness: the light does not shade it (a lamp). */
    emissive?: boolean;
    /** `false`: `pick` passes through it. */
    pick?: boolean;
    /** Anything; `root()` climbs to the nearest tagged ancestor. */
    tag?: unknown;
    /** box: the faces kept, a bit mask (1 top, 2 bottom, 4 +x, 8 −x, 16 +z, 32 −z; default 63). */
    mask?: number;
    /** cyl: sides (default 10). */
    sides?: number;
    /** cyl: the top's scale (default 1; under 0.02, a cone). */
    top?: number;
    /** prism: the outline, [x, z] points. */
    outline?: ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number>>;
    /** prism: the bottom's scale (default 1). */
    taper?: number;
}
```

### DioramaObject (interface, ALPHA)

A live object: change `pos`, `rot`, `color`, `alpha`, `tint`, `hidden`, `off`, `shadow`, `layer`, `behind` between draws. `M` is its world matrix from the last draw it was on in (3 × 3 rotation row by row, then x, y, z).

```ts
export interface DioramaObject {
    /** Its name, or null. */
    readonly id: string | null;
    /** Its shape. */
    readonly shape: DioramaShape;
    /** [w, h, d]. */
    readonly size: Float64Array;
    /** Position (see `DioramaObjectDef.pos`). */
    pos: Float64Array;
    /** Rotation, radians. */
    rot: Float64Array;
    /** `#rrggbb`. */
    color: string;
    /** 0..1. */
    alpha: number;
    /** Colour override for it and its children, or null. */
    tint: string | null;
    /** Not drawn (its children still are). */
    hidden: boolean;
    /** Off with its whole subtree: not drawn, no shadows, not picked, matrices not computed. */
    off: boolean;
    /** Blob shadow strength. */
    shadow: number;
    /** Order inside its cluster. */
    layer: number;
    /** The cut plane. */
    below: {
        y: number;
        layer: number;
    } | null;
    /** Layers it drops by on the far side of its parent. */
    behind: number;
    /** Unshaded. */
    emissive: boolean;
    /** Pickable. */
    pick: boolean;
    /** Anything. */
    tag: unknown;
    /** The parent's id (change it with `on()`). */
    readonly on: string | null;
    /** The parent object. */
    readonly parent: DioramaObject | null;
    /** The world matrix from the last draw. */
    readonly M: Float64Array;
}
```

### DioramaCamera (interface, ALPHA)

The orbit camera: it looks at (tx, ty, tz) from `dist` away, turned by `yaw` and raised by `pitch` (radians); `fov` is the vertical field of view; (ox, oy) shift the picture in CSS px.

```ts
export interface DioramaCamera {
    /** Turn around the target (radians). */
    yaw: number;
    /** Look down from the horizon (radians; π/2 is straight down). */
    pitch: number;
    /** Distance to the target. */
    dist: number;
    /** Target x. */
    tx: number;
    /** Target y. */
    ty: number;
    /** Target z. */
    tz: number;
    /** Screen shift x, CSS px. */
    ox: number;
    /** Screen shift y, CSS px. */
    oy: number;
    /** Vertical field of view (radians). */
    fov: number;
}
```

### PointsOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `points`: capacity, where they sort, their colour or their own painter.

```ts
export interface PointsOptions {
    /** How many (fixed). */
    cap: number;
    /** The cluster they sort in (default: after every cluster, by depth among themselves). */
    cluster?: string;
    /** Their layer inside it (default 5). */
    layer?: number;
    /** `"depth"`: each point sorts among the clusters by its own depth, as if it were an unfixed
     *  cluster anchored on itself (debris behind a figure draws before it, in front after it);
     *  `cluster` is then ignored. Default: the pool sorts in one cluster. */
    rank?: "depth";
    /** Fill colour of the default disc (default `#ffffff`; `color[i]` overrides one). */
    color?: string;
    /** Paint point i yourself: its screen centre and radius are `sx[i]`, `sy[i]`, `sr[i]` (CSS px). */
    paint?: (ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, i: number, p: DioramaPoints) => void;
}
```

### DioramaPoints (interface, ALPHA)

A fixed pool of points drawn in the depth sort: write `x`, `y`, `z` (world), `r` (world radius), `a` (alpha, 0 skips it) for 0 ≤ i < `n`, then draw. `sx`, `sy`, `sr` are their screen values.

```ts
export interface DioramaPoints {
    /** Live count: points 0..n−1 draw. */
    n: number;
    /** World x. */
    readonly x: Float64Array;
    /** World y. */
    readonly y: Float64Array;
    /** World z. */
    readonly z: Float64Array;
    /** World radius. */
    readonly r: Float64Array;
    /** Alpha (starts at 1). */
    readonly a: Float64Array;
    /** Per-point fill, or undefined for the pool's colour. */
    readonly color: (string | undefined)[];
    /** Screen x from the last draw. */
    readonly sx: Float64Array;
    /** Screen y from the last draw. */
    readonly sy: Float64Array;
    /** Screen radius from the last draw. */
    readonly sr: Float64Array;
    /** The cluster they sort in, or null. */
    cluster: string | null;
    /** Their layer. */
    layer: number;
    /** `"depth"`: each point ranks among the clusters by its depth; null: in `cluster`. */
    rank: "depth" | null;
    /** The default disc colour. */
    colorAll: string;
    /** A custom painter, or null. */
    paint: PointsOptions["paint"] | null;
}
```

### DioramaOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `diorama`: light, background, overlay, edges and capacities.

```ts
export interface DioramaOptions {
    /** The light's direction (towards the light; default [0.5, 1, 0.4]). */
    light?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Ambient light, 0..1 (default 0.56). */
    ambient?: number;
    /** Clear colour each draw (a string, or a function read each draw); none: transparent. */
    background?: string | (() => string);
    /** Shadow colour (default `#000000`); a getter is read each draw. */
    shadowColor?: string;
    /** Edge lines (default true). */
    edge?: boolean;
    /** Paint over the finished frame (HUD, cursors): `overlay(ctx, d)`. */
    overlay?: (ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, d: Diorama) => void;
    /** The most pixel density drawn (default 2). */
    maxDpr?: number;
    /** Vertex capacity (default 16384; `add` throws past it). */
    maxVerts?: number;
    /** Faces, shadows, points and decals per frame (default 8192; past it they are dropped and counted). */
    maxFaces?: number;
    /** Blob shadows per frame (default 512). */
```

### diorama (function, ALPHA)

A diorama on `canvas`: `add` objects, aim `cam` (or `fit` it), then `draw()`. It never touches the DOM beyond the canvas's backing store (`resize`), and allocates nothing per draw.

Signature: `diorama(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, o?: DioramaOptions): Diorama`
- canvas: `HTMLCanvasElement`
- o (optional): `DioramaOptions`
- returns: `Diorama`

```ts
export declare function diorama(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, o?: DioramaOptions): {
    /** The canvas's 2D context. */
    ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D;
    /** The camera `draw`, `project`, `ground` and `pick` use: change it freely between draws. */
    cam: DioramaCamera;
    /** The last draw: faces, shadows, points, verts, objects on (matrices computed; `off` subtrees left out), and entries dropped (over maxFaces). */
    stats: {
        faces: number;
        shadows: number;
        points: number;
        verts: number;
        objects: number;
        dropped: number;
    };
    /** Add an object (`DioramaObjectDef`); returns its live handle. Throws past `maxVerts`. */
    add: (d: DioramaObjectDef) => DioramaObject;
    /** The object named `id`. */
    get: (id: string) => DioramaObject | undefined;
    /** Rest `ob` on `parentId` (null: on nothing); its `pos` is from then on from the new parent's top. */
    on(ob: DioramaObject, parentId: string | null): void;
    /** Remove every object, cluster, decal and point pool (meshes stay cached). */
    clear: () => void;
    /** Name a cluster: `{ fixed: n }` draws before every unfixed one, in n order (a room, a table);
     *  `{ at: [x, y, z] }` ranks it far to near by that point. Redefining one keeps its objects. */
    cluster: (name: string, c: {
        fixed?: number;
        at?: ArrayLike<number>;
    }) => void;
    /** Paint `fn(ctx)` in the sort: in `cluster` at `layer`, behind that layer's faces, or by the
     *  depth of `at` (read each draw) among them. */
    decal(cl: string, layer: number, fn: (ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D) => void, at?: ArrayLike<number> | null): void;
    /** A fixed pool of points (sparks, shells, smoke) drawn in the depth sort (`DioramaPoints`). */
    points(p: PointsOptions): DioramaPoints;
    /** Set the light's direction (towards it) and the ambient level. */
    setLight: (v: ArrayLike<number>, a?: number) => void;
    /** Size the backing store: CSS width and height and the density (no arguments: the canvas's
     *  client size and devicePixelRatio, capped at `maxDpr`; a layout read, so call it after a resize). */
    resize: (w?: number, h?: number, r?: number) => void;
    /** Frame `points` ([x, y, z, …], world) inside the safe rect: sets c.dist, then c.ox and c.oy so
     *  the points' screen box is centred in it. Uses c's yaw, pitch, target and fov; returns c. */
    fit: (c: DioramaCamera, pts: ArrayLike<number>, s: SafeRect) => DioramaCamera;
    /** Hold `c` (default `cam`) inside the limits; returns c. */
    clamp: (l: CameraLimits, c?: DioramaCamera) => DioramaCamera;
    /** Draw the frame: matrices, sort, paint, then `overlay`. */
    draw: () => void;
    /** The front-most pickable object under (x, y) (CSS px), as of the last draw, or null. */
    pick: (x: number, y: number) => DioramaObject | null;
    /** Where the ray under (x, y) meets the plane y = planeY: out = [x, y, z]; false if it never does. */
    ground: (x: number, y: number, py: number, out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }) => boolean;
    /** World (x, y, z) to screen: out = [x, y, depth]; false when behind the camera. */
    project(x: number, y: number, z: number, out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }): boolean;
    /** The camera's world position (the eye): out = [x, y, z]; returns out. */
    eye<T extends {
        [i: number]: number;
    }>(out: T): T;
    /** Screen px per world unit at depth 1 (a size s at depth z is s × focal() / z px). */
    focal: () => number;
    /** Call fn on every object (recolour on a theme change, find parts). */
    recolor(fn: (ob: DioramaObject) => void): void;
    /** The nearest ancestor with a `tag` (or the top of the chain): what a pick on a part belongs to. */
    root(ob: DioramaObject | null): DioramaObject | null;
    /** CSS width, as last sized. */
    readonly width: number;
    /** CSS height, as last sized. */
    readonly height: number;
    /** Device pixels per CSS px. */
    readonly dpr: number;
};
```

### Diorama (type, ALPHA)

What `diorama` returns.

```ts
export type Diorama = ReturnType<typeof diorama>;
```

### OccludeOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `occlude`: the objects that may stand in the way and how they fade.

```ts
export interface OccludeOptions {
    /** Root objects (no `on`) whose boxes (`size` from `pos`, turned by `rot[1]`) can hide the targets. */
    objects: DioramaObject[];
    /** The alpha of an object in the way (default 0.16). */
    ghost?: number;
    /** Seconds a full fade takes (default 0.15). */
    t?: number;
    /** Reduced motion: snap instead of fading (also a live field on the result). */
    reduced?: boolean;
    /** A box met within this distance of a target is touching it, not in the way (default 0). */
    near?: number;
}
```

### occlude (function, ALPHA)

Fade what stands between the eye and the targets (a chase camera in a town): each `step(dt, pts)` casts rays from `d.eye()` to every target point (`pts`: [x, y, z, …], world; `n` of them, default all) against each object's box; one in the way eases its `alpha` toward `ghost`, one the eye is inside toward 0, the rest back to 1. Returns true while anything is still fading (keep the engine awake). Writes `alpha` only (render side, never the sim). Boxes off the bounds of the eye and the targets are skipped; `tested` counts the boxes ray-tested in the last step. No allocation per step.

Signature: `occlude(d: Diorama, o: OccludeOptions): { reduced: boolean; tested: number; step(dt: number, pts: ArrayLike<number>, n?: number): boolean; }`
- d: `Diorama`
- o: `OccludeOptions`
- returns: `{ reduced: boolean; tested: number; step(dt: number, pts: ArrayLike<number>, n?: number): boolean; }`

```ts
export declare function occlude(d: Diorama, o: OccludeOptions): {
    reduced: boolean;
    tested: number;
    step(dt: number, pts: ArrayLike<number>, n?: number): boolean;
};
```

## @fzlt/core/dice

Status: ALPHA. Size: 4262 B gzip (budget 4352 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/dice.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/dice"`

Seeded dice for tabletop games. `roll(seed, n, sides)` gives the values; `dice()` also builds a short tumble for each d6 (positions and orientations over time) that lands on the value the seed picked, so every player who rolls the same seed sees the same roll. - The values come from integer maths only (a 32-bit hash generator): the same seed gives the same values in every browser. The tumble is made to end on them (it is not a physics run that might land on an edge), so the face that lands up is the value by construction. The tumble is the look and never feeds a result: it keeps the builtin `Math.sin`, `cos`, `acos` and `**`, whose last bit may differ between engines (a path may differ in its last bits; the values never do), so an online sim reads `value`, never `path`. - The path is data: `path` holds `frames` samples per die of [x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw] (y up, the centre's height over the floor, a unit quaternion), and `pose(i, t, out)` reads it at any time. - `dioramaDice` builds the dice into an `@fzlt/core/diorama` scene (a chamfered body, pips painted on the faces that look at the camera) and shows them at a time; `popDome` puts them under a clear dome that you press: they jump, tumble and land. No allocation per `roll`, `pose` or `show` in the steady state (typed arrays, fixed capacity). Distances on the floor use steer's exact `hypot` (the builtin boxes its arguments).

### DiceOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `dice()`: how many, their size and the tumble's length and sample rate.

```ts
    /** The most dice (default `count`). */
    cap?: number;
    /** Edge length in world units (default 1). */
    size?: number;
    /** Seconds from the throw to rest (default 1.4). */
    duration?: number;
    /** Samples per second in `path` (default 60). */
    rate?: number;
}
```

### ThrowOptions (interface, ALPHA)

```ts
export interface ThrowOptions {
    /** Where the throw starts, [x, z] on the floor (default [−4 × size, 0] from `to`). */
    from?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Where the dice land, [x, z] (default [0, 0]). */
    to?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** How high the dice start over where they rest (a throw), or how high they jump (a pop); default 2.5 × size. */
    height?: number;
    /** Space between the dice across the throw (default 1.7 × size). */
    spread?: number;
    /** Each landing spot moves up to this far, seeded (default 0.35 × size). */
    jitter?: number;
    /** Full forward rolls on the way (default: by the distance; at least 1). */
    turns?: number;
    /** A pop: each die jumps from where it rests (the last roll's landing), straight up. */
    pop?: boolean;
}
```

### dice (function, ALPHA)

A set of d6 with tumble paths: `roll(seed, throw)` fills `value` and `path`; `pose(i, t, out)` reads die i at t seconds. Between rolls the dice rest where they landed.

## @fzlt/core/track

Status: ALPHA. Size: 2055 B gzip (budget 2112 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/track.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/track"`

Board paths for roll-and-move games. Spaces along a closed loop or an open path, straight between the points you give or on a smooth curve through them, in board coordinates [x, z] (diorama's floor plane; y is up). Jumps (chutes, ladders, shortcuts) take a token from one space to another; several tokens on one space spread around it, then stack upward. - `move(token, steps)` works out the whole move at once: the hops (a step per space, then any jumps), with a flag on each for passing the start ("go"), bouncing back, the finish and the landing; an open path ends by stopping at the end, needing the exact count, or bouncing back. - The hops are data with times: `sample(t, out)` gives the moving token's [x, y, z] (an arc per step, a slide or climb for a jump), `apply(ob, t)` writes it into a diorama object's `pos`. - Events, if you pass an event ring (`engine.events`), as `move` works the move out: `track:pass`, `track:jump`, `track:finish`, `track:land` and `track:stay` (an exact finish overshot), each with the token and the space. No randomness (the dice decide) and no allocation per move or sample (typed arrays, fixed capacity). Lengths use steer's exact `hypot` (the builtin boxes its arguments).

### TrackEvents (interface, ALPHA)

Something that takes events: an engine's ring (`engine.events`).

```ts
export interface TrackEvents {
    emit(type: string, a?: number, b?: number): unknown;
}
```

### TrackFinish (type, ALPHA)

How an open path ends when a move would go past the last space.

```ts
export type TrackFinish = "stop" | "exact" | "bounce";
```

### TrackOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `track()`: the path, its spaces, jumps, sharing, the end rule and the hop's look.

```ts
export interface TrackOptions {
    /** The path's points, [x0, z0, x1, z1, …], in board units. */
    points: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** A loop: the last space leads to the first (default false: an open path, start to finish). */
    closed?: boolean;
    /** Lay this many spaces at even distances along the path (default: one space per point). */
    spaces?: number;
    /** A smooth curve through the points (Catmull-Rom) instead of straight lines; needs `spaces`. */
    smooth?: boolean;
    /** Jumps as [from, to] space pairs: a ladder up, a chute down, a shortcut. */
    jumps?: ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number>>;
    /** Tokens side by side on a space before the next ones stack on top (one number, or one per space; default 4). */
    cap?: number | ArrayLike<number>;
    /** How far apart tokens that share a space stand from its centre (default 0.3). */
    spacing?: number;
    /** The height of one stacked level (default 0.3). */
    level?: number;
    /** The most tokens (default 8). */
    tokens?: number;
    /** An open path's end: "stop" at the last space (default), "exact" (a move past it does not move)
     *  or "bounce" (count back from it). */
    finish?: TrackFinish;
    /** The space a token passes on a loop to "pass go" (default 0). */
    start?: number;
    /** The arc's height over a step (default 0.6). */
    hop?: number;
    /** Seconds per step (default 0.22). */
    hopTime?: number;
    /** Board units per second along a jump (default 6; at least 1.5 steps long). */
    jumpSpeed?: number;
    /** The most hops in one move (default 64). */
    maxHops?: number;
    /** An event ring for `track:pass`, `track:jump`, `track:finish`, `track:land`. */
    events?: TrackEvents;
}
```

### HOP (const, ALPHA)

Hop kinds and flags (`hops.kind`, `hops.flag`).

Type: `{ /** A step to the next (or previous) space. */ readonly step: 0; /** A jump from a space to its target. */ readonly jump: 1; /** Flag: this hop enters the start space going forward on a loop (pass go). */ readonly pass: 1; /** Flag: a step backward after the end (bounce). */ readonly back: 2; /** Flag: the move ends on the last space of an open path. */ readonly finish: 4; /** Flag: the last hop of the move. */ readonly land: 8; }`

```ts
export declare const HOP: {
    /** A step to the next (or previous) space. */
    readonly step: 0;
    /** A jump from a space to its target. */
    readonly jump: 1;
    /** Flag: this hop enters the start space going forward on a loop (pass go). */
    readonly pass: 1;
    /** Flag: a step backward after the end (bounce). */
    readonly back: 2;
    /** Flag: the move ends on the last space of an open path. */
    readonly finish: 4;
    /** Flag: the last hop of the move. */
    readonly land: 8;
};
```

### track (function, ALPHA)

A board path on `o.points`: `place` tokens, `move` them, then `sample` the hops over time.

Signature: `track(o: TrackOptions): Track`
- o: `TrackOptions`
- returns: `Track`

```ts
export declare function track(o: TrackOptions): {
    /** Spaces. */
    n: number;
    closed: boolean;
    /** Space centres. */
    x: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    z: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Each space's heading: diorama's rot[1] that turns +x along the path. */
    a: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Each space's jump target, or −1. */
    jump: Int32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Each token's space, or −1 off the board. */
    at: Int32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** The last move's hops (`HOP` kinds and flags; `A`, `B`: each hop's ends, [x, y, z] × n). */
    hops: {
        /** Hops in the last move. */
        n: number;
        kind: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        flag: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        from: Int32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        to: Int32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        t0: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        t1: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        A: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
        B: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    };
    /** The token the last move moved, or −1. */
    readonly token: number;
    /** Seconds the last move takes. */
    duration: number;
    /** Put token k on space s (−1 takes it off), with no hops. */
    place(k: number, s: number): void;
    /** Tokens on space s. */
    count(s: number): number;
    /** Move token k by `steps` (negative: back) and any jumps where it lands. Fills `hops` and
     *  returns its count (0: it did not move, e.g. an exact finish it overshot). */
    move(k: number, steps: number): number;
    slot: (k: number, out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }, s?: number) => {
        [i: number]: number;
    };
    spot: (s: number, r: number, m: number, out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }) => {
        [i: number]: number;
    };
    /** Where the moving token is at t seconds into the last move: out = [x, y, z] (y over the board's
     *  top). False once the move is over (out is then its landing place). */
    sample(t: number, out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }): boolean;
    /** Write `sample(t)` into a diorama object's `pos` (plus `y0` up); true while it moves. */
    apply(ob: {
        pos: {
            [i: number]: number;
        };
    }, t: number, y0?: number): boolean;
};
```

### Track (type, ALPHA)

What `track` returns.

```ts
export type Track = ReturnType<typeof track>;
```

## @fzlt/core/water

Status: ALPHA. Size: 5264 B gzip (budget 5376 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/water.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/water"`

Animated water for `@fzlt/core/diorama` scenes (a bay, a pond, a wave pool), lifted from the Salvo Bay prototype. `water(d, { rect | outline, level, … })` builds the water's body (depth bands as prisms) and paints its surface in the diorama's depth sort: wave crests that roll across, a drifting sheen, foam lapping along the edges you pick, bow waves and wakes behind the objects you `wake`, and pooled effects: `splash` (a column of water, spray, a crown of drops, rings and ripples that travel out), `ripple`, `bubbles` and `whirl` (something going down). - The surface is a function: `height(x, z, t)` is the same for the same (x, z, t) on every run (sines of the wave, plus the optional `swell`: a travelling, peeling crest a surfer can ride, its `slope` and its `crest` position). Effects are seeded (`seed`), so a replay splashes the same. - It has its own clock: `step(dt)` moves it and returns `busy`. The idle roll runs `idle` seconds after the last effect or `stir()`, then rests, so the engine can settle; `still` (reduced motion, on by default when the page asks for it) freezes the surface and keeps every effect short. - Everything is clipped to the outline and drawn from fixed pools (particles, rings, whirls, bubble emitters, wake trails): no allocation per `step` or draw in the steady state; past a pool's capacity an effect is dropped, never grown. Wakes read the object's world matrix from the last draw. DOM-free (one `matchMedia` read for the `still` default); 2D lengths use steer's exact `hypot`.

### water (function, ALPHA)

Water on diorama `d`. Call `step(dt)` from a fixed step (it returns `busy`); the diorama's own `draw()` paints it.

Signature: `water(d: Diorama, o: WaterOptions): Water`
- d: `Diorama`
- o: `WaterOptions`
- returns: `Water`

```ts
export declare function water(d: Diorama, o: WaterOptions): {
    /** The surface band and depth bands (diorama objects), bottom first. */
    bodies: DioramaObject[];
    /** The particle pool in the diorama's sort. */
    points: DioramaPoints;
    /** The surface's height, y. */
    level: number;
    /** Reduced motion: the surface holds still and effects stay short. */
    still: boolean;
    /** True while anything moves (set by `step`). */
    busy: boolean;
    /** The surface's clock (seconds it has rolled). */
    readonly time: number;
    /** Live particles after the last step. */
    readonly live: number;
    step: (dt: number) => boolean;
    /** Keep the surface rolling `sec` more seconds (default `idle`). */
    stir: (sec?: number) => void;
    height: (x: number, z: number, t?: number) => number;
    /** The surface's slope at (x, z): out = [dh/dx, dh/dz]. */
    slope<T extends {
        [i: number]: number;
    }>(x: number, z: number, out: T, t?: number): T;
    /** The swell now: out = [crest along its dir (x·dx + z·dz), the break point across it (from its
     *  low end), its height]; false when there is no swell or the crest is off the water. */
    crest(out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }, t?: number): boolean;
    /** A miss: a column of water that rises and falls back, spray and a crown of drops at its foot,
     *  a ring and ripples running out (size scales it). */
    splash(x: number, z: number, size?: number): undefined;
    /** A ring and a ripple running out from (x, z). */
    ripple(x: number, z: number, size?: number): void;
    /** Bubbles breaking on the surface round (x, z) for `sec` seconds, `spread` across. */
    bubbles(x: number, z: number, sec?: number, spread?: number): undefined;
    /** A whirlpool at (x, z), `size` across its arms, for `sec` seconds, and its rings. */
    whirl(x: number, z: number, size?: number, sec?: number): undefined;
    /** Bow waves and a trail behind `ob` (its position from its world matrix, as of the last draw). */
    wake(ob: DioramaObject, w?: WakeOptions): WaterWake;
    /** Stop a wake. */
    unwake(k: WaterWake): void;
    /** End every effect now (the surface keeps its clock). */
    clear(): void;
};
```

### Water (type, ALPHA)

What `water` returns.

```ts
export type Water = ReturnType<typeof water>;
```

## @fzlt/core/props

Status: ALPHA. Size: 3115 B gzip (budget 3200 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/props.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/props"`

A kit of small low-poly models for `@fzlt/core/diorama` scenes, so a new diorama starts furnished. Each prop is a function `prop(d, opts)` that adds a `group` root (its `size` is the prop's footprint, so its blob shadow fits) and its parts resting on it, at `pos`, turned by `rot` (yaw) and sized by `scale`, in soft pastel colours you can override by key; it returns the root. Move, turn, tilt, tint or hide the root and the whole prop follows; `d.root(d.pick(x, y))` on any part gives the root (its `tag` is the prop's name unless you pass one). - Sets: nature (`pineTree`, `roundTree`, `bush`, `rocks`, `cactus`), town (`house`, `shop`, `lamppost`, `bench`, `fence`, `trafficCone`, `crates`), coast (`lighthouse`, `dock`, `buoy`) and display vehicles (`car`, `truck`). Import only the props you use: each is its own function. - Units: about a metre (a house is 2.4 wide); local x is a prop's width, z its depth and +z its front (doors, windows, a car's side). `fence` and `dock` segments join end to end along x at `FENCE_STEP` and `DOCK_STEP` × scale. - Variants: `seed` (an integer) picks heights, widths, turns and counts from integer maths, so every player who builds the same seed gets the same scene. Each jitter is one of eight steps, so the diorama's mesh cache stays small however many seeds a scene uses. - Sorting: each prop is its own diorama cluster (named by its id) unless you pass `cluster`, and its parts are layered low to high, so props in a row never interleave. Make what they stand on a `fixed` cluster (`d.cluster("floor", { fixed: 0 })`), as clusters anchored on a point sort far to near. - Colours: every prop reads `colors[key]` before its own default, and the keys are shared across props (`wood`, `roof`, `glass`, `metal`, `lamp`, …), so one object re-themes a scene (a night set). Adding a prop allocates only what `d.add` does for its parts (pass an `id`; without one, a name is made from a counter). Nothing runs per frame: props are data in the diorama, drawn by its `draw()`.

### PropOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options every prop takes.

```ts
export interface PropOptions {
    /** The root's id (default `"prop" + n`, a counter); its parts are anonymous. */
    id?: string;
    /** The id of the object it stands on (its `pos` is then from that object's top centre). */
    on?: string | null;
    /** Position of its bottom centre, [x, y, z] (default [0, 0, 0]). */
    pos?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Turn around y, radians (default 0). */
    rot?: number;
    /** Size multiplier (default 1). */
    scale?: number;
    /** An integer picking the variant (default 0). */
    seed?: number;
    /** Colour overrides by key, `#rrggbb` (each prop lists its keys). */
    colors?: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
    /** Its diorama cluster (default: its own, named by its id; null: its parent's). */
    cluster?: string | null;
    /** Blob shadow strength on what it stands on (default 0.16 when `on` is set). */
    shadow?: number;
    /** The root's layer (default: diorama's, its parent's + 1); parts layer above it. */
    layer?: number;
    /** `false`: `pick` passes through every part. */
    pick?: boolean;
    /** The root's tag (default: the prop's name, e.g. `"house"`). */
    tag?: unknown;
}
```

## @fzlt/core/beam

Status: ALPHA. Size: 4388 B gzip (budget 4480 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/beam.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/beam"`

Lasers on a board. Parts (mirrors, splitters, blockers, targets, emitters) stand on a flat board plane in board coordinates [x, z], free or on a grid; `run()` casts every emitter's ray, reflecting off mirrors at any angle, passing through and splitting at splitters, stopping at blockers, targets and the board's edge, and writes the segments and hits into fixed typed arrays. - A part is a segment (`len`, turned by `a`) or a circle (`r`). Angles are radians from +x toward +z; on a diorama an object turned to angle a has `rot[1] = −a`. Multiples of π/4 take exact directions (no `Math.cos` rounding), so a grid puzzle traces the same bits in every browser. - Deterministic: the same parts give the same segments in the same order (depth first, the transmitted ray before the reflected one). `bounces` caps the turns on one path (`capped` counts the paths it stopped), `segs` the segments (`dropped` counts the rest). - `dioramaBeam` draws the result on an `@fzlt/core/diorama` board: glowing beams as decals in the depth sort (split into short pieces so they sort among the parts), a pulse of points along them, sparks where a beam hits a target or a blocker; a re-routed beam grows out from where it changed. No allocation per `run()` or `show()` in the steady state. 2D lengths use steer's exact `hypot`.

### MIRROR, SPLITTER, BLOCKER, TARGET, EMITTER (const, ALPHA)

Part kinds, as stored in `kind`.

```ts
export declare const MIRROR = 1, SPLITTER = 2, BLOCKER = 3, TARGET = 4, EMITTER = 5;
```

### BeamKind (type, ALPHA)

A part's kind by name.

```ts
export type BeamKind = "mirror" | "splitter" | "blocker" | "target" | "emitter";
```

### BeamPart (interface, ALPHA)

One part to `add`: where it stands, its shape and what it does to a beam.

```ts
export interface BeamPart {
    /** What it does: reflect, split (pass and reflect), stop, stop and light, or emit. */
    kind: BeamKind;
    /** Board x (or `col` on the grid). */
    x?: number;
    /** Board z (or `row` on the grid). */
    z?: number;
    /** Grid column: x is the cell's centre (needs `grid`). */
    col?: number;
    /** Grid row: z is the cell's centre. */
    row?: number;
    /** Angle, radians from +x toward +z: a segment's direction, or an emitter's beam (default 0). */
    a?: number;
    /** Segment length (default: the grid cell, or 1). */
    len?: number;
    /** A circle of this radius instead of a segment (a peg, a round target). */
    r?: number;
    /** A mirror reflects on its front only (the side its normal (−sin a, cos a) points to); its back blocks. */
    one?: boolean;
    /** Off: beams pass it, emitters stay dark (default on). */
    off?: boolean;
    /** Anything (the game's object). */
    tag?: unknown;
}
```

### BeamOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `beam()`: capacities, the cap on turns, the board's edge and grid.

```ts
export interface BeamOptions {
    /** The most parts (default 64). */
    cap?: number;
    /** The most segments per run (default 256). */
    segs?: number;
    /** The most hits per run (default 128). */
    hits?: number;
    /** The most turns (mirror or splitter hits) on one path (default 24). */
    bounces?: number;
    /** The board's edge [x0, z0, x1, z1]: beams stop there (default ±10,000). */
    bounds?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** A grid: cell size and the board point of cell (0, 0)'s corner; `col`/`row` place parts on it. */
    grid?: {
        cell: number;
        x0?: number;
        z0?: number;
    };
}
```

### beam (function, ALPHA)

A beam board: `add` parts, `run()` after any change, then read `segs` and `hits`.

Signature: `beam(o?: BeamOptions): Beam`
- o (optional): `BeamOptions`
- returns: `Beam`

```ts
export declare function beam(o?: BeamOptions): {
    /** Parts added. */
    readonly parts: number;
    /** Per part: its kind (MIRROR … EMITTER), centre, angle, direction, half length, radius. */
    kind: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    x: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    z: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    a: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    ux: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    uz: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    h: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    r: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Per part: 1 off, 2 one-sided. */
    flag: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Per part: hits in the last run (a target is lit when > 0). */
    lit: Uint16Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Per part: what `add` was given as `tag`. */
    tag: unknown[];
    /** Segments in the last run. */
    n: number;
    /** Segment start and end, board coordinates. */
    x0: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    z0: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    x1: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    z1: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Segment: distance along its path from the emitter at the start (a re-route grows from here). */
    sl: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Segment: power (1, halved at each split). */
    sp: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Segment: turns before it. */
    sg: Uint16Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Segment: the part it ends on, or −1 at the board's edge. */
    se: Int16Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Segment: its emitter (−1 for `cast`). */
    ss: Int16Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Hits in the last run. */
    nh: number;
    /** Hit: the part, the point, the segment that ends there. */
    hp: Int16Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    hx: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    hz: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    hs: Int16Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Paths the `bounces` cap stopped in the last run. */
    capped: number;
    /** Segments or splits past capacity in the last run. */
    dropped: number;
    /** Runs so far (a drawing helper redraws when it changes). */
    ver: number;
    /** Add a part; returns its index. */
    add: (p: BeamPart) => number;
    /** Move part i to (px, pz), turned to angle `ang` (radians). Then `run()`. */
    set(i: number, px: number, pz: number, ang?: number): void;
    /** Turn part i by `da` radians (a quarter turn of a grid mirror: π/2). Then `run()`. */
    turn(i: number, da: number): void;
    /** Switch part i on or off. Then `run()`. */
    enable(i: number, on: boolean): void;
    /** The grid cell [col, row] holding board point (px, pz): out = [col, row]. */
    cellAt(px: number, pz: number, out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }): {
        [i: number]: number;
    };
    /** The part centred in grid cell (col, row), or −1. */
    partAt(col: number, row: number): number;
    /** Targets lit in the last run. */
    litCount(): number;
    /** Clear the last run (segments, hits, lit). */
    reset: () => void;
    /** Append one ray from (px, pz) along (dx, dz) (no emitter part) at `power`; returns the segment count. */
    cast(px: number, pz: number, dx: number, dz: number, power?: number): number;
    /** Clear, then cast every emitter that is on; returns the segment count. */
    run: () => number;
};
```

### Beam (type, ALPHA)

What `beam` returns.

```ts
export type Beam = ReturnType<typeof beam>;
```

### DioramaBeamOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `dioramaBeam`: where the beams sit, their look and their motion.

```ts
export interface DioramaBeamOptions {
    /** The id of the board object the parts stand on: board [x, z] is from its top centre. */
    on: string;
    /** The beams' height over the board (default 0.35). */
    y?: number;
    /** The cluster they sort in (default "@" + on, the board's own). */
    cluster?: string;
    /** Their layer in it (default 5: among parts resting on a root board). */
    layer?: number;
    /** Glow colour (default `#ff3b3b`). */
    color?: string;
    /** Core colour (default `#fff1ea`). */
    core?: string;
    /** Spark colour (default `#ffd36b`). */
    spark?: string;
    /** Beam width, world units (default 0.1). */
    width?: number;
    /** The longest piece a segment is drawn in (default 1): shorter pieces sort better among parts. */
    piece?: number;
    /** The most pieces (default 192). */
    pieces?: number;
    /** How fast a beam grows out, world units per second (default 24). */
    speed?: number;
    /** Pulse points' spacing along the beam (default 1.6; 0: none). */
    pulse?: number;
    /** Pulse speed, world units per second (default 5). */
    pulseSpeed?: number;
    /** The most pulse points (default 96). */
    dots?: number;
    /** The most sparks (default 64). */
    sparks?: number;
    /** Seconds the pulse plays after a change before it fades and `show` lets the engine settle (default 1.4; Infinity: always). */
    hold?: number;
    /** false (reduced motion): beams appear at once, no pulse, no sparks. */
    motion?: boolean;
    /** Called when a target's light turns on (the beam reached it) or off: tint the target. */
    light?: (part: number, on: boolean) => void;
}
```

### dioramaBeam (function, ALPHA)

Draw beam `b` on diorama `d`. `show(t)` (t: a running clock in seconds) before each `d.draw()`; true while anything moves (a beam growing, sparks, the pulse within `hold` of a change).

Signature: `dioramaBeam(d: Diorama, b: Beam, o: DioramaBeamOptions): DioramaBeam`
- d: `Diorama`
- b: `Beam`
- o: `DioramaBeamOptions`
- returns: `DioramaBeam`

```ts
export declare function dioramaBeam(d: Diorama, b: Beam, o: DioramaBeamOptions): {
    /** Per part: 1 once the drawn beam reached it (a target's light). */
    on: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Pieces drawn. */
    readonly pieces: number;
    /** Targets lit on screen. */
    readonly lit: number;
    /** The pulse points and sparks pools. */
    dots: DioramaPoints;
    sparks: DioramaPoints;
    /** Pose the beams at t (seconds, a running clock); true while anything still moves. */
    show(t: number): boolean;
};
```

### DioramaBeam (type, ALPHA)

