## @fzlt/core/cards

Status: ALPHA. Size: 3383 B gzip (budget 3456 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/cards.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/cards"`

A deck of cards for tabletop games. Cards are numbers 0..size−1 (the game says what each one is); every card is in exactly one pile, at one place in it, face up or down. `shuffle(pile, seed)`, `draw`, `deal` to hands, `move`, `flip`, `gather` piles back. - The shuffle is a Fisher-Yates over a 32-bit integer generator with rejection sampling (no modulo bias), so the same seed gives the same order in every browser: both online players see the same deck. - Each change stamps the card with the deck's clock, so a drawing helper animates the moves in the order they were made. - `dioramaCards` builds the deck into an `@fzlt/core/diorama` scene: each card a thin card-shaped prism with its face or back painted on the side that looks at the camera (by your callbacks: the game paints its own art), laid out per pile as a stack, a row on the table, or a hand fanned toward the camera; moves fly in arcs, flips turn over, staggered in move order. `pick` names the card under a point. No allocation per deck operation, `show()` or draw in the steady state.

### DeckOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `deck()`: how many cards and the piles.

```ts
export interface DeckOptions {
    /** Cards (default 52). */
    size?: number;
    /** The piles: a count, or their names for `id` (default ["draw"]). Pile 0 holds the deck at first. */
    piles?: number | string[];
}
```

### deck (function, ALPHA)

A deck of `size` cards in piles. Read `pile`, `pos`, `up` per card and `count`/`at` per pile.

Signature: `deck(o?: DeckOptions): Deck`
- o (optional): `DeckOptions`
- returns: `Deck`

```ts
export declare function deck(o?: DeckOptions): {
    /** Cards. */
    size: number;
    /** Piles. */
    piles: number;
    /** Per card: its pile. */
    pile: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Per card: its index in the pile (0 is the bottom). */
    pos: Uint16Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Per card: 1 face up. */
    up: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Per card: the clock when it last moved or flipped. */
    stamp: Uint32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Moves and flips so far (each one stamps its card with the next tick). */
    clock: number;
    /** Changes so far (a shuffle counts one): a drawing helper re-lays the piles when it changes. */
    ver: number;
    /** A pile's index by name (−1 if none). */
    id: (name: string) => number;
    /** Cards in pile p. */
    count: (p: number) => number;
    /** The card at index i of pile p (0 the bottom; −1 the top, −2 under it, …), or −1. */
    at(p: number, i: number): number;
    /** The top card of pile p, or −1. */
    top: (p: number) => number;
    /** Every card back in pile 0, in order 0..size−1, face down (or up: `face` 1). */
    reset: (face?: number) => void;
    /** Move card c to pile `to` at index `at` (default: on top), face up (1), down (0) or as it is (−1). */
    move: (c: number, to: number, at?: number, face?: number) => number;
    /** Move the top `n` cards of `from` to `to`, one by one (the top first), face as given; returns
     *  the last card moved, or −1 if `from` ran out first. */
    draw(from: number, to: number, n?: number, face?: number): number;
    /** Deal `each` cards from `from` to each pile in `to`, round by round, face as given; returns the
     *  cards dealt (fewer if `from` ran out). */
    deal(from: number, to: ArrayLike<number>, each?: number, face?: number): number;
    /** Move every card of `from` onto `to` (keeping their order), face as given. */
    gather(from: number, to: number, face?: number): void;
    /** Turn card c over (or set it: 1 up, 0 down). */
    flip(c: number, face?: number): void;
    /** Shuffle pile p from `seed` (any 32-bit integer): the same seed, the same order, everywhere. */
    shuffle(p: number, seed: number): void;
};
```

## @fzlt/core/flick

Status: ALPHA. Size: 5410 B gzip (budget 5504 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/flick.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/flick"`

Light tabletop physics for diorama pieces. Discs and boxes slide on a table (and on ramps, and on each other), take a flick as an impulse, slow down with friction, bounce off each other and off fixed walls, fall off the table's edges and topple off stacks. It is a game's physics, not a rigid-body engine: - The table is the plane y = 0 inside `table` ([width, depth], centred on the origin): the frame of a diorama table's top centre, so a pose goes straight into an object that is `on` the table. Past an edge a piece falls to `floor` and is flagged `off`. - Pieces move in the plane: discs as circles, boxes as turned rectangles (they spin from off-centre hits), ramps and walls as fixed rectangles. Contacts are frictionless impulses with restitution (`bounce`); sliding friction is μ·g against what a piece rests on, so a piece resting on another is dragged along by it. - Falling and toppling: a piece whose centre of mass (with everything stacked on it) leaves what holds it tips about that edge, the pieces on it with it, then falls; a fast one flies off. It lands flat, on a side or on an end (the nearest quarter turn), never balanced on an edge. - Fixed step and deterministic: `step(dt)` runs `sub` sub-steps of arithmetic only (no Math.sin, Math.cos or Math.atan2 inside a step; steer's exact `hypot`), so two players who start from the same pieces and send the same shots (`sling`'s integer angle and power) see the same result bit for bit. Poses (`pose`, `apply`) are output only and never feed back. - `busy` is false once everything rests; `step` returns it for the engine's `busy()`. `run()` plays the shot to rest at once (reduced motion, a server, a replay check): the same steps. No allocation per step, pose or sling in the steady state (typed arrays, fixed capacity).

### FlickEvents (interface, ALPHA)

Something that takes events: an engine's ring (`engine.events`).

```ts
export interface FlickEvents {
    emit(type: string, a?: number, b?: number, x?: number, y?: number, v?: number): unknown;
}
```

### FlickOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `flick()`: capacity, the table, gravity and the step.

```ts
export interface FlickOptions {
    /** The most pieces, ramps and walls (default 32). */
    cap?: number;
    /** The table top, [width, depth] centred on the origin (default [10, 6]). */
    table?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Where a piece that falls off lands and rests (default −2). */
    floor?: number;
    /** Sliding friction μ on the floor (default 0.8: what falls off stops soon). */
    floorFriction?: number;
    /** Gravity, world units per s² (default 9.8). */
    gravity?: number;
    /** Sub-steps per `step(dt)` (default 4). */
    sub?: number;
    /** Faster than this (units per s) a piece flies off an edge instead of tipping over it (default 0.6). */
    tip?: number;
    /** The highest lip a sliding piece rides up onto a ramp (default 0.08). */
    lip?: number;
    /** Events: `flick:hit` (a, b, x, z, speed), `flick:topple` (a), `flick:fall` (a), `flick:rest`. */
    events?: FlickEvents;
}
```

### FlickBodyDef (interface, ALPHA)

One piece, ramp or wall for `add`.

```ts
export interface FlickBodyDef {
    /** `disc` (a puck, a coin), `box` (a block, a crate) or `ramp` (fixed, tall at its −x end like
     *  diorama's `wedge`; default `disc`). */
    shape?: "disc" | "box" | "ramp";
    /** [width (x), height (y), depth (z)]; a disc's width is its diameter (default [1, 0.3, 1]). */
    size?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** [x, z]: on the highest surface under it; [x, y, z]: from that height (it falls if above). */
    pos?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Turn about y, radians (diorama's `rot[1]`). */
    yaw?: number;
    /** Mass (default 1). */
    mass?: number;
    /** Sliding friction μ (default 0.25). */
    friction?: number;
    /** Restitution, 0..1, averaged with what it hits (default 0.8). */
    bounce?: number;
    /** Never moves (a wall, a rail, a post); ramps always are. */
    fixed?: boolean;
}
```

### flick (function, ALPHA)

A tabletop world: `add` pieces, `flick` one, `step` it from the engine, `apply` the poses.

Signature: `flick(o?: FlickOptions): Flick`
- o (optional): `FlickOptions`
- returns: `Flick`

```ts
export declare function flick(o?: FlickOptions): {
    /** Pieces added. */
    readonly n: number;
    /** Anything moving, falling or tipping (false: everything rests). */
    readonly busy: boolean;
    /** Bottom centre x, y, z (the table top's frame) and velocity, per piece. */
    x: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    y: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    z: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    vx: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    vy: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    vz: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Spin about y (rad/s), mass and inverse spin inertia (0: a disc, a fixed piece). */
    spin: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    mass: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    ii: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** `STATE` per piece; `off`: 1 once it fell off the table; `on`: what it rests on (−1 the
     *  table, −2 the floor, −3 nothing: in the air) or another piece's index. */
    state: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    off: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    on: Int32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** Add a piece, ramp or wall (`FlickBodyDef`); returns its index. Add what holds a piece first. */
    add(d?: FlickBodyDef): number;
    /** Put piece i at (x, z) upright and still: on the highest surface under it, or from height y. */
    place(i: number, x: number, z: number, y?: number): void | -3;
    /** Flick piece i with impulse (jx, jz) (velocity change: impulse ÷ mass). */
    flick(i: number, jx: number, jz: number): void;
    /** Advance dt seconds (`sub` fixed sub-steps); returns `busy`. Call it from the engine's step. */
    step(dt: number): boolean;
    /** Step at `dt` until everything rests or `max` steps pass; returns the steps taken. */
    run(dt?: number, max?: number): number;
    /** How far a piece sliding at `speed` on a flat goes before friction stops it: v² ÷ 2μg. */
    reach: (i: number, speed: number) => number;
    /** Piece i's pose for a diorama object: out = [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] (its bottom-centre origin and
     *  `rot`, through a topple too). */
    pose(i: number, out: {
        [k: number]: number;
    }): {
        [k: number]: number;
    };
    /** Write piece i's pose into a diorama object (`pos`, `rot`) resting on the table (or on a parent
     *  whose top is at height `y0` in the table's frame: −2 for a floor at `floor` −2, so its shadow
     *  falls on the floor). */
    apply(i: number, ob: {
        pos: {
            [k: number]: number;
        };
        rot: {
            [k: number]: number;
        };
    }, y0?: number): void;
};
```

What `flick` returns.

```ts
export type Flick = ReturnType<typeof flick>;
```

### sling (function, ALPHA)

A slingshot drag that turns a pointer into an aimed flick: press on a piece (`begin` with its centre and the pointer's point on the table, from diorama's `ground`), pull back (`move`), let go (`end`). The shot points from the pointer to the piece; `power` (0..1) is the pull over `pull`, the meter to draw. The shot is two integers, `angle` and `level`, so a game sends them as they are and the other player's `set(angle, level)` gives the same `jx`, `jz` bit for bit (no Math.sin).

Signature: `sling(o?: SlingOptions): Sling`
- o (optional): `SlingOptions`
- returns: `Sling`

```ts
export declare function sling(o?: SlingOptions): {
    /** A drag is on. */
    active: boolean;
    /** The piece's centre the drag pulls from. */
    ax: number;
    az: number;
    /** The shot: direction index (0..turns − 1, from +x toward +z) and power level (0..steps). */
    angle: number;
    level: number;
    /** level ÷ steps. */
    power: number;
    /** The unit direction and the impulse for `flick`. */
    dx: number;
    dz: number;
    jx: number;
    jz: number;
    /** Start a drag on the piece at (x, z), the pointer at (px, pz). */
    begin(x: number, z: number, px: number, pz: number): void;
    /** The pointer moved to (px, pz): the shot points from it to the piece. */
    move(px: number, pz: number): void;
    /** Set the shot from its two integers (a remote player's): the same impulse everywhere. */
    set(angle: number, level: number): void;
    /** Let go: true if it is a shot (power ≥ `min`); then `jx`, `jz`, `angle`, `level` hold it. */
    end(): boolean;
    /** Drop the drag without a shot. */
    cancel(): void;
};
```

### Sling (type, ALPHA)

What `sling` returns.

```ts
export type Sling = ReturnType<typeof sling>;
```

## @fzlt/core/actor

Status: ALPHA. Size: 908 B gzip (budget 1229 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/actor.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/actor"`

Units, bots, turrets and shots as data. One fixed-capacity table of typed arrays, one row per actor: alive, side, kind, tag bits, health (`hp` of `max`) and a body (`x`, `y`, heading `a`, velocity `vx`, `vy`, radius `r`). Nothing allocates after `actors()`: spawn takes a free row, kill marks it dead, and `sweep()` (once per step, after your loops) gives dead rows back. A game's own fields are its own typed arrays of length `cap`, indexed by row (cooldowns, orders, timers). Iterate the dense list, which keeps spawn order, so a seeded run replays: for (let k = 0; k < A.n; k++) { const i = A.list[k]!; if (!A.alive[i]) continue; ... } A row is reused once swept, so hold on to an actor across steps by its handle (`ref(i)`), not its row: `get(handle)` is -1 once that actor is gone, even if its row lives again. Share the body with @fzlt/core/steer by passing its arrays (`actors({ cap, x: m.x, y: m.y, a: m.a })`). With `events` (engine.events) it rings `actor:spawn`, `actor:hurt` and `actor:kill` (a: row, b: side, x, y: where, in whole pixels, v: damage, or health on spawn) for sound, effects and the HUD. Whole pixels because small integers never box: a double passed to the ring can cost a heap number.

### ActorOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `actors()`: capacity, sides, optional shared body arrays and the event ring.

```ts
export interface ActorOptions {
    /** Rows (fixed: the arrays never grow; spawn returns -1 when full). */
    cap: number;
    /** Sides counted by `count(side)` (default 8, at most 32: `nearest` takes them as bits). */
    sides?: number;
    /** Bring your own body arrays (length ≥ cap), e.g. a steer's, so both move the same numbers. */
    x?: Float64Array;
    y?: Float64Array;
    a?: Float64Array;
    /** engine.events: actor:spawn, actor:hurt, actor:kill. */
    events?: EventRing;
}
```

### actors (function, ALPHA)

A fixed-capacity actor table: typed-array rows with spawn, kill, hurt, heal, sweep, handles, side counts, tags and nearest.

Signature: `actors(o: ActorOptions): Actors`
- o: `ActorOptions`
- returns: `Actors`

```ts
export declare function actors(o: ActorOptions): {
    cap: number;
    x: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>;
    y: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>;
    a: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>;
    vx: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    vy: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    r: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    hp: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    max: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    alive: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    side: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    kind: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    tags: Uint32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    gen: Uint32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** The dense list: rows list[0..n), in spawn order (dead ones stay until `sweep()`). */
    list: Int32Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    readonly n: number;
    /** Actors alive right now. */
    readonly live: number;
    /** A new actor on `side` with `health` (its max too); its body is zeroed. -1 when full. */
    spawn(s: number, health: number, k?: number, t?: number): number;
    /** Dead now (alive = 0, out of `count`); its row comes back at `sweep()`. False if already dead. */
    kill: (i: number) => boolean;
    /** Take `damage`; true when that killed it. */
    hurt(i: number, damage: number): boolean;
    /** Back up by `amount`, never over max. */
    heal(i: number, amount: number): void;
    /** Give dead rows back (keeps the list's order). Once per step, after the loops that kill. */
    sweep(): void;
    /** Live actors on side s. */
    count(s: number): number;
    /** A handle that outlives the row: `get(ref(i))` is i while that actor lives, -1 after. */
    ref(i: number): number;
    get(h: number): number;
    /** Every bit of `bits` set? / set or clear them. */
    has(i: number, bits: number): boolean;
    tag(i: number, bits: number, on?: boolean): void;
    /** The nearest live actor to i (not i) within `range`, on a side in the `sides` bits (1 << side)
     *  and carrying every `need` tag bit; -1 if none. Ties go to the earlier spawn. */
    nearest(i: number, range?: number, sides?: number, need?: number): number;
    /** Everything dead and every row free (a new match). Handles from before stay stale. */
    clear: () => void;
};
```

### Actors (type, ALPHA)

The table `actors()` returns.

```ts
export type Actors = ReturnType<typeof actors>;
```

## @fzlt/core/aim

Status: ALPHA. Size: 691 B gzip (budget 1024 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/aim.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/aim"`

Where bots and turrets point and when they may fire. Bound once to body arrays (a @fzlt/core/actor's or a steer's `x`, `y`, heading `a`, velocity `vx`, `vy`) and, for line of sight, a @fzlt/core/grid board; then everything takes rows: - `lead(i, j, speed)`: where i must shoot a shot of `speed` px/s to meet j, moving at (vx, vy): the intercept of a straight shot and a straight mover, the earliest one ahead; - `cone(i, j, half, range)`: j inside i's heading ± `half` radians and within `range`; - `sees(i, j)`: no `mask` cell strictly between them on the board (Bresenham, symmetric), or the game's own `clear(i, j)`; - `pick(i, list, n, half, range)`: the nearest `foe` of i among list[0..n) in its cone and in sight (an actor table's `list` and `n` as they are). Results land in `out[0..3]` ([x, y, t, d]: aim point, seconds to impact or the off-heading angle, and distance), so no call returns a double: doubles returned or passed across a call V8 doesn't inline are boxed. Distances are @fzlt/core/steer's exact `hypot` (Math.hypot's bits, no heap number). DOM-free, stateless between calls, zero allocation.

### AimOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `aim()`: the body arrays, an optional board and sight mask, and who counts as a foe.

```ts
export interface AimOptions {
    x: Float64Array;
    y: Float64Array;
    /** Headings in radians (for `cone`); without them every cone is a circle. */
    a?: Float64Array;
    /** Velocities in px/s (for `lead`); without them targets stand still. */
    vx?: Float64Array;
    vy?: Float64Array;
    /** Line of sight on this board (world px; its `cell` size); without one everything is in sight. */
    board?: Board;
    /** Cell flags that block sight (default 1: grid's BLOCKED; BLOCKED | COVER lets cover block). */
    mask?: number;
    /** Your own line of sight, used instead of `board` (a game whose tiles have their own rule). */
    clear?(i: number, j: number): boolean;
    /** May i shoot at j? (default: any j but i). With actors: `(i, j) => A.side[j] !== A.side[i]`. */
    foe?(i: number, j: number): boolean;
}
```

### aim (function, ALPHA)

Aiming bound to body arrays: `lead`, `cone`, `sees` and `pick`, results in `out`, zero allocation.

Signature: `aim(o: AimOptions): Aim`
- o: `AimOptions`
- returns: `Aim`

```ts
export declare function aim(o: AimOptions): {
    out: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** out = [aim x, aim y, seconds to impact, distance to the aim point]. False when the shot can
     *  never catch j (out is then j where it stands, t = -1). */
    lead(i: number, j: number, speed: number): boolean;
    /** j within `range` px and inside i's heading ± `half` rad. out = [j's x, y, angle off heading
     *  (signed, -π..π: turn by it), distance]. */
    cone(i: number, j: number, half: number, range: number): boolean;
    sees: (i: number, j: number) => boolean;
    /** The nearest foe of i among rows list[0..n) inside its cone and range and in sight; -1 if none.
     *  Skip dead rows with `foe` (e.g. `A.alive[j] && …`). Sight is checked last, and only for a row
     *  closer than the best so far, so a long list costs a sight check per closer candidate, not per row. out is the pick's. */
    pick(i: number, list: Int32Array, n: number, half: number, range: number): number;
};
```

### Aim (type, ALPHA)

The aimer `aim()` returns.

```ts
export type Aim = ReturnType<typeof aim>;
```

## @fzlt/core/view-dom

Status: ALPHA. Size: 882 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/view-dom.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/view-dom"`

A @fzlt/core/actor table drawn as DOM nodes, one per row, pooled. A row's node is made the first time it shows (`make(i)`, default an empty `<i>`), put in `host` through the ledger, and kept for good: when the actor dies the node hides (`hidden`), and when the row lives again (a new actor) the same node comes back. So the page holds at most `cap` nodes, and `engine.destroy()` (Recall) takes every one away and leaves the host as it was. Each render it writes, change-only through the ledger: `transform` (the body's `x`, `y` times `scale`, to 0.01 px, centred on the node unless `center: false`, turned by the heading `a` unless `turn: false`), `--hp` (hp / max, to 0.01), and `data-side` / `data-kind` when a row shows. The look is the page's CSS (`[data-side="1"] { … }`, `width: calc(var(--hp) * 100%)`); give `hidden` the last word if a rule sets `display`. `paint(i, el)` runs after for a row's own change-only writes (through engine.ledger). A board that holds still writes nothing and calls no `busy()`, so an engine with `settle` sleeps. A death can `linger` (seconds, with `data-dead` set, for a CSS fade) and holds the engine awake that long; with reduced motion the node hides at once. The step only counts lingering deaths down: no DOM, no allocation. A moved row costs one transform string in render; a still one costs nothing.

### ViewOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `viewDom()`: node factory, scale, turn, centring, linger, motion and paint.

```ts
export interface ViewOptions {
    /** A node for row i, made once, the first time row i shows (default: an empty `<i>`). */
    make?(i: number): El;
    /** Pixels per world unit (default 1): a board whose units live in cells passes its tile size. */
    scale?: number;
    /** Turn by the heading `a` (default true). */
    turn?: boolean;
    /** Centre the node on (x, y) (default true: `translate(-50%, -50%)`). */
    center?: boolean;
    /** Seconds a dead actor's node stays, with `data-dead`, before it hides (default 0). */
    linger?: number;
    /** Animate deaths (default: yes, unless the visitor prefers reduced motion). */
    motion?: boolean;
    /** After the view's writes for a showing row, each render: the game's own (change-only) writes. */
    paint?(i: number, el: El): void;
}
```

### viewDom (function, ALPHA)

An actor table as pooled DOM nodes, written change-only through the ledger; settles when still, `destroy()` removes every node.

Signature: `viewDom(engine: Engine, A: Actors, host: El, o?: ViewOptions): ViewDom`
- engine: `Engine`
- A: `Actors`
- host: `El`
- o (optional): `ViewOptions`
- returns: `ViewDom`

```ts
export declare function viewDom(engine: Engine, A: Actors, host: El, o?: ViewOptions): {
    /** Row i's node (undefined until it first shows). */
    node: (i: number) => El | undefined;
    /** Stop drawing (the nodes stay until Recall: engine.destroy()). */
    remove: () => void;
};
```

### ViewDom (type, ALPHA)

The view `viewDom()` returns.

```ts
export type ViewDom = ReturnType<typeof viewDom>;
```

## @fzlt/core/announce

Status: BETA. Size: 612 B gzip (budget 614 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/announce.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/announce"`

Game events read out to screen readers through one polite live region, rate-limited. The game says what happened on the event ring (in its steps, as it already does for sound and effects); `words` turns an event into a sentence in render; the region speaks at most once per `gap` seconds. const a = announce(engine, { words: (e) => e.type === "score" ? `Score ${e.a}` : e.type === "over" ? "Game over" : null, }); a.say("lives", "2 lives left"); // or directly, from a HUD or a menu - One region per page, shared by every engine: `[data-fz-announce]`, role status, polite, atomic, visually hidden. Made on the first word, never before; destroy() removes it if this one made it. - Coalesced by key (an event's `type`): a newer sentence for the same key replaces the waiting one, so a score that ticks ten times a second is read once, as its latest value. Waiting sentences are read together, in the order their keys first came, joined with ". ". - The same sentence twice is read twice (a trailing no-break space alternates). - Nothing in step; in render it reads the ring only. One timer while something waits, none after. - Recall: destroy() (or the engine's) removes the system, the timer and the region it made.

### AnnounceOptions (interface, BETA)

Options for `announce()`: `words(event)` turns ring events into sentences, `gap` is the least time between writes, `doc` the document.

```ts
export interface AnnounceOptions {
    /** An event in words, or nothing (null, undefined, "" or false) to stay quiet. Runs in render. */
    words?: (e: FizEvent) => string | null | undefined | false | void;
    /** Seconds between two writes to the region (default 1). */
    gap?: number;
    /** The page (default: the engine root's document, else `document`). */
    doc?: Document;
}
```

### announce (function, BETA)

Game events read out to screen readers through one polite live region per page, coalesced by key and rate-limited; `destroy()` removes the region.

Signature: `announce(engine: Engine, o?: AnnounceOptions): Announcer`
- engine: `Engine`
- o (optional): `AnnounceOptions`
- returns: `Announcer`

```ts
export declare function announce(engine: Engine, o?: AnnounceOptions): {
    /** Queue a sentence under a key (coalesced with what waits under that key). */
    say: (key: string, text: string) => void;
    /** Read what waits now, ignoring the gap (a result screen that must not wait). */
    flush: () => void;
    /** Remove the system, the timer and the region this one made. */
    destroy: () => void;
};
```

### Announcer (type, BETA)

What `announce()` returns: `say`, `flush`, `destroy`.

```ts
export type Announcer = ReturnType<typeof announce>;
```

## @fzlt/core/scene

Status: ALPHA. Size: 8369 B gzip (budget 8704 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/scene.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/scene"`

An animation recipe as data. A scene is JSON: a **stage** (a fixed pixel grid fitted to the box, a background, a starfield, shake, the clock), a **cast** (sprites, rects, text and lines, drawn in order, each value a number, a track or a blink on the scene clock), the **cues** (one-shot fx moments: a pop word, a kick, a burst) and the **gags** (a running bit: an fx emitter held open over a window, following a track). One player runs them all, so a gallery entry ships its data, not its own code. Bricks: the kernel (fps cap, settle), @fzlt/core/fx (particles, words, shake), @fzlt/core/sprite (pixel art, baked once), @fzlt/core/timeline's easings, and @fzlt/core/slot (`scene(data)` is a slot mount). The contract: time moves in the step on numbers only (no DOM, no allocation); one canvas, added through the ledger, so `destroy()` gives the page back exactly; after `end` seconds it rests on the last frame and the engine settles (`busy(sec)` holds it awake until then); a tap plays it again. With reduced motion it draws the poster frame (no cues, no gags) and settles.

### Val (type, ALPHA)

A value on the scene clock `t` (seconds): - a number or a string (a colour): constant; - a track `[from, to, at, dur, ease?]`: `from` until `at`, then eased to `to` over `dur` seconds (an EASES name, default "linear"); `dur` 0 jumps once `t` is past `at`, and works on strings; - a blink `{ blink: [a, b], hz, on?: [from, to], then? }`: `a` before `from`; inside the window `b` on odd ticks of `hz` per second, `a` on even ones; `then` (default `a`) from `to` on.

```ts
export type Val = number | string | readonly [number | string, number | string, number, number, string?] | Blink;
```

### Blink (interface, ALPHA)

A blink: `blink[0]` outside its window, `blink[1]` on odd ticks of `hz` inside it, `then` after it (see Val).

```ts
export interface Blink {
    blink: readonly [number | string, number | string];
    hz: number;
    on?: readonly [number, number?];
    then?: number | string;
}
```

### SpriteItem (type, ALPHA)

A sprite from `art`: centre at (x, y), turned by `rot` radians, `scale` px per art pixel, a palette index.

```ts

    pal?: Val;
```


### Cue (type, ALPHA)

A cue, once, when `t` passes its time (in order; several may share a time): `[t, "word", word, x, y, colour, size]`, `[t, "kick", amount]` or `[t, "emit", kind, x, y, n, colour, colours, scale]` (@fzlt/core/fx's word, kick and emit).

A gag: every step while `from < t < to`, emit `n` of `kind` at (x + dx, y + dy); x and y may be tracks.

### SceneData (interface, ALPHA)

A scene as JSON: the stage, the art, the cast, the cues and the gags (format version 1).

```ts
export interface SceneData {
    /** Format version: 1. */
    v: 1;
    stage: {
        /** The grid in scene pixels, fitted to the box and centred. */
        w: number;
        h: number;
        /** Frame-rate cap (default 30). */
        fps?: number;

        delay?: number;
        /** Starfield: `[count, colour, share of the height]`, seeded from the engine. */

        shake?: number;

        poster?: number;
    };
    /** @fzlt/core/fx options, and its particle kinds by name (a Kind, or a name in fx's KINDS). */
    fx?: {
        cap?: number;
        gravity?: number;
        scorch?: number;
        colors?: string[];
        words?: string[];
        kinds?: Record<string, Kind | keyof typeof KINDS>;
    };
    /** Pixel art by name: rows of characters (@fzlt/core/sprite), coloured by `ink` and `palettes`. */
    art?: Record<string, string[]>;
    ink?: Record<string, string>;
    palettes?: Record<string, string>[];
    /** Drawn in order, under the effects; shaken with them. */
    cast?: Item[];
    /** Drawn last, above the effects, never shaken (captions). */
    over?: Item[];
    cue?: Cue[];
    gag?: Gag[];
}
```

## @fzlt/core/terrain

Status: ALPHA. Size: 5566 B gzip (budget 5568 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/terrain.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/terrain"`

A heightfield for diorama scenes. A grid of vertex heights in world units (y up, x and z the floor plane, like diorama), filled from data, a seeded noise generator (hills, or ridged dunes stretched across a wind) and stamps (`bump`, `ramp`, `whoops`, `berm`, a flat `ribbon` for the track), then queried for physics and drawn into a `@fzlt/core/diorama` scene. - Each cell is two triangles split along the same diagonal the drawing uses, so `height(x, z)` is exactly the surface on screen and `normal(x, z, out)` its face's normal; `sample` gives both. `split: "adaptive"` picks each cell's diagonal along its smaller height difference (sharp crests without stair-steps); the default keeps one fixed diagonal. - Generation is pure: integer hashing for the noise and only + − × ÷ and square roots (no sine, no cosine), so the same seed and stamps give the same heights, bit for bit, in every browser; both players of an online race drive the same course. - `terrainView(d, t, opts)` draws it as flat-shaded faces in diorama's painter's sort: a colour per height band, a steep band, painted kinds (the track); chunks, each culled off screen and drawn at a coarser cell further from the camera (`lod`), its edges stitched to the neighbour so no crack opens; blob shadows that lie on the slope. Nothing to call per frame: `d.draw()` runs it. No allocation per query or per draw (typed arrays; shades made once as strings). Lengths use steer's exact `hypot` (the builtin boxes its arguments).

### TerrainOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `terrain()`: the grid and its first heights.

```ts
export interface TerrainOptions {
    /** Cells along x (vertices: cols + 1). */
    cols: number;
    /** Cells along z (vertices: rows + 1). */
    rows: number;
    /** A cell's side in world units (default 1). */
    cell?: number;
    /** World x of the first vertex (default: the grid centred on 0). */
    x0?: number;
    /** World z of the first vertex (default: centred). */
    z0?: number;
    /** Vertex heights, row by row along x ((cols + 1) × (rows + 1)); default all `base`. */
    heights?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** The starting height (default 0). */
    base?: number;
    /** How each cell splits into two triangles: "fixed" (default) along (i, j)–(i + 1, j + 1) in every
     *  cell; "adaptive" along the diagonal with the smaller height difference (it follows a crest or a
     *  gully, so a sharp ridge reads as a straight fold, not stair-steps). The queries use the same split. */
    split?: "fixed" | "adaptive";
}
```

### NoiseOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `noise()`: seeded value noise in octaves, added to the heights.

```ts
export interface NoiseOptions {
    /** The seed (an integer; the same seed, the same hills). */
    seed: number;
    /** Height of the tallest hill (default 1): the noise adds 0..amp. */
    amp?: number;
    /** World units between noise lattice points of the first octave (default 8). */
    scale?: number;
    /** Octaves (default 3), each half the size and `gain` the height of the last. */
    octaves?: number;
    /** Each octave's height over the last (default 0.5). */
    gain?: number;
    /** 0..1: sharp crests (dunes) instead of round hills (default 0). */
    ridge?: number;
    /** The wind's direction [x, z] (default [1, 0]): crests run across it. */
    wind?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** How much longer the features are across the wind than along it (default 1; dunes ~3). */
    stretch?: number;
}
```

### StampOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options shared by the line stamps: width and a soft edge.

```ts
export interface StampOptions {
    /** Full height across this width (default 2). */
    width?: number;
    /** Height of the stamp (default 1; negative digs). */
    height?: number;
    /** Fade out over this much past the width on each side (default 1). */
    edge?: number;
}
```

### Terrain (type, ALPHA)

A heightfield: heights, the queries and the stamps.

```ts
export type Terrain = ReturnType<typeof terrain>;
```

### terrain (function, ALPHA)

A heightfield of `cols` × `rows` cells: `h` holds the vertex heights; stamp it, query it, draw it.

Signature: `terrain(o: TerrainOptions): Terrain`
- o: `TerrainOptions`
- returns: `Terrain`

```ts
export declare function terrain(o: TerrainOptions): {
    /** Cells along x. */
    cols: number;
    /** Cells along z. */
    rows: number;
    /** A cell's side, world units. */
    cell: number;
    /** World x of vertex column 0 (`terrainWindow` moves it). */
    x0: number;
    /** World z of vertex row 0 (`terrainWindow` moves it). */
    z0: number;
    /** Vertex heights, (cols + 1) per row; write them freely, then bump `version`. */
    h: Float64Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** A painted kind per triangle (0: none), two per cell (the one with corner (i + 1, j) first; in an
     *  adaptive cell split along 10–01, the one with (i + 1, j + 1) first):
     *  `ribbon` paints the track; `terrainView` colours it; `sample` returns it. */
    kind: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
    /** The cells' split ("fixed" or "adaptive"): `terrainView` draws the same one by default. */
    split: string;
    /** Bumped by every stamp: a view re-reads its bounds when it changes. */
    version: number;
    /** The surface height under (x, z) (the drawn triangle's; outside the grid, its edge). */
    height: (x: number, z: number) => number;
    /** The face's unit normal under (x, z): out = [nx, ny, nz]; returns out. */
    normal<O extends {
        [i: number]: number;
    }>(x: number, z: number, out: O): O;
    /** Height and normal at once (what a wheel needs): out = [h, nx, ny, nz]; returns the face's kind. */
    sample(x: number, z: number, out: {
        [i: number]: number;
    }): number;
    /** The kind painted on the face under (x, z) (0: none). */
    kindAt: (x: number, z: number) => number;
    /** Vertex height at column i, row j. */
    at: (i: number, j: number) => number;
    /** Set every vertex: h = fn(x, z, h). */
    shape: (fn: (x: number, z: number, h: number) => number) => /*elided*/ any;
    /** Add seeded value noise (`NoiseOptions`): round hills, or ridged dunes with `ridge`, `wind`, `stretch`. */
    noise(n: NoiseOptions): /*elided*/ any;
    /** A round bump (or a dip, height < 0) of radius r at (x, z): smooth to its rim. */
    bump(x: number, z: number, r: number, height: number): /*elided*/ any;
    /** A jump ramp from `from` [x, z] rising to `height` at `to`, then falling back to the ground over
     *  `back` (default one cell: a sharp lip that throws a vehicle into the air). */
    ramp(from: ArrayLike<number>, to: ArrayLike<number>, so?: StampOptions & {
        back?: number;
    }): /*elided*/ any;
    /** `count` rolling humps (whoops) from `from` to `to`. */
    whoops(from: ArrayLike<number>, to: ArrayLike<number>, so?: StampOptions & {
        count?: number;
    }): /*elided*/ any;
    /** A banked turn along `points` [x0, z0, x1, z1, …]: a bowl across its width, rising toward
     *  `side` (1, the default: the right of the direction of travel, the outside of a left turn; −1
     *  the left). Past each end the bank keeps its cross-section and runs out to the ground over
     *  `edge` (no lump on the centre line beyond the ends). */
    berm(points: ArrayLike<number>, so?: StampOptions & {
        side?: number;
    }): /*elided*/ any;
    /** Carve a flat track along `points`: its cross-section level (at the height the ground had under
     *  each point, or `y`), blended into the ground over `edge`; paints `kind` on the faces whose centre is inside its width. */
    ribbon(points: ArrayLike<number>, so?: {
        width?: number;
        edge?: number;
        y?: number;
        kind?: number;
    }): /*elided*/ any;
};
```

### TerrainWindowOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `terrainWindow()`: the window's grid, how far it slides, and the ground it shows.

```ts
export interface TerrainWindowOptions {
    /** Cells along x (vertices: cols + 1). */
    cols: number;
    /** Cells along z (default `cols`). */
    rows?: number;
    /** A cell's side in world units (default 1). */
    cell?: number;
    /** Cells per slide (default 8): `follow` moves the window in whole steps. */
    step?: number;
    /** The cells' split, as `terrain()`'s (the queries and `terrainView` use it). */
    split?: "fixed" | "adaptive";
    /** Write the ground into the window: heights `t.h[j * (t.cols + 1) + i]` for every vertex i0..i1,
     *  j0..j1 (window indices, inclusive), and kinds (0: none) for every cell inside that range, if the
     *  game paints any. Vertex (i, j) is at lattice point (t.origin[0] + i, t.origin[1] + j), world
     *  ((t.origin[0] + i) × cell, (t.origin[1] + j) × cell). It must be a pure function of the place: a
     *  range can repeat one vertex row or column the window already holds. Only integers cross this call. */
    fill(i0: number, j0: number, i1: number, j1: number, t: TerrainWindow): void;
}
```

### TerrainWindow (type, ALPHA)

A terrain whose origin follows a point: what `terrainWindow` returns.

```ts
export type TerrainWindow = Terrain & {
    /** The first vertex on the world lattice [i, j] (x0 = i × cell, z0 = j × cell). */
    origin: Int32Array;
    /** Moves so far (the first fill included); vertices `fill` was asked for so far. */
    stats: {
        slides: number;
        filled: number;
    };
    /** Put the first vertex at lattice point (i, j): keep the overlap, fill the rest. True if it moved. */
    moveTo(i: number, j: number): boolean;
    /** Keep (x, z) in the middle step: slide by whole steps when it leaves it. True if it slid. */
    follow(x: number, z: number): boolean;
};
```

### terrainWindow (function, ALPHA)

An endless ground: a `terrain` of cols × rows cells that slides over the world lattice and asks `fill` only for the rows and columns it gains. The same queries (the same face rule) and the same `terrainView`; `version` bumps once per slide. The window decides no height (they come from `fill`), so where it sits is not game state. Nothing is filled until the first `follow` or `moveTo`.

Signature: `terrainWindow(o: TerrainWindowOptions): TerrainWindow`
- o: `TerrainWindowOptions`
- returns: `TerrainWindow`

```ts
export declare function terrainWindow(o: TerrainWindowOptions): TerrainWindow;
```

### TerrainViewOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `terrainView`: colours, light, chunks and level of detail, how it sorts, shadows.

```ts
export interface TerrainViewOptions {
    /** Colour by height: [[top, "#rrggbb"], …] low to high; a face takes the first band its mean
     *  height is under (the last above all). Default one sand colour. */
    bands?: ArrayLike<readonly [number, string]>;
    /** Faces steeper than this (1 − normal y, 0..1) take `steepColor` (default 0.35; 1: never). */
    steep?: number;
    /** The steep faces' colour (default: the first band's, darker). */
    steepColor?: string;
    /** Colours of painted kinds: kinds[0] is kind 1 (the ribbon's track). */
    kinds?: ArrayLike<string>;
    /** Towards the light (default diorama's [0.5, 1, 0.4]). */
    light?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Ambient light, 0..1 (default 0.56). */
    ambient?: number;
    /** Cells per chunk side, a power of two (default 8): the unit of culling and detail. */
    chunk?: number;
    /** Camera distances past which a chunk's drawn cell doubles: [30, 60] draws 1×, 2×, then 4×. */
    lod?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** "ground" (default): every face before every object (a cluster fixed at `fixed`), exact among
     *  themselves; "depth": a cluster per chunk ranked by its far edge, so hills hide what is behind. */
    sort?: "ground" | "depth";
    /** The cluster name (default "terrain"; depth mode adds ":<chunk>"). */
    cluster?: string;
    /** Ground mode: its fixed rank (default 0). */
    fixed?: number;
    /** Its layer (default 0). */
    layer?: number;
    /** The cells' split as drawn (default the terrain's `split`); "adaptive" picks each drawn cell's
     *  diagonal along its smaller height difference, at every level of detail. */
    split?: "fixed" | "adaptive";
    /** Stroke each face in its own colour to close anti-aliasing seams (default true). */
    seams?: boolean;
    /** Blob shadows on the slope, set with `shadow(i, …)` (default 8). */
    shadows?: number;
    /** Shadow colour (default `#000000`). */
    shadowColor?: string;
    /** Faces fade into `color` with their distance in the floor plane from the camera's target (the
     *  player, under a chase camera): untouched before `from`, all `color` past `to` (16 steps between).
     *  Shadows are not hazed. */
    haze?: {
        from: number;
        to: number;
        color: string;
    };
}
```

### terrainView (function, ALPHA)

Draw terrain `t` into diorama `d` as flat-shaded faces, painted inside `d.draw()` (decals in the sort): nothing to call per frame. Faces with a vertex behind the camera are dropped.

Signature: `terrainView(d: Diorama, t: Terrain, o?: TerrainViewOptions): TerrainView`

```ts
export declare function terrainView(d: Diorama, t: Terrain, o?: TerrainViewOptions): {
    /** The last draw: faces painted, chunks on screen. */
    stats: {
        faces: number;
        chunks: number;
    };
    /** Chunks along x and z. */
    chunks: readonly [number, number];
    /** Chunk strides from the last draw (1: every cell; 2: every other…). */
```

## @fzlt/core/drive

Status: ALPHA. Size: 5262 B gzip (budget 5312 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/drive.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/drive"`

Vehicle feel on a heightfield, for diorama racing and trail games. One small, fixed-step model for two wheels (a dirt bike) and four (a Jeep, a truck, a buggy, a car): throttle, brake (and reverse), steering that tightens less at speed, grip and drift (the tyres hold a sideways slide only up to `grip`, a handbrake input lets the rear go), a spring and damper per wheel so the body pitches, rolls, squats and dives with the ground under each wheel, airtime off a lip, and a landing that is judged: a bike that lands nose or tail too far off the slope, or a car that rolls past `crashRoll`, crashes. - The ground is anything with `sample(x, z, out)` (out = [height, nx, ny, nz], returns a surface kind): `@fzlt/core/terrain` is one, and its painted kinds can change the grip (`surfaces`). - Deterministic: the same inputs from the same start give the same path, bit for bit. The model uses only + − × ÷, square roots and its own polynomial sine and arctangent (the builtins may differ in the last bit between browsers), so two players replaying the same inputs agree. - Suspension: each wheel samples the ground on its own and has its own spring (`stiffness` or `hz`, `progressive`), damper (`damping` compressing, `rebound` extending), `travel` and a `bump` stop; the body heaves, pitches and rolls on the sum of the spring loads with its own `inertia`, so a big drop compresses the springs, rebounds and settles (a long-travel buggy: `travel` 0.5 or more, soft and progressive, more rebound than compression damping). - Outputs for drawing: `pos` and `rot` (diorama's order: [roll, yaw, pitch]) for the body, per wheel `comp` (how far its spring is pushed in) and `press` (the same, 0..1 of the travel), `spin` (radians) and `contact`, `bodyPitch` and `bodyRoll` (the lean on the springs), `stroke` (the most any spring is in: 1 is the bump stop), the front wheels' `steerAngle`, and `dust` (0..1: how hard the tyres throw dirt, spray or sand) for an emitter. - Drift: the handbrake input lets the rear go (the grip drops to `drift`, the tail swings out by `swing`, the slide is held under `slide` radians and counter-steer catches it; letting go hands `recover` of the sideways speed back as forward speed). `drift` (0..1) says how hard it is drifting right now, `slide` the body's angle to its travel, `chain` the drift score so far (∫ drift dt); a chain that ends banks as `drive:drift` (v: its score; b: 1 when a crash or a spin-out broke it). `spinOut(rate, secs)` spins it round with no control for a moment. - Contact between vehicles: `touch(a, b, opts)` (or `touchAll(list, opts)`, every pair in order) pushes two hulls apart (a box from `hull` [half length, half width], or a circle: one radius) by their `mass` and bounces their velocities along the contact normal; `onHit(a, b, hit)` gets the impulse in `hit` (`touchHit`: [impulse, nx, nz, depth, x, z], the normal from a to b), so a game can spin out a drifting car it rams. - `chase(cam, target, opts, dt)` eases a diorama camera behind and above anything with `pos` and `yaw` (cosmetic: it uses the builtin maths; pass `snap` for reduced motion). - Rollback: `state` is every byte the model carries from step to step (one buffer); `save(dst)` and `load(src)` copy it out and back, so a game can rewind and replay a car bit for bit. Zero allocation per step, also with several vehicles in one process (typed arrays; locals; one class for every vehicle, its model in module functions, so a loop over cars keeps one call target). Speeds are world units per second, angles radians.

```ts
    sample(x: number, z: number, out: {
```

### DriveOptions (interface, ALPHA)

Options for `drive()`: the vehicle's shape, its feel and its limits. Defaults by `kind`.

```ts
export interface DriveOptions {
    /** "car" (four wheels, default) or "bike" (two in line, leans into turns, rear-wheel drive). */
    kind?: "car" | "bike";
    /** Wheel offsets from the body's centre, [forward, right, …] (car: ±0.75 × ±0.5; bike: ±0.6 × 0). */
    wheels?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Wheel radius (car 0.28, bike 0.32). */
    radius?: number;
    /** Spring length at full stretch, from the body's origin to the wheel centre (car 0.3, bike 0.35). */
    rest?: number;
    /** Spring travel before the bump stop (car 0.24, bike 0.3; a long-travel buggy or trophy truck 0.5 or more). */
    travel?: number;
    /** Bounce frequency of the springs, Hz (default 2.2). */
    hz?: number;
    /** The spring rate instead of `hz`: the whole vehicle's, per unit mass, 1/s² (the sag is gravity / stiffness;
     *  default (2π · 2.2)² ≈ 191). */
    stiffness?: number;
    /** Progressive springs: the rate grows by this share times (compression / travel)² (default 0: linear; 1 is
     *  twice as stiff at full travel, soft over small bumps and firm on a big landing). */
    progressive?: number;
    /** Damping ratio of the springs while they compress (default 0.75). */
    damping?: number;
    /** Damping ratio while they extend (default `damping`): more holds the body down after a landing instead of a bounce. */
    rebound?: number;
    /** The bump stop past `travel`: its rate as a multiple of the spring's (default 10). */
    bump?: number;
    /** Body inertia for pitch and roll, a multiple of the springs' match (same bounce as heave): one number, or
     *  [pitch, roll] (default 1; more pitches and rolls slower and further). */
    inertia?: number | ArrayLike<number>;
    /** How fast a wheel off the ground drops to full droop, units / s (default Infinity: at once; drawing only). */
    droop?: number;
    /** Gravity, units / s² (default 20). */
    gravity?: number;
    /** Acceleration at full throttle from a standstill (car 10, bike 12). */
    accel?: number;
    /** Top speed on the flat (car 16, bike 18): throttle's pull fades to 0 there. */
    top?: number;
    /** Braking deceleration (default 22). */
    brake?: number;
    /** Top speed backwards (brake held at a stop; default 5). */
    reverse?: number;
    /** Rolling drag with no pedal, units / s² (default 2.5). */
    coast?: number;
    /** Sideways grip, in g (car 1, bike 1.15): the most sideways acceleration the tyres hold. */
    grip?: number;
    /** Rear grip left at the full handbrake / drift input (default 0.4). */
    drift?: number;
    /** How far the tail swings out on the handbrake: the turn tightens by 1 + swing (default 1). */
    swing?: number;
    /** Most slide angle (body to travel) a drift holds before the swing stops, radians (default 0.8). */
    slide?: number;
    /** Share of the sideways speed the tyres hand back as forward speed coming out of a drift (default 0.35). */
    recover?: number;
    /** For `touch`: mass (car 1, bike 0.5). */
    mass?: number;
    /** For `touch`: the hull, [half length, half width] (a box; default the wheels plus their radius), or one radius (a circle). */
    hull?: number | ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Most steering, as a wheel angle (car 0.6, bike 0.7). */
    steer?: number;
    /** Speed at which steering is down to half (default 12). */
    steerFall?: number;
    /** Centre of mass height over the springs: squat, dive and body roll (car 0.35, bike 0.3). */
    cg?: number;
    /** Bike: most lean into a turn (default 0.9). */
    lean?: number;
    /** Pitch control in the air, rad / s² at full throttle (nose up) or brake (nose down) (car 2, bike 6). */
    airPitch?: number;
    /** A landing (or a moment on the ground) this far off the slope's pitch crashes (car 1, bike 0.65). */
    crashPitch?: number;
    /** Off the slope's roll by this much crashes: a rollover (car 1.1; bikes do not check). */
    crashRoll?: number;
    /** Landing faster than this downward crashes (default 30). */
    crashDrop?: number;
    /** Grip multiplier per ground kind: surfaces[k] for kind k (default 1). */
    surfaces?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Steps per `step()` (default 2: the springs stay stable at 60 Hz). */
    substeps?: number;
    /** An event ring: `drive:air`, `drive:land` (v: how far off the slope), `drive:crash`, `drive:drift`
     *  (v: the chain's score; b: 1 when broken), with `id` as a. */
    events?: DriveEvents;
    /** The id events carry (default 0). */
    id?: number;
}
```

## @fzlt/core/math

Status: BETA. Size: 1746 B gzip (budget 1792 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/math.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/math"`

Trig that gives the same bits on every engine, for anything that steps a sim. `sin`, `cos`, `atan`, `atan2` and `hypot` from + − × ÷, `Math.sqrt`, `Math.abs`, `Math.trunc` and `%` (all exact, so the same everywhere) and bit reads only. The builtins may differ between engines in the last bit (WebKit calls the system's libm), and one bit in a heading is a different game online: a desync. These are fdlibm 5.3's algorithms (k_sin.c, k_cos.c, s_sin.c, s_cos.c, the medium path of e_rem_pio2.c, s_atan.c, e_atan2.c), the ones V8 ports for its Math.sin, cos, atan and atan2: in Node they return what the builtins return, bit for bit (tests/math.test.mjs), so a sim tested headless keeps its numbers; in Chromium and WebKit they return the same bits as in Node (tests/math-engines.mjs), while those browsers' own builtins differ from them (measured on Chromium 153 and WebKit 26: about 3% of sin and cos results and 18% of atan2's). `hypot` is V8's two-argument Math.hypot, written out (moved here from `@fzlt/core/steer`, which re-exports it). One limit: past |x| = 2^20·π/2 (about 1.6 million radians) fdlibm's exact reduction needs a big table; here such an x is first taken mod 2π (`%` is exact), so every engine still agrees, but V8's builtin may differ there. No game needs an angle that large. Rendering may keep the builtins (a pixel off is fine). Allocation-free wherever they are called from: a double returned from a call the JIT does not inline is boxed (a heap number each call), and so are its double arguments, and fdlibm's bodies are past V8's inlining limit: so the bodies take their arguments from one shared buffer and leave their result in another, and each export is a tiny wrapper (write, call, read) that always inlines. Shared buffers for the bit reads and the reduced argument too; every export tree-shakes on its own.

### sin (const, BETA)

sin(x), the same bits on every engine (Math.sin's on V8).

- returns: `number`


### hypot (const, BETA)

Math.hypot of two numbers, without the builtin call: V8 boxes Math.hypot's arguments, a heap number per call in a hot loop. Same steps as V8's own (Infinity wins over NaN, scale by the larger, sum, sqrt), so it returns the same bits (tested against Math.hypot).

Signature: `hypot(dx: number, dy: number): number`
- dx: `number`
- dy: `number`
- returns: `number`

```ts
export declare const hypot: (dx: number, dy: number) => number;
```

## @fzlt/core/arcade

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 24145 B gzip (budget 24156 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/arcade.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/arcade"`

The shell every page arcade game repeats, so a game is only its rules and its art. One engine per run over the host page (`@fzlt/core/board-page`: its words are terrain, its buttons are targets), a fixed overlay with a canvas and a scoreboard in the Board UI kit (title, sound, pause, fold and exit keys, readouts, an optional meter, action keys, a comms toast), keys and pointer (`@fzlt/core/input`), the touch pad on coarse pointers (`@fzlt/core/pad`), sound from the event ring (`@fzlt/core/sound`), sparks and stacking score popups, factory health painted into the buttons, and a controller a hub drives: start, pause, resume, stop, destroy, getSnapshot. While a run is live, a click on the page fires instead of following a link; the scoreboard, fields and `[data-virus-ignore]` / `[data-fizlet-ignore]` keep their clicks. Recall (Escape, the exit key, stop) destroys the engine, so every letter and button comes back exactly; a run that ends keeps the scoreboard with the result until Recall. The game supplies `create(ctx)`: its own systems on `ctx.engine`, reading `ctx.ctl` (written in the read phase) and drawing in render. The scoreboard and controls are a HUD preset, chosen per game with `hud` (BOARD-UI.md §19): `arcadeHud()` is today's card and the default (no `hud` renders it byte for byte); `skirmishHud({...})` is Battlefield Blitz's top bar with a clock, rank and armor bar, a feed, a banner, aim toggles and counted keys, and its flow (countdown, pause / surrender, result) on `@fzlt/core/match`: then match owns the phase, the shell asks it to pause, resume or end and follows it (`HudView.ask`, `HudRun.go`). Each preset is its own export, so a game ships only the one it names.

### skirmishHud (function, COMPLETE)

The `skirmish` preset (Battlefield Blitz): `hud: skirmishHud({ readouts: [{ label: "Kills", tone: "team" }, { label: "Time", kind: "clock" }, { label: "Armor", kind: "bar", low: 0.3 }] })`. `hud(out)` fills the readouts in order, then any count slots.

- returns: `ArcadeHud`

### SkirmishOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for the `skirmish` HUD preset: its readouts, header and nav keys, feed, banner, overlays, result, aim toggles and key counts.

```ts
export interface SkirmishOptions {
    /** Readouts, in the order `hud(out)` fills them. */
    readouts: SkirmishReadout[];
    /** Header keys, in order (default full screen, sound, pause, exit; `fold` hides the title and the
     *  text keys). Full screen shows only where the page may use it. */
    header?: ("fullscreen" | "sound" | "pause" | "fold" | "exit")[];
    /** Text keys after the actions, as on the card (default none): `next` (Next gate, G), `restart`,
     *  `auto` (Auto fire: needs `fire`). */
    nav?: ("next" | "restart" | "auto")[];
    /** A feed of the last `rows` (default 4) events of type `on`, newest first. */
    feed?: {
        rows?: number;
        on: string;
        line: (a: number, b: number) => string;
    };
    /** A centred banner (title, sub) on each event of type `on`. */
    banner?: {
        on: string;
        text: (a: number, b: number) => readonly [string, string?];
    };
    /** Overlays (default all four; @fzlt/core/match runs the flow either way). `countdown` holds the start
     *  for 3, 2, 1 on the flow's clock; without `pause` or `result` that phase shows no overlay; without
     *  `surrender` the pause card has no SURRENDER key. */
    overlays?: ("pause" | "surrender" | "countdown" | "result")[];
    /** The result card: `stats()` keys to list, and the one whose best is kept on this device. */
    result?: {
        stats: string[];
        best?: string;
    };
    /** Aim toggles: the intents `aim-auto` and `aim-lock` (`ctx.input.down("aim-lock")`). */
    aim?: ("auto" | "lock")[];
    /** Counted keys: action id → the `hud(out)` slot of its count, a badge on its keys. */
    counts?: Record<string, number>;
}
```


### MODE, PX, PY, PON, KX, KY, FIRE, VW, VH, CALM, TARGET_HP (const, COMPLETE)

Controls and view, written once per frame in the read phase (a step reads them): mode (0 keys or stick, 1 pointer), pointer x, y and on, move x, y (-1..1), fire, viewport width and height, and reduced motion (1/0). The game writes TARGET_HP: the full health of a target, for its paint.

```ts
export declare const MODE = 0, PX = 1, PY = 2, PON = 3, KX = 4, KY = 5, FIRE = 6, VW = 7, VH = 8, CALM = 9, TARGET_HP = 10;
```

### ArcadeAction (interface, COMPLETE)

One action key: the intent it drives, its keyboard code and its scoreboard text.

```ts
export interface ArcadeAction {
    /** The controls intent: `ctx.input.hit(id)` in a step. */
    id: string;
    /** KeyboardEvent.code, e.g. "KeyB". */
    key: string;
    /** Scoreboard key text, e.g. "B · Cover". */
    label: string;
}
```

### ArcadeStatus (type, COMPLETE)

Where a run is: idle, running, paused, won, game over or destroyed.

```ts
export type ArcadeStatus = "idle" | "running" | "paused" | "won" | "gameover" | "destroyed";
```

### ArcadeOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `arcade()`: the board and its selectors, theme, seed, reduced motion, sound and controls, and the `onState` / `onEvent` / `onError` hooks.

```ts
export interface ArcadeOptions<S> {
    /** The board: a selector or an element (default document.body). */
    root?: string | Element;
    textSelector?: string;
    targetSelector?: string;
    excludeSelector?: string;
    /** "system" (default) follows the visitor's colour scheme. */
    theme?: "dark" | "light" | "system";
    seed?: number;
    reducedMotion?: boolean;
    /** Start with sound on (default true; it waits for a gesture to unlock). */
    sound?: boolean;
    /** "keyboard": the mouse never steers. */
    controls?: "mouse" | "keyboard";
    onState?: (state: ArcadeSnapshot<S>) => void;
    onEvent?: (event: {
        type: string;
        game: string;
        [key: string]: unknown;
    }) => void;
    onError?: (error: unknown) => void;
}
```

### ArcadeSnapshot (type, COMPLETE)

What the controller reports about a run: its status, time and frame cost, plus the game's own state.

```ts
export type ArcadeSnapshot<S> = Partial<S> & {
    id: string;
    status: ArcadeStatus;
    elapsed: number;
    frameMs: number;
    maxFrameMs: number;
    notice: string;
    /** Letters indexed, on screen and spent, and the range reads the last measurement made. */
    board?: {
        indexed: number;
        visible: number;
        spent: number;
        measurements: number;
    };
    /** Sparks alive (at most 100). */
    particles?: number;
};
```

### ArcadeController (interface, COMPLETE)

The controller `arcade()` returns: start, pause, resume, stop and destroy a run, and read its snapshot.

```ts
export interface ArcadeController<S> {
    start(): ArcadeSnapshot<S>;
    pause(): void;
    resume(): void;
    stop(): void;
    destroy(): void;
    getSnapshot(): ArcadeSnapshot<S>;
}
```

### ArcadeContext (interface, COMPLETE)

What `create` gets: the run's engine and board, the controls, and the shell's presentation.

```ts
export interface ArcadeContext {
    engine: Engine;
    board: BoardPage;
    input: Controls;
    /** MODE … TARGET_HP (see the constants). */
    ctl: Float64Array;
    reduced(): boolean;
    /** A popup at (x, y): `+value` when `text` is null (stacked with nearby ones), else the text.
     *  Tone 0 score, 1 accent (upgrade), 2 hurt. Call it from render (react). */
    popup(x: number, y: number, value: number, text: string | null, tone?: 0 | 1 | 2): void;
    /** n sparks from (x, y) in colour `c` (an index into `colors`); none under reduced motion. */
    spark(x: number, y: number, n: number, c: number): void;
    /** A line in the comms toast. */
    say(text: string, ms?: number): void;
    /** onEvent for the hub (a plain object: call it from render, not a step). */
    emit(type: string, data?: Record<string, unknown>): void;
    /** In-page art: a shadow root in an overlay inside `el` (an absolutely positioned host that
     *  follows the page's layout, scrolling and transforms natively). A static `el` becomes
     *  relative. Through the ledger: Recall removes it and puts the style back. Call from create
     *  or reset (it reads computed style), never from a step. Null for replaced elements. */
    attach(el: Element): ShadowRoot | null;
}
```

### ArcadeGame (interface, COMPLETE)

One run of your game, as the shell drives it: reset, draw, the HUD and meter, page scroll, reactions to events, stats, and whether the run is over.

```ts
export interface ArcadeGame<S> {
    /** A fresh run (the viewport is in ctl[VW], ctl[VH]). */
    reset(): void;
    /** 0 playing, 1 lost, 2 won: read every render; the run ends the frame it turns non-zero. */
    over(): number;
    /** The page scrolled by (dx, dy): move page-space things (read phase). */
    scroll?(dx: number, dy: number): void;
    /** Each event on the ring this frame (render): popups, sparks, the toast, onEvent. */
    react?(ev: FizEvent): void;
    /** Draw on the canvas (render), after the target beacons, before sparks and popups. */
    draw(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, dt: number): void;
    /** The readout values, in `readouts` order, then the meter's change key (render, change-only). */
    hud(out: Float64Array): void;
    /** The meter's left text, right text and fill 0..1, when its change key moved. */
    meter?(): readonly [string, string, number];
    /** The snapshot's game fields (not a hot path). */
    stats(): S;
}
```

### ArcadeDef (interface, COMPLETE)

Your game for `arcade()`: its id, title, accent, hint, CSS, actions, readouts, sound cues and `create()`, which makes a run.

```ts
export interface ArcadeDef<S> {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    /** The game's accent (hex): title, meter, popups, target paint at full health. */
    color: string;
    hint: string;
    touchHint?: string;
    /** The Board UI kit CSS text (the game bakes in the sections it uses). */
    css: string;
    /** Hold Space / the pointer to fire; a Fire key on the touch pad and an Auto fire key. */
    fire?: boolean;
    actions?: ArcadeAction[];
    /** Touch move control (default "stick"; "dpad" for grid games). */
    pad?: "stick" | "dpad";
    /** Keys (or the stick) only: the mouse never steers. */
    keyboard?: boolean;
    /** The card's readouts: label, tone, how the value shows, and whether it hides when the board is
     *  folded. A preset with its own readouts (skirmish) leaves this out. */
    readouts?: [label: string, tone?: "team" | "enemy" | undefined, fmt?: ((v: number) => string) | undefined, fold?: boolean | undefined][];
    meter?: {
        label: string;
    };
    /** Spark colours, by index. */
    colors: string[];
    /** Event type → sound cue. */
    cues: Record<string, Cue>;
    /** Paint targets with their health (default true). */
    paint?: boolean;
    /** The scoreboard and controls: a HUD preset (default `arcadeHud()`, today's card). */
    hud?: ArcadeHud;
    create(ctx: ArcadeContext): ArcadeGame<S>;
}
```

### ArcadeHud (interface, COMPLETE)

A HUD preset: its CSS (after the game's kit CSS) and a mount, once per run.

```ts
export interface ArcadeHud {
    css: string;
    /** Extra controls intents the HUD drives (e.g. aim toggles): intent → key codes. */
    keys?: Record<string, string[]>;
    mount(run: HudRun): HudView;
}
```

### HudRun (interface, COMPLETE)

What the shell gives a HUD when a run starts.

```ts
export interface HudRun {
    /** The kit root (`.bui`), the canvas already in it. */
    ui: HTMLElement;
    def: ArcadeDef<any>;
    engine: Engine;
    input: Controls;
    /** A coarse pointer: build the touch pad. */
    coarse: boolean;
    /** The game, once `create` returned: read it in `write`, never in `mount`. */
    game: ArcadeGame<any>;
    /** Sound (a scoreboard key flips `on`). */
    sfx: {
        on: boolean;
    };
    /** Aborts at Recall: the overlay's life. */
    signal: AbortSignal;
    status(): ArcadeStatus;
    /** Moves the run, for a HUD that owns its flow (`ask`), once its phase changed: pause, resume,
     *  the end (won, lost), a rematch (restart) or Recall (exit). */
    go(to: ArcadeFlow | "restart" | "exit"): void;
}
```

### ArcadeFlow (type, COMPLETE)

A change in a run's flow the HUD is told about: paused, resumed, won or lost.

```ts
export type ArcadeFlow = "pause" | "resume" | "won" | "lost";
```

### HudView (interface, COMPLETE)

A mounted HUD. Keys are `button[data-a]` (sound, pause, exit, restart, gate, auto, fold, or the HUD's own) and `button[data-act]` (an action): the shell runs them, then calls `key`.

```ts
export interface HudView {
    /** The comms toast. */
    msg: HTMLElement;
    /** Every render and once at start: change-only writes, nothing allocated in the steady state. */
    write(): void;
    /** The status changed: the pause key, overlays. */
    sync(): void;
    /** A scoreboard key ran: repaint its face (`auto`: auto fire is on). */
    key(a: string, b: HTMLElement, auto: boolean): void;
    /** At start, in place of starting the engine: a countdown that calls `go` when it is done. */
    begin?(go: () => void): void;
    /** Before the engine goes at the end of a run (its ledger takes back what went through it). */
    hold?(): void;
    /** The run ended and the page is back: show the result. */
    end(won: boolean, notice: string, stats: Record<string, unknown>): void;
    /** The HUD owns the phase (skirmish: `@fzlt/core/match`): the shell's pause, resume and end are asked of
     *  it, and it answers with `HudRun.go` (one owner; the shell keeps the keys and delegates). */
    ask?(to: ArcadeFlow): void;
}
```

### ArcadeHudOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for the default HUD: which header keys and which nav keys, in order.

```ts
export interface ArcadeHudOptions {
    /** Header keys, in order (default all four). */
    header?: ("sound" | "pause" | "fold" | "exit")[];
    /** The nav row after the action keys (default all three; `auto` needs `fire`). */
    nav?: ("next" | "restart" | "auto")[];
}
```

### arcadeHud (function, COMPLETE)

The `arcade` preset, the default: one card with the title, sound / pause / fold / exit keys, the readouts, one meter, the nav row (actions, Next gate, Restart, Auto fire) and the toast; phones get the pad and the card folded at the top. `arcadeHud()` renders exactly what leaving `hud` out renders. Values: `hud(out)` fills the readouts in order, then the meter's change key.

Signature: `arcadeHud(o?: ArcadeHudOptions): ArcadeHud`
- o (optional): `ArcadeHudOptions`
- returns: `ArcadeHud`

```ts
export declare function arcadeHud(o?: ArcadeHudOptions): ArcadeHud;
```

### arcade (function, COMPLETE)

The shell every page arcade game repeats: one engine per run over the host page (its words are terrain, its buttons targets), a Board UI overlay with a canvas and scoreboard, input, sound and the run's flow. `def` is only the game's rules and art.

Signature: `arcade<S>(def: ArcadeDef<S>, options?: ArcadeOptions<S>): ArcadeController<S>`
- def: `ArcadeDef<S>`
- options (optional): `ArcadeOptions<S>`
- returns: `ArcadeController<S>`

```ts
export declare function arcade<S>(def: ArcadeDef<S>, options?: ArcadeOptions<S>): ArcadeController<S>;
```

## @fzlt/core/debug

Status: COMPLETE. Size: 1133 B gzip (budget 1536 B). Page: https://fizlet.com/bricks/debug.html

Import: `import { … } from "@fzlt/core/debug"`

Development-only checks. `guardLayout(engine)` counts every layout read (rects, offset/client/scroll sizes, computed style) made while the engine is in its STEP phase, the contract's "no layout reads in the tick". `touchLog()` puts an on-screen log of pointer and touch events on a real phone. Never ship this in a production build.

### guardLayout (function, COMPLETE)

Count layout reads made during a step; the number shows as `engine.violations`.

Signature: `guardLayout(engine: Engine): () => boolean`
- engine: `Engine`
- returns: `() => boolean`

```ts
export declare function guardLayout(engine: Engine): () => boolean;
```

### TouchLogOptions (interface, COMPLETE)

Options for `touchLog()`.

```ts
export interface TouchLogOptions {
    /** Lines kept on screen, newest last (default 14). */
    lines?: number;
    /** Also log pointermove and touchmove (default false: they flood the log). */
    moves?: boolean;
    /** Where the overlay goes (default document.body). */
    host?: HTMLElement;
}
```

### touchLog (function, COMPLETE)

An on-screen log of the last pointer and touch events on the page (type, pointer type and id or the touch count, x, y, and the element hit; each line starts with ms since start, inside open shadow roots too), for finding why a control doesn't answer on a real phone. A fixed box that never takes a touch itself; listeners are passive and capture on window, so nothing is cancelled or stopped. Nothing is saved or sent. Dev only: wire it to your own query flag. `stop()` removes the box and every listener.

Signature: `touchLog(o?: TouchLogOptions): { … }`
- o (optional): `TouchLogOptions`
- returns: `{ … }`

```ts
export declare function touchLog(o?: TouchLogOptions): {
    /** The overlay (a fixed `<pre>`). */
    el: HTMLPreElement;
    /** The lines on screen, oldest first. */
    lines: readonly string[];
    /** Remove the box and every listener. */
    stop(): void;
};
```
